jobs.title: Aviation Program Analyst
jobs.description:
Aviation Program Analyst

Location: Remote (U.S.-based)

Employment Type: Full-Time

Position Overview

Crown Innovations is seeking a motivated Aviation Program Analyst to support a growing portfolio of state government, federal, and commercial aviation initiatives focused on Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS), Advanced Air Mobility (AAM), airport electrification, and emerging aviation technologies.

This role is ideal for a professional with approximately 3-4 years of experience in aviation, aerospace, transportation, UAS, AAM, airport planning, or a related field. The successful candidate will support program delivery, stakeholder engagement, research and analysis, technical writing, and implementation planning for innovative aviation programs across the United States.

The position provides the opportunity to work directly with state departments of transportation, airports, industry leaders, healthcare systems, utility companies, OEMs and operators of aviation systems, federal agencies, and emerging aviation technology companies helping shape the future of aviation. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting project execution, coordinating stakeholders, developing technical content, and helping clients solve problems through planning work and advisory for the implementation of emerging aviation technologies.

Key Responsibilities

• Program and Project SupportSupport the successful execution of aviation, UAS, AAM, and airport-related projects and programs.Maintain project schedules, task trackers, action-item logs, timelines, and project management tools.Coordinate activities among clients, internal team members, subject matter experts, and external stakeholders.Assist in the preparation of project status reports, progress updates, meeting summaries, and client communications.Track project milestones, deliverables, and project risks to help ensure on-time project delivery.Support program implementation efforts and large-scale aviation initiatives involving government and industry partners.
• Research and AnalysisConduct research on UAS, Advanced Air Mobility, airport electrification, emerging aviation technologies, and related policy developments.Track and analyze state, local, and federal initiatives supporting advanced aviation integration.Monitor programs such as FAA eIPP, BEYOND, SMART, and other emerging aviation initiatives.Support environmental, regulatory, operational, infrastructure, and economic analyses associated with aviation projects.Develop market assessments, implementation strategies, and industry research summaries.
• Stakeholder EngagementCoordinate outreach efforts with airports, government agencies, industry organizations, private companies, and community stakeholders.Develop interview guides, surveys, questionnaires, and stakeholder engagement materials.Conduct virtual and in-person interviews with organizations evaluating UAS and AAM applications, including healthcare, utilities, infrastructure, logistics, emergency response, and construction sectors.Document findings and prepare recommendations, summaries, and implementation considerations.
• Technical Writing and CommunicationsDraft technical reports, white papers, research papers, case studies, presentations, and briefing materials.Support the development of thought leadership content related to advanced aviation technologies and implementation strategies.Prepare client-ready deliverables and executive-level communications.Assist with proposal development, grant applications, and business growth initiatives.
• Industry and Market IntelligenceTrack airports, states, utilities, and industry organizations implementing UAS, AAM, and electrification initiatives.Monitor developments in FAA policy, industry trends, infrastructure investments, and technology adoption.Maintain awareness of key stakeholders, technology providers, operators, and emerging market opportunities across the advanced aviation ecosystem.Support development of GIS-based analyses, mapping products, dashboards, and visualization tools to communicate aviation infrastructure, UAS, AAM, and airport planning information to clients and stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Aviation, Aerospace, Transportation Planning, or a related field.
• Approximately 3-5 years of professional experience supporting aviation, aerospace, transportation, airport planning, UAS, AAM, or related consulting and infrastructure projects.
• Working knowledge of Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS), Advanced Air Mobility (AAM), airport operations, aviation planning, or emerging aviation technologies.
• Experience supporting project delivery, stakeholder coordination, client engagement, or consulting projects involving multiple organizations and technical subject matter experts.
• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and Teams.
• Ability to synthesize technical, regulatory, operational, and market information into actionable recommendations for clients and stakeholders.
• Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to conduct interviews, facilitate discussions, and engage with industry, government, and airport stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

• FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certification or the ability to obtain certification within six months of hire.
• Experience with airport planning, airport development, Airport Layout Plans (ALPs), aviation infrastructure, or FAA-related projects.
• Experience supporting AAM, UAS integration, drone operations, remote sensing, photogrammetry, or related technology initiatives.
• Knowledge of GIS analysis, geospatial data management, web-based mapping applications, or spatial analysis tools.
• Experience conducting stakeholder outreach, workshops, interviews, surveys, or public engagement activities.
• Familiarity with federal, state, or local government programs related to aviation, transportation, infrastructure, or emerging technologies.
• Experience with data visualization, business intelligence, and analytical tools.
• Participation in aviation industry organizations such as AUVSI, AAAE, NASAO, NBAA, AOPA, or similar professional associations.

Benefits

Crown offers a competitive benefits package including:

• Generous PTO

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans

• Health Savings Account (HSA) & Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

• 401(k) with company match

• Life insurance

• Tuition reimbursement

About Crown Innovations

Crown Innovations is a recognized leader in research, development, and engineering, shaping the future of air transportation through concept development, system design, advanced integration, and emerging technologies. Our expertise spans air traffic management, survey administration, lifecycle data management for informed decision-making, infrastructure sustainment and modernization, and National Airspace System (NAS) integration.

For more than three decades, Crown has partnered with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), NASA, the Energy Information Administration (EIA), state and local governments, and commercial organizations to deliver innovative engineering, strategic planning, software development, data analytics, modeling and simulation, regulatory compliance, and advanced information solutions that enhance national infrastructure, operational performance, and mission success.

As a prime contractor supporting several high-impact federal programs, Crown is committed to delivering innovative, reliable, and customer-focused solutions while fostering a culture of collaboration, integrity, continuous improvement, and technical excellence.

Crown has consistently been recognized as one of the best places to work in the Washington, DC metropolitan area by investing in exceptional people who are passionate about supporting our customers' missions and driving meaningful innovation.

Compliance & Equal Opportunity

Persons unable to complete an online application should contact Crown HR for assistance at (703) 650-0663 ext. 3068.

As a government contractor, certain positions may require U.S. citizenship.

Crown is a VEVRAA Federal Contractor.

EOE: Disability/Veterans

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Tissue Donation Coordinator (Hybrid Opportunity)
jobs.description:
Looking for meaningful work, great benefits, and a place to belong? As a Tissue Donation Coordinator, the work you do will help guide donor families through the tissue donation process that can lead to impacting countless individuals.

Tissue donations are pivotal in helping children who require heart valve transplants lead full and healthy lives, breast cancer survivors in need of mastectomy surgeries feel whole again, restoring sight to those who suffer from corneal blindness, and so many others.

What You’ll Do:

• Handle incoming donor referral calls from hospital staff and clinical partners to obtain and evaluate medical information regarding potential tissue donor suitability
• Work empathetically and compassionately with potential donor families to advocate for donation, conduct history questionnaires, and obtain informed consent to donation
• Coordinate logistics of tissue recoveries with both internal and external partners and stakeholders
• Follow best practices and provide exemplary customer service while communicating with teammates, partners, and stakeholders including Hospital staff, Clinical partners, Funeral Homes, Medical Examiners, District Attorneys, and others.

What You’ll Work:

• Three 12-hour shifts per week
• One 12-hour on-call shift every 2 weeks
• A variety of Day, Mid, and Night shifts
• Shifts you select in our collaborative self-scheduling model
• Shifts in person and remote in our fully hybrid staffing model

Ability to work both remotely from a home office setting and onsite in Waltham, MA - remote opportunities are available once you have completed the orientation process (after several months) and you are completely independent.

• During the orientation period all shifts will be on site in Waltham, MA.
• Shifts that support our 24-hour, 365-day a year mission including weekends and holidays
• Now interviewing for our November and December 2026 New Hire Orientation start dates

What You’ll Be a Part Of:

You will be part of a team that supports the NEDS mission, to Save and Heal Lives, through the gift of Organ and Tissue Donation.  As an NEDS employee, our benefits include:

• Generous paid time-off program
• Health, Dental, Vision, and Mental Health insurance coverage
• 2x Annual Salary Life Insurance
• Fertility Benefits
• Flex Spending Account Options
• 403(b) Retirement Plan with Organizational Contributions
• Tuition Reimbursement
• Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
• Pet Insurance
• Working Advantage discounts Program.
• Personal career and skill development opportunities

You can also participate in Corporate sponsored events  like the annual Blue & Green Walk, Community Volunteering opportunities, Organization-wide team-building outings, and more!

What You’ll Bring:

• Bachelor’s degree and one year of relevant experience; or, strong consideration will be given to candidates who have an Associate’s degree, certification or license and 3+ years of relevant experience in medical field, health sciences, mental health or counseling with expertise in crisis intervention and/or grief counseling
• Working knowledge of medical terminology
• Excellent telephone communication skills
• Strong computer skills including Microsoft Office suite, clinical databases, and Electronic Medical Records
• Excellent organizational skills and a strong attention to detail
• Must be flexible and proactive, and have a positive attitude
• Ability to work both remotely from a home office setting and onsite in Waltham, MA - remote opportunities are available once you have completed the orientation process and you are completely independent. During the orientation period all shifts will be on site in Waltham, MA.

HIRING ALERT: NEDS continues to take precautions to protect our community, staff and partners from COVID-19. In order to be employed at NEDS, you must be vaccinated and boosted for COVID-19.

When you join New England Donor Services you can expect competitive salaries and a great benefit package. Benefits include a generous paid time off program, BCBS Health and Dental Insurance, Healthcare Reimbursement Account, 2x Annual Salary Life Insurance, Pet Insurance, Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Coverage, 403(b) Retirement Contribution, Tuition Reimbursement, Employee Assistance Program and Discounts through Working Advantage.

New England Donor Services is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes candidates from all backgrounds to apply to meet the needs of the communities we serve.

jobs.title: Loss Prevention Inventory Specialist (East Location)
jobs.description:
North 40 Outfitters in Great Falls, MT, East Location, is looking to hire a Full-Time Loss Prevention Inventory Specialist to join our team.  We believe that each team member plays a vital role in the success of our company.  We are looking for authentic and enthusiastic people who love our lifestyle and believe in service before self.  As a Loss Prevention Inventory Specialist at North 40, you play a key role in the overall customer experience by safeguarding company assets with auditing processes and procedures and maintaining the accuracy of the store’s inventory.  The ideal candidate has strong communication skills, open availability and dependable.  Proficiency in Microsoft Suite: Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

This full-time position requires the ability to work all scheduled shifts between the business hours of Mon-Sat 7 am to 7 pm, and Sunday 9 am to 5 pm. This shift can include working weekends and certain holidays and will require flexibility in scheduling based on business needs.

• Loss PreventionFunction as the stores Loss Prevention Coordinator to proactively detect and prevent losses. Analyze shrink/loss data to identify and track problem areas and trends. Review and monitor process controls and audits and identify problem areas or procedural deficiencies.In partnership with store management, teach, train and coach associates in loss prevention protocols and techniques as well as use of equipment and technologies.Oversee EAS system operation and coordinate on maintenance and compliance.Advise Store Managers and Loss Prevention on policy and procedure violations.Assist store management team with the implementation and adherence of Standard Operating Procedures (SOP’s) and all company policies and procedures. Report all issues to Loss Prevention.Watch for and recognize potential theft, and take appropriate steps to prevent, report, or handle these situations.Recognize safety and security risks and remedy the situation and alert proper personnel.Monitor and audit cash handling processes and procedures. Conduct random counts of safe and tills.Assist store management with the stores key control, authorized access areas, alarm logs, and physical security.
• Perform counts and verify inventory: Moving Targets and Cycle CountsObtain moving targets list from Loss Prevention on a weekly basis.Physically check accuracy of counts on each item on the moving target list.Research as needed and note reason for variances; track and file all major discrepancies for audit by Loss Prevention.Obtain department count lists from Loss Prevention monthly.Break down the list by department; assign the department list to the lead and assist in counting inventory as able.Research as needed on large discrepancies.Correct PIP to reflect actual product availability on all counts.Obtain negative count lists daily when possible, minimum of twice per week; reconcile discrepancies and PIP as needed to reflect actual quantity availability.
• Active Inventory Management (AIM)Ensure inventory counts are adjusted properly using PIP process.Understand all PIP types.Utilize appropriate PIP according to each individual situation for optimal tracking.PIP inventory accordingly to reflect actual product availabilityVerify correct price and SKU on signage and labels as product is counted.Notify department leads with any tagging discrepancies that need to be addressed.Verify zero counts on empty bins and pegs near items that are counted.
• Other Duties as assigned including:Provide position specific Loss Prevention training to new hires.Provide ongoing training to store teams based on discovered trends and observed practices regarding Loss Prevention and inventory handling processes and procedures.Assist in educating and maintaining store wide standards in safety and security.Assist customers while conducting all assigned duties.

BENEFITS & COMPENSATION

We offer a competitive wage, a rewarding work environment, and generous benefits and perks such as paid holidays, a 401(k) option, Health Savings Accounts (HSAs), medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, and a phenomenal employee discount on all products North 40 sells.

North 40 Outfitters is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
Fortune Brands is hiring a Product Manager to lead the Valve and Cartridge product line within our Moen water brand.

Every Moen faucet, shower, and bath product depends on a valve or cartridge to assembly effortlessly, seal perfectly, and provide the ideal tactile feel over years of use. This core technology serves as the foundation for our water control systems. As Product Manager, you will play a critical role in generating the growth and success of Valves and Cartridges and, consequently, Moen water products as a whole.

You will shape product strategies by aligning product offerings, channels, and pricing in ways that meet both customer and business needs. You propose strategic direction, drive the roadmap, and watch your decisions show up on shelves and in people’s homes.

This role calls for curiosity, empathy, and thoughtful analysis to understand market trends and customer experiences. You will work closely with cross-functional partners to develop meaningful strategies, communicate shared goals, and contribute to outcomes that strengthen market presence over time. This entails a strong business acumen with a technical aptitude to become a SME of the inner workings of Valves and Cartridges and the products they interface with.

The ideal candidate combines strong product management capabilities with a deep understanding of fluid-control technologies and consumer-facing products. They can translate customer insights, competitive analysis, and technical requirements into a compelling product strategy, while partnering with engineering teams to deliver innovative, reliable, and market-leading plumbing or fluid-control solutions.

POSITION LOCATION: This is a hybrid position based in our world-class Deerfield, IL campus, with flexibility to work from home on Mondays and Fridays.

What you will be doing:

• Development of strategic product plans by aligning performance, pricing, and supply chain with long-term business goals to support sustainable revenue and market growth.
• Partner with cross-functional teams to guide new product development and innovation initiatives through the full stage-gate process.
• Build collaborative relationships with external customers by sharing insights and helping identify opportunities for category growth.
• Work closely with Revenue Growth Management, Sales, Analytics, and Finance teams to better understand channel dynamics and evaluate pricing strategies.
• Contribute to go-to-market approaches by sharing perspectives and helping guide product and business decisions.
• Collaborate with Operations, including Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Quality, to support product launches and monitor ongoing product performance.
• Advocate for the voice of the customer by developing a deep understanding of customer needs, preferences, and market trends.
• Communicate product strategies and priorities clearly and thoughtfully to a variety of stakeholders.
• Support sales teams through training, participation in industry events, and ongoing engagement with partners and associations.
• Partner with Brand, Channel Marketing, Digital, and Commercialization teams to co-create marketing materials and promotional strategies.
• Review product-related communications to ensure clarity, consistency, and accuracy.
• Provide training and guidance to internal teams and external partners on product offerings and updates.
• Maintain regular, supportive communication with field sales teams, including occasional travel (approximately 15%).
• Contribute to additional projects and responsibilities as needed.

• Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Engineering, or related field.
• 3-5+ years of proven experience in product management, product development, or engineering leadership for high-volume manufactured products. (We will strongly consider engineering leaders ready to move into product management.)
• Experience managing products within the plumbing, kitchen and bath, or water delivery product categories OR other valve, cartridge, and fluid control technologies, including thermostatic and pressure-balancing mechanisms.
• Understanding of sealing technologies, including elastomeric and ceramic components, as well as flow performance, cavitation, acoustic/noise reduction, and durability requirements.
• Experience with high-volume manufactured products in industries such as plumbing, appliance, HVAC/R, water heating, beverage dispensing, irrigation, water treatment, pool and spa, or automotive fluid control systems.
• Ability to translate customer needs, competitive analysis, and engineering requirements into product strategy, roadmap priorities, and successful product launches through a stage-gate or equivalent process.
• Experience partnering closely with market-facing roles (such as Sales) and partnering with technical roles (engineering) to bring a quality product portfolio to market
• Strong analytical and communication skills to support collaborative decision-making.
• Technical aptitude and the ability to understand the engineering, functionality, and internal mechanics imperative to the product while having the business acumen (financials) to build strong business cases, derive market insights and product trends to ensure portfolio success.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word).
• Willingness and ability to travel up to 15%.

Preferred Qualifications:

• MBA or advanced degree in Marketing, Business, or a related field.
• Ideal candidates will have experience in plumbing developing high-volume consumer, commercial, or automotive products that incorporate fluid control systems, including thermostatic and pressure-compensating valves, cartridges, elastomeric and ceramic sealing technologies, flow regulation, noise and cavitation management, and durability/lifecycle performance.
• Background in building products, home improvement, or durable goods.Experience with both B2C and B2B product environments.
• Familiarity with connected product technologies or smart home categories.

jobs.title: Maintenance Supervisor
jobs.description:
Key Responsibilities

Leadership and Supervision:

Directly supervise Maintenance personnel and provide day‑to‑day leadership for the Maintenance department.

Carry out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies, procedures, and applicable local, state, and federal regulations.

Recruit, interview, hire, onboard, train, evaluate, and develop employees.

Plan, assign, and direct work; monitor performance; address employee concerns; and administer corrective action as necessary.

Operational Excellence:

Plan, direct, and delegate Maintenance activities to ensure uninterrupted production, adherence to quality standards, and control of manufacturing costs.

Develop and manage preventive and predictive maintenance programs using current technologies, data analysis, and CMMS software.

Ensure accurate maintenance records, including asset repair history and preventive maintenance schedules.

Communicate equipment status, maintenance priorities, and project progress with supervisors, managers, and engineering teams.

Project and Cost Management:

Develop and execute aggressive yet achievable project schedules and realistic cost estimates in support of business requirements.

Participate in and support initiatives related to cost reduction, process improvement, and operational efficiency.

Recommend changes to working conditions, workflows, and equipment utilization to improve productivity and effectiveness.

Compliance and Safety:

Ensure compliance with OSHA, ISO, company standards, and all applicable safety programs and procedures.

Enforce compliance with applicable bargaining unit agreements within assigned areas of responsibility.

Promote a culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement throughout the Maintenance team.

Cross-Functional Support:

Support Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Planning teams with accurate data for production scheduling, capacity planning, and material availability.

Collaborate with EHS, HR, Engineering, Quality & Continuous Improvement teams to ensure data supports regulatory and compliance requirements.

Identify opportunities to improve data workflows, reduce manual effort, and increase automation.

Participate in lean, digital manufacturing, and operational excellence initiatives.

Additional Responsibilities:

Coordinate and participate in administrative and technical programs, including training initiatives and communication efforts.

Perform other duties as assigned to support departmental and organizational objectives.

Core Qualifications and Requirements

• Education: High school diploma/GED is standard, with vocational training, technical certificates, or an associate/bachelor’s degree in facility management or industrial technology highly valued.
• Experience: Requires 5+ years of general Maintenance experience with at least 2 years in a supervisory or leadership position preferred.
• Technical Skills: Deep knowledge of building systems, including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, carpentry, and building automation systems.
• Safety & Compliance: Thorough understanding of OSHA & NFPA regulations, safety protocols, and risk management.

Required Skills and Abilities

• Leadership: Proven ability to manage a team, schedule staff, train employees, and manage vendors.
• Problem-Solving: Strong diagnostic skills for diagnosing and repairing equipment.
• Administrative & Computer Skills: Proficiency in Computerized Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS) and MS Office, plus experience with budgeting.
• Physical Stamina: Ability to perform tasks involving lifting, climbing, and working in varied environmental conditions.

Common Industry-Specific Experience

• Industrial/Manufacturing: Focus on production machinery, automation, robotics, and heavy equipment maintenance.
• Institutional/Facilities: Focus on equipment reliability, HVAC, complex building systems, and vendor management.

Work Environment

• Manufacturing and office environment.

• Collaboration with production floor personnel.

• Support during process implementation and production launches.

Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability / veterans

jobs.title: Instrumentation Controls & Power Generation Manager
jobs.description:
Overall Purpose and Objective of Position

This position will be a technical manager and leader of the resources at LDC Grand Junction, for overseeing all instrumentation and control activities at the site including real time health of said systems in our DCS SCADA system. This position will be responsible for overseeing multiple operational technologies and electrical power systems. This includes directing LDC and 3rd party I&E technicians as needed, to support the efficient installation, testing, maintenance, and troubleshooting of all instrumentation, measurement, control, power generation, and CSD devices for power generation both boiler steam and turbine electrical. This manager will also interface directly with the utility on incoming and outgoing power systems. This manager will be focused on optimizing the performance and reliability of all plant systems related to power generation, combustion, or instrumentation, driving preventative maintenance and repair initiatives, while maintaining world class safety standards and expectations. In addition, this manager will work closely with peers and other management to support operational objectives and foster enhanced team coordination. To be successful this individual should not only be highly technically adept, but also innovative, with a keen eye for detail and problem solving.

Primary Responsibilities/Essential Functions

• Lead and manage the Instrumentation and Controls (I&C) team, including I&C technicians both internal and external, and support staff.
• Develop and implement training programs to enhance the technical skills and expertise of team members in control systems and instrumentation.
• Ability to work on-site in a power plant environment, perform hands-on tasks in the field solely or with the Solar team ensuring tasks are carried out efficiently and safely.
• Plan, prioritize, and oversee the maintenance of process automation systems to optimize steam and electrical power production, ensuring the reliable operation of boilers and environmental systems.
• Foster a safe work environment by promoting adherence to safety protocols and addressing unsafe practices or conditions.
• Cultivate strong communication and relationships across all teams
• Oversee maintenance activities related to electrical systems, process control, and automation systems, including installation, preventative maintenance, troubleshooting, testing, and calibration, ensuring thorough documentation and peak system performance and reliability.
• Collaborate with Area Managers on routine electrical and mechanical engineering tasks as well as special projects.
• Supervise troubleshooting and maintenance of distributed control systems (DCS) and programmable logic controllers (PLC), including Allen Bradley, Schnieder and Solar systems and the ability to troubleshoot and evaluate plant performance issues using eDNA and historians.
• Oversee the reception, installation, and configuration of all process related servers, networks, and equipment
• Monitor all data communication platforms
• Organize and maintain all license support documents
• Prepare documentation diagrams, process control narratives, instrumentation lists, I/O lists, as any part of project design or maintenance activities
• Provide oversight and support for Solar workstation computer and related equipment maintenance.
• Ensure that all responsibilities are executed in accordance with LDC Management’s established expectations.
• Contribute to the annual budgeting process for maintenance-related parts and materials.
• Schedule and manage preventive maintenance (PM) calibration of various field instrumentation.
• Identify and report necessary spare parts for efficient plant operation and improvement initiatives to Area Managers and direct managers
• Offer technical guidance and mentorship to the I&E team, ensuring continuous development and expertise.
• Uphold plant policies and procedures, ensuring all tasks are performed safely and in compliance with environmental regulations.
• Participate in Process Safety, 3D Model and Design Reviews such as:PRA/PHA/HAZOPControl narrativesCause and Effect documentsElectrical Area Classification
• Take on additional responsibilities as required and mutually agreed upon with Primary Energy Management.

Additional Responsibilities

• Serve as one of the primary interfaces for engineering on instrumentation, electrical generation or boiler issues with operations.
• Problem solving and troubleshooting as requested by operations or maintenance when requested.
• Works with the Safety, Health, and Environmental (SHE) staff to assure regulatory certifications and compliance on capital and process improvements, normal operating practices regarding SHE
• Reviews plant operations for potential process / procedural improvements for higher throughput and / or cost savings.
• Maintains good working knowledge of SHE policies, rules and procedures applicable to area of responsibility and ensures all applicable requirements are adhered to.
• Ensure employees are provided required training for area assigned, and jobs and tasks prior to assigning work.
• Ensures unsafe working conditions are remedied as soon as practicable.
• Follows construction completion criteria and construction requirements with the maintenance manager.
• Assists in the project start-up with local management.
• Additional projects and duties as assigned.

Education/Professional Certifications/Licenses

The following is the basic qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering; Chemical, Electrical or automation/Instrumentation engineering
• Professional Engineer (P.Eng) is preferred.
• Project Management Professional (PMP) is desired.

Experience

jobs.title: Onboarding Operations Coordinator
jobs.description:
The Onboarding Operations Coordinator is responsible for coordinating and managing the end-to-end process of onboarding employees into customer systems. This position serves as the primary point of contact between IBOS Operations, employees, internal support teams, and the customer for account setup, system access, customer-provided equipment, and onboarding-related issues.

The coordinator ensures that new employees receive the system access and customer-provided equipment required to perform their assigned responsibilities. The role monitors onboarding and access requests through completion, resolves access issues, maintains accurate records, escalates unresolved concerns, and provides timely updates to stakeholders.

The position is also responsible for managing and tracking customer-provided equipment, including phones and laptops. This includes maintaining accurate assignment records, completing routine physical inventory counts, monitoring device activity through smart locker reports, investigating discrepancies, and reporting lost, missing, or damaged equipment.

YOUR TASKS

• Customer-Provided Equipment and Smart Locker Management
• Manage and track customer-provided equipment, including phones, laptops, accessories, and other assigned devices.
• Maintain accurate records showing the location, status, condition, and assigned employee for each device.
• Coordinate the assignment, return, reassignment, and storage of customer-provided equipment.
• Ensure employees properly sign devices in and out using the designated smart locker system.
• Manage smart locker access and device-assignment records.
• Review smart locker reports regularly to monitor device checkouts, returns, assignments, and usage activity.
• Investigate devices that are overdue, not returned, assigned incorrectly, or not accounted for in the smart locker reports.
• Follow up with employees and operational leaders regarding missing devices, incomplete returns, or equipment discrepancies.
• Perform regular physical inventory counts and reconcile results against equipment trackers and smart locker reports.
• Document and investigate differences between the physical inventory, equipment-assignment records, and smart locker activity.
• Inspect returned equipment and document its condition.
• Report lost, missing, damaged, or unaccounted-for equipment to the appropriate customer and internal stakeholders.
• Maintain documentation for equipment damage, loss, return, and replacement.
• Coordinate the return or replacement of damaged equipment according to established customer requirements.
• Ensure unused and returned equipment is stored securely and remains properly accounted for.
• Support periodic equipment audits and provide accurate inventory and accountability records when requested.
• Identify recurring equipment-control issues and recommend improvements to the assignment, return, storage, and tracking processes.
• Develop and maintain clear work instructions for equipment checkout, return, smart locker use, physical inventory counts, and damage reporting.

Equipment Accountability Measures

The coordinator’s equipment-management responsibilities may be measured through:

• Accuracy of customer equipment inventory records
• Percentage of customer devices assigned to an identifiable employee or secure storage location
• Completion of required physical inventory counts
• Timely reconciliation of inventory discrepancies
• Accuracy of smart locker assignment and activity records
• Timeliness of device returns during employee offboarding or role changes
• Number and age of unresolved missing-equipment cases
• Timely reporting of lost or damaged equipment
• Compliance with device checkout, return, storage, and accountability requirements

• High school diploma or equivalent required.
• 1-3 years of experience in operations, administration, onboarding, customer service, inventory management, or a related field.
• Strong organizational and time-management skills.

• Strong attention to detail and accuracy.

• Experience maintaining records, trackers, or databases preferred.
• Experience with inventory management, asset tracking, or equipment accountability preferred.
• Ability to conduct physical inventory counts and reconcile discrepancies.
• Experience supporting employee onboarding or system access processes preferred.
• Ability to lift and move equipment weighing up to 25 pounds as needed.

jobs.title: Managing Director of High Schools (26-27)
jobs.description:
The Managing Director of High Schools (MDHS) leads the improvement of KIPP Team & Family’s existing high schools and builds the long-term design for what a KIPP TEAM & Family (KTAF) high school should be. The role starts with the schools we have — driving four-year college matriculation, SAT and GPA outcomes, and student and staff culture — and grows into the org-wide strategy work that determines what our high schools become.

The MDHS reports to the CAO and is also a member of the Newark regional leadership team, working in close partnership with the Managing Director of Schools in Newark. Over time, the person in this role may also join the Camden, Paterson, and Miami regional leadership teams to support high school-specific outcomes and workstreams.

Scope of Responsibility

• Newark: Direct management of high school School Leaders.
• Camden, Miami, Paterson: Dotted-line management of the high school Principal Manager in each region; accountable for partnering with those managers to produce strong high school outcomes. Our Paterson high school will be founded in the near future, and the person in this role will help to inform and shape the school design.
• Org-wide: Owns the KTAF high school strategic plan and leads a cross-functional team of high school specialists.

Priorities

Priority 1: Improve our current high schools: This is the first job and the one that matters most in year one. Raise four-year college matriculation by moving our topline SAT and GPA goals, and improve student and staff culture.

• Serve as the Principal Manager for Newark high school School Leaders — set goals, coach, observe, and hold the bar.
• Set annual academic and culture goals with School Leaders, aligned to org-wide strategy and approved by the CAO/CEO.
• Drive SAT and GPA topline goals and four-year college matriculation across the high school band.
• Improve student culture and staff culture, measured by survey results, attrition, attendance, and walkthroughs.
• Monitor school health indicators and intervene where schools are off track.

Priority 2: Lead and rally the high school specialists: Build one high-performing team out of the people whose work touches high schools across Teaching & Learning, Special Education, Student Experience, and KIPP Forward.

• Direct management: high school Teaching & Learning and Special Education.
• Dotted-line management: high school Student Experience and KIPP Forward.
• Set a shared vision, agenda, goals, and standards across this group so high schools get coherent support rather than four separate workstreams.
• Collaborate with the Director of Special Education on strategy and programming for students with disabilities.
• Partner with KIPP Forward on college match strategy and post-secondary outcomes.

Priority 3: Coach and develop each region’s high school principal manager: Camden and Miami high schools improve through the MD of High School’s influence and partnership, not direct management.

• Hold a standing, structured partnership with each region’s high school Principal Manager through a dotted-line reporting relationship.
• Agree on outcome targets with each Principal Manager and their regional leader; review progress on a set cadence.
• Build a cohesive high school culture across the band — shared norms, common data protocols, and real best-practice sharing between cities.
• Present high school perspective and best practices in regional leadership team spaces when appropriate.

Priority 4: Build the KTAF high school strategic plan: Research, design, build, and implement a plan that answers the question “what makes a KIPP Team & Family high school?” in each of our regions.

• Assess the changing high school and post-secondary landscape in Newark, Camden, and Miami — each city is different, and the plan should say how.
• Address the need for alternative and therapeutic programming for students our current model does not serve well.
• Maintain an in-depth knowledge of research-based, trends, and innovation in the high school space.
• Expand CTE and industry certification options in response to what our communities are asking for, while holding our identity as college-preparatory schools.
• Evaluate innovative models, dual enrollment, and magnet designs.
• Define what is standardized across KTAF high schools and what is decided regionally.
• Own 8th-to-9th grade transition outcomes and ensure that our top-performing middle school students seek to enroll in our high schools.

jobs.title: Total Rewards Analyst
jobs.description:
The Compensation & Benefits Analyst supports the administration and ongoing maintenance of the Company’s U.S. compensation and benefits programs. This role provides analytical support, data reporting, and day-to-day operational assistance across compensation and employee benefits activities. The position helps ensure programs are competitive, compliant, and delivered accurately to employees.

YOUR TASKS

• Administer and maintain salary structures, pay evaluations, and pay grades, ensuring data accuracy and alignment with internal processes.
• Manage annual compensation processes including merit increases, bonus administration, and salary planning cycles (data preparation, validation, reporting, and tracking).
• Conduct market pricing and benchmarking using compensation surveys and available market data; summarize findings for review.
• Support pay equity analyses by gathering data, preparing reports, and assisting with documentation.
• Prepare standard compensation reports and dashboards to support internal decision-making.

• Support day-to-day U.S. benefits administration, including medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, life insurance, FSAs, voluntary benefits, leaves of absence, disability, and retirement plans.
• Assist with annual benefits renewals and lead open enrollment activities, including vendor coordination, data support, employee communications, and enrollment tracking.

• Assist with leave of absence and disability administration by coordinating documentation and supporting employee inquiries in alignment with policy and regulatory requirements.
• Help maintain benefits documentation, job aids, and employee-facing communications.
• Support compliance activities for compensation and benefits programs (e.g., ERISA, ACA, COBRA, FMLA, pay transparency) through data gathering, documentation, and reporting support.
• Assist with audits and internal reviews by compiling requested data, tracking responses, and maintaining records.
• Perform routine data quality checks across compensation and benefits records; report discrepancies and support remediation.
• Contribute to process improvements by documenting workflows, identifying recurring issues, and suggesting practical enhancements.
• Partner with Payroll, HRIS, HR Business Partners, Finance, and external vendors to support accurate administration and timely issue resolution.
• Communicate program information clearly and professionally to employees and internal partners.

• Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, or a related field preferred.
• Progress toward relevant certification (e.g., CCP/CBP/CEBS) preferred.
• 3+ years of experience in compensation, benefits, HR operations, or HR analytics (total rewards exposure preferred).
• Experience working with HRIS systems and handling HR data with confidentiality.

jobs.title: Department Manager - St. Clair Square
jobs.description:
About the Role

As a Department Manager, you’ll be the leader supporting and encouraging your whole team. By bringing everyone together, you’ll be able to create an inclusive culture that promotes collaboration and an entrepreneurial spirit, helping you, your team, and H&M succeed. Ensuring an excellent operational & visual experience for your store, customers & colleagues. You’ll be aware of your store’s strengths, opportunities, and competitors. Analyze and follow up on sales, and create plans to optimize results and profits.

A Day in the Life

Working at H&M means no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will include the following responsibilities*

Customer Sales & Profit

• You are responsible for the total OMNI customer experience in your store, ensuring visual and commercial curation according to global guidelines
• Representing yourself and the H&M brand positively during customer interactions
• Be aware of and take responsibility of your department's strengths and identifying commercial opportunities and acting on them
• Establish & analyze sales and budget goals, creating plans to optimize results
• Ensure customer service is provided in all areas of the store and that your team has the ability to work towards actively promoting and selling products to customers
• Following up that your team is actively promoting our Customer Loyalty App (Hello Member) & in-store sustainability initiatives
• Manage your department in a cost-efficient way
• Ensure correct routines in fitting room and checkout, including transaction, returns and exchanges
• Ensure all admin routines for both people and operations are handled in a correct way

Fashion & Trend Awareness

• Keep up-to-date with fashion scene, trends, tendencies, styles, brands, products, competitors and relevant influencers, etc
• Ensure your team provides product and fashion knowledge as well as other relevant information during customer interactions

Team & Development

• Responsible for recruitment, onboarding, performance management, upskilling & developing your team in-store
• Complete performance evaluations and succession planning to support business & team needs
• Retain and share your knowledge and skills with your team
• Collaboration, planning & teamwork with in-store Visual Merchandiser team
• Give & receive feedback with your colleagues to learn, develop & support each other
• Responsible for the teams planning & scheduling
• Regular communication to store colleagues to inform, motivate and inspire – daily, weekly meetings, etc
• Ensure all procedures, routines, and legal requirements in all areas of the store are followed
• Participate in relevant available Onboarding & introduction processes, trainings and courses relevant for your role & future development

Retail Operations/ Visual & Commercial Execution

• Secure a clean and tidy sales floor and back of house including stockroom areas
• Ensure high fashion quality, visual and commercial product presentation, with good garment care
• Secure good stock levels and provide input on allocation to Area team
• Ensure the full garment cycle – from delivery to garment presentation – and fitting room routines are according to our standards and routines set internally, utilizing all tools and technology provided
• Upkeep & follow best practice for any in-store OMNI Services & in-store tech services/tools, etc (Instore Care App, Click & Collect, Smart Store etc)
• Secure a strong balance and the maintenance of price signs in-store and throughout the sales floor/store following guidelines according to global and local strategies & sales market/regional requirements to ensure a strong and consistent price perception throughout store
• Updating & upkeep of BOH Areas for all colleagues (key information, health & safety, tidiness etc)
• Responsible for opening & closing of store daily

Who You Are

• To be a successful and effective Department Manager, you’ll be a strong leader who enjoys taking responsibility for others.
• You must be ambitious, an effective communicator, supportive, an analytical solution finder, capable of working with numbers and managing statistics.
• You are achievement-oriented, motivated by performance and competition to be truly customer centric.

Why You’ll Love Working at H&M

• We value diverse backgrounds, including but not limited to race, ethnicity, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, and disability
• We pride ourselves on being a values-driven organization, guided by our 7 unique values that have been part of our success story for over 75 years
• You’ll have access to our Colleague Resource Groups (CRGs) to find community and networking opportunities among colleagues
• We are an inclusive company where you’re encouraged to be yourself at work
• You will have access to a large global talent community, where career growth and aspirations have no limits
• We believe in supporting your overall wellbeing and offer comprehensive benefits inclusive of health insurance, wellness and family support programs, company match retirement plan, paid leave programs, and paid time off, including a community day to serve your local community
• You’ll be able to express your personal style with our employee discount at H&M, & Other Stories, and COS

Compensation: expected base salary range is $23.56-$27.09 hourly**

EEOC Code: SLS

Pay Status: Non-Exempt, Hourly

*This job posting highlights the most critical responsibilities and requirements of the job and is not all-inclusive. There may be additional duties, and responsibilities assigned for this job at the company’s discretion.

jobs.title: Global Quality Assurance Leader (Contact Center)
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Immediate Multilingual Learners Teacher (High Schoo)
jobs.description:
POSITION OVERVIEW

We are seeking a passionate and skilled Multilingual Teacher of Record (MLTOR) to support multilingual learners in developing their English language proficiency while maintaining academic excellence. The ideal candidate will be committed to ensuring that all students, regardless of their language background, have access to high-quality instruction that meets their linguistic and academic needs. KIPP Indy’s MLTOR is responsible for providing specialized instruction, managing Individual Learning Plans (ILPs) services, and collaborating with general education teachers to support multilingual learners.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Demonstrate a strong understanding of student learning and effective teaching strategies for Emergent Bilingual Students
• Design and deliver effective, differentiated instruction to multilingual learners that aligns with state standards and is tailored to their English language proficiency levels.
• Develop and implement individualized ILP plans, ensuring compliance with state and federal regulations.
• Regularly assess and monitor student progress in both English language acquisition and academic content, using data to inform instruction.
• Provide appropriate scaffolding, accommodations, and modifications to ensure access to grade-level curriculum for multilingual learners.
• Collaborate with classroom teachers to integrate language development into content instruction, adapting lessons to meet the diverse needs of multilingual learners.
• Collaborate with general education teachers, support staff, and families to create an inclusive learning environment that supports linguistic and cultural diversity.
• Advocate for the academic and social-emotional needs of multilingual learners within the school community.
• Build strong relationships with students and their families, maintaining ongoing communication to support language development and academic success.
• Stay current with best practices in language acquisition and culturally responsive teaching.
• Participate in case conferences and maintain accurate records, ensuring that all documentation related to multilingual learners complies with state and federal requirements.
• Use formative assessment data to adjust instruction, ensuring that all multilingual learners are progressing toward proficiency.
• Actively work with academic coaches to continuously improve instructional practices, embrace feedback, and implement strategies for professional growth.
• Take ownership of your professional development by seeking out learning opportunities and reflecting on your teaching practices.

EXPECTATIONS

• Arrive at school by 8:10 a.m.
• Participate in school-wide and individual professional development, including two weeks during the summer, weekly school-wide meetings, and ongoing core values trainings
• Provide time in the evening, by phone, for questions and concerns that students and/or families may have regarding education-related issues that could not be handled during the school day
• Attend and participate in all staff meetings
• Maintain open and effective communication with all staff, contributing to a collaborative/ supportive work environment.
• Meet all expectations and requirements as stated in the KIPP Indy Employee Handbook
• Willing to meet the varied and constant needs of the students and staff at KIPP Indy

COMPETENCIES

• Demonstrates tenacity, persevering through significant challenges to reach goals
• Manages time and resources effectively, prioritizing efforts according to organizational goals
• Communicates across lines of differences and proactively creates inclusive environments
• Holds high expectations for all students and expresses belief in their potential to become exceptional leaders who will make a positive impact on the world.

• Valid Indiana teaching license with an English Learner (EL) certification or eligibility (required).
• Bachelor’s degree in education, TESOL, or a related field (required).
• Minimum of 2 years of experience teaching multilingual learners (preferred).
• Strong knowledge of language acquisition theories and instructional strategies for English learners (required).
• Experience in developing and implementing ILPs (preferred).
• Commitment to the KIPP Indy mission and the Indianapolis community (required).
• Pass a criminal background check (Required)

Licensed teacher starting at $50,000

Salary is commensurate with experience and includes a highly competitive benefits package. Opportunities for performance-based bonuses are also available.

jobs.title: Senior Cost Manager / Quantity Surveyor – Data Center Construction

This position can be based in the Chicago, IL area, with travel to the project site near St. Louis, MO approximately once per month for 2–3 days.

In this role, you will serve as a key day-to-day client interface, leading the delivery of high-value cost management services across a complex, multi-phase data center development. You will be responsible for driving cost planning, procurement strategy, change management, and commercial governance, ensuring consistency, accuracy, and rigor across multiple workstreams and packages.

The ideal candidate is a confident, client-facing professional with strong communication skills, a proactive mindset, and the ability to operate both independently and collaboratively within a high-performing project team.

Responsibilities:

• Lead scope delivery for assigned phases/packages; coordinate with designers, GC/CM, and trade partners.
• Prepare and present clear written and verbal updates, executive summaries, and recommendations.
• Develop estimates and cost plans through design, presenting updates at each design milestone.
• Review and reconcile estimates with the GC/CM and design team; validate quantities and scope alignment.
• Provide commercial input to design optioneering and value engineering (VE); inform engineering priorities based on cost/constructability.
• Support procurement strategy and contract administration; review contractor/subcontractor pricing.
• Lead/assist price negotiations to drive fair and competitive contract values.
• Provide independent cost/market inputs using internal benchmarks and supplier intelligence.
• Manage change orders end‑to‑end: evaluate, negotiate, and track through approval.
• Maintain commitment tracking, contingency management, trend analysis, and risk registers.
• Ensure robust cost validation, auditing, and change control processes throughout delivery.
• Produce timely monthly cost reports, forecasts, cash flows, and variance analyses.
• Coordinate funding data, develop executive‑level summaries, and facilitate VE/risk sessions.
• Implement and maintain Turner & Townsend Business Management Systems (BMS) and delivery tools; comply with SOX controls where applicable.
• Mentor and coach junior team members; model T&T purpose, values, and service excellence.
• Contribute to continuous improvement of internal tools, templates, benchmarks, and best practices.
• Support account growth and cross‑selling through strong stakeholder relationships.
• SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.

• Ability to travel to the St. Louis, MO area monthly for a 2–3 day trip.
• Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Engineering, or related field (advanced degree a plus).
• A minimum of 6-7 years of cost management / project controls experience, including leading cost deliverables on medium‑to‑large, complex projects.
• Data center or mission‑critical/industrial project experience strongly preferred.
• Consultancy experience preferred; strong knowledge of procurement, commercial management, contracts, change, and risk.
• Demonstrated expertise in estimating, cost planning, budgeting, reporting, and cost control systems.
• RICS accreditation (or working toward it) strongly preferred.
• Excellent client‑facing communication and negotiation skills; ability to influence stakeholders.
• Strong analytical skills with high attention to detail; proficiency with industry‑standard cost tools.

jobs.title: Senior Cost Manager / Quantity Surveyor - Data Center Construction
jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend are looking for an experienced Senior Cost Manager and/or Quantity Surveyor to act as the key, day to day client interface on a major, mission‑critical hyperscale data center construction project, ensuring that client objectives are met through the delivery of a value-added cost management service.

To be successful in this role you must have great communication skills and be comfortable operating in a client-facing role. The ideal candidate will be self-motivated, driven, and able to work independently as well as part of a team. In this significant position, you will be responsible for providing leadership and direction, embedding, and promoting the purpose, values, and vision of Turner & Townsend.

The project site is located approximately 25 miles south of Naperville, in Grundy County. This role offers a hybrid schedule with an expected presence on‑site 3 days per week depending on the project phase and client requirements.

Responsibilities:

• Estimating and negotiating change orders throughout the construction lifecycle.
• Provide estimate and cost planning to include producing and presenting the final cost plan.
• Review and participate with the design services team and general contractor in the development of cost estimates.
• Reconcile changes and assist the general contractor to ensure that their data is accurate.
• Communicate or meet with the general contractor and owner of project manager to gather status information to prepare a cost estimate update.
• Prepare written comments to the general contractor’s submissions, including the executive summary.
• Coordinate all sources of cost information for cost discussions and suppliers direct from NPA, subs, quantities from A/Es.
• Inform and drive engineering priorities based on cost impact.
• Work proactively with minimal supervision to resolve scheduling issues.
• Manage cost checks and carry out valuations on larger projects. Complete timely, accurate cost checking and valuation processes.
• Participate effectively with post-contract cost variances and the change of control processes.
• Manage Cost impact / contingency management and commitment tracking logs.
• Prepare funding data presentations and coordinate VE sessions with stakeholders.
• Developing cost plans and estimates through the design phase, delivering updated cost plans at appropriate design milestones.
• Providing commercial input to design optioneering and input into value engineering exercises.
• Reviewing contractor and subcontractor pricing and leading negotiations on behalf of the client to drive fair contract prices.
• Performing quantity surveying, cost controls, and change management activities throughout the project lifecycle.
• Ensuring that post-contract cost variances and change control processes are managed effectively.
• Ensuring that cost auditing and valuation work is managed effectively and that a robust process for cost validation is in place.
• Carrying out the production of monthly cost reports for presentation to the client.
• Ensuring that final accounts are negotiated and agreed upon in a timely manner.
• Compiling built cost estimate records for benchmarking purposes.
• Identify, coach and mentor talent to realize their potential and celebrate the success of others.
• Display excellence in leadership and service delivery on commissions is in line with the conditions of appointment
• Financial Management - Utilize internal software to track ongoing margin levels and monthly fee/resource forecasts for each commission and financial reports
• Implement and maintain the use of internal Business Management Systems and company delivery methodologies and tools in the office to ensure consistent delivery of best practice for Clients and the company
• Be a role model that drives a one business culture that achieves great outcomes by striking the right balance for our people, clients, stakeholders, and society.
• SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.

• Bachelor’s degree in construction management, cost management, quantity surveying, engineering or field related to construction.
• RICS accredited or working towards it is advantageous.
• Minimum 5-7 years of relevant experience working in a cost management role in the construction industry.
• Construction consultancy experience is strongly desirable.
• Prior experience supporting data center, mission-critical, industrial, or similar large-scale infrastructure projects is strongly preferred.
• Experience of leading cost management on medium or large sized construction projects of medium to high complexity.
• Good knowledge of construction industry technical matters, such as different procurement routes, value management, and value engineering.
• Excellent communication skills.

*On-site presence and requirements may change depending on our client's needs.

The base salary range for this role is $135K-$165K USD. This range reflects the company's good faith estimate of the base salary for this position at the time of the posting. Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity. In addition to base salary, employees may be eligible for bonuses and a comprehensive benefits package.

jobs.title: Senior Scheduler (Data Center Due Diligence and Preconstruction)
jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend is seeking a Senior Scheduler for a confidential hyperscale data center client, both setting the standard other reviewers work to and carrying a portfolio of independent schedule reviews yourself. You will test whether developer-provided delivery dates are realistic, and you will decide what a rigorous review looks like for everyone doing that work alongside you.

Responsibilities

• Schedule review: Assess developer construction schedules from the ground up: logic, critical path and near-critical activity credibility, float, and sequencing. Confirm whether the delivery date, power connection, and commissioning and testing timelines are actually realistic, against the client's and our team's benchmarks.
• Supply chain and resourcing: Review the equipment and staffing plan behind a schedule, including long lead equipment orders and resource loading, and confirm whether the labor and materials backing the dates are firm commitments or assumptions.
• Evidence discipline: Be precise about what is known versus what is assumed. State plainly whether a number or date is confirmed, estimated, or simply what the developer has claimed, and hold your team to the same standard.
• Risk identification: Flag the risks a clean-looking schedule hides: long lead equipment, permitting, utility connections, seasonal weather, and compressed commissioning windows.
• Trend and variance analysis: Track how each schedule moves from one review to the next, not just a single point-in-time snapshot, and flag material variances and their likely cause.
• Acceleration analysis: Where a date is at risk, assess what could actually recover time, and which options are real versus cosmetic.
• Delivery handover: At construction start, make sure a clear schedule record, what was confirmed, what was assumed, and what is still an open risk, is handed to the onsite construction team on every deal your team touches.
• Setting the standard: Define what a complete, defensible schedule review looks like: the checklist, the depth of testing, and the level of evidence required, and hold every review on the team to it.
• Quality control: Review your team's higher-stakes findings before they reach a client, catching gaps or unsupported claims before anyone else does.
• Benchmarking: Build and maintain the library of schedule benchmarks, typical durations for long lead equipment, permitting, energization, and commissioning, that the whole team reviews against, so judgment calls are grounded in real data rather than memory.
• Process improvement: Build and refine the templates, tools, and checklists the schedule discipline runs on as the portfolio and the team grow.

SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.

• 10 plus years of planning and scheduling experience, data center or other mission-critical facility delivery strongly preferred.
• Preferably located in/near San Francisco, CA or Northern VA but will consider remote candidates as well as long as they are able to travel occasionally for site visits and team collaboration.
• Working fluency in P6 or equivalent scheduling software, including logic, critical path, and float credibility.
• Familiarity with earned value management (EVM) or similar progress-measurement methods, to independently sanity-check a developer's reported percent complete against actual schedule progress.
• Practical knowledge of long lead equipment timelines, utility and energization sequencing, permitting, and commissioning and testing durations in complex facility construction.
• Understanding of acceleration levers in data center construction, and the judgment to tell a real one from a cosmetic one.
• Comfortable delivering a difficult finding to a developer directly, professionally, and on a deadline, and comfortable holding a colleague's work to that same standard.
• Able to work from incomplete or dated information and state the caveats plainly, rather than waiting for a perfect dataset.
• Proven ability to manage competing priorities across multiple concurrent projects, and across a team's workload, not just your own.
• Strong written communication. Findings need to be usable by people who were not in the review, and feed directly into the client-facing due diligence report.
• AACE PSP or PMI-SP certification is a plus, not required.
• Technologically proficient, including MS Suite and Google Workspace in addition to scheduling software.

Project/Program Specifications

• Market sector experience: Data center development, mission critical facilities, or complex technical and hyperscale buildings strongly preferred.
• Software specific requirements: P6 or equivalent scheduling software, MS Suite, and Google Workspace.
• Travel: Minimal, approximately 3 days per month, plus occasional site visits and team collaboration.

Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity. In addition to base salary, employees may be eligible for bonuses and a comprehensive benefits package.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
The Technical Program Manager (TPM) is responsible for ensuring the successful planning, execution, and delivery of complex technical initiatives. This position requires a strong technical background, a deep understanding of system architecture, and the ability to effectively collaborate across functions to achieve impactful outcomes. The TPM transforms product plans into technology requirements for services, determining which resources will be required to deliver initiatives on the product roadmap and then aligning those to various workstreams in the program. The TPM is accountable for program management throughout the entire lifecycle, including analysis, design, development, testing, implementation, and post-implementation phases. The TPM is accountable for on-time delivery of milestones, identifying and mitigating risk, adherence to service architecture requirements, quality, and ultimately ensuring that the overall technical solution achieves the intended business outcomes.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

• Manage the lifecycle of complex cross-functional product initiatives. Unblock teams and increase the speed of delivery. Negotiate resources and priorities and escalate effectively.
• Transform product requirements into technology requirements for services and map to required resources needed for execution. Establish individual workstreams. Leverage technical expertise to define scope, effort, success metrics, and delivery timing for each workstream. Identify and resolve priority discrepancies in bottlenecked resources. Track resource spend against budget.
• Coordinate program execution across impacted cross-functional federated teams (Data & Analytics, UX/UI, DevSecOps, Architecture / Infrastructure, Product Management, and Engineering) and ensure that everyone is aligned towards common objectives resulting in ongoing alignment of milestones, deliverables, and dependencies so that issues are found early and solved, reducing risk to delivery dates
• Confirm alignment of project goals with business objectives; establish communication cadence with stakeholders to secure necessary resources and support
• Partner closely with tech leads to bridge the business needs with the technical challenges to help balance time-to-market with quality, reliability, security, and scalability
• Establish overarching program-level governance to ensure alignment across projects and promote effective coordination; including success metrics, technical standards, defining authority levels, and establishing communication channels among project teams
• Proactively identify potential technical and operational risks, develop mitigation strategies
• Gain acceptance of high-level design and detailed design documentation through enterprise and peer design reviews
• Support the design of application architecture components and documentation of relevant system or software changes or enhancements
• Communicate ideas effectively, verbally and in writing, to a wide range of audiences including Directors and VPs. Foster a constructive dialogue, harmonize discordant views, and lead the resolution of contentious issues (build consensus). Partner successfully with customers, Product owners, other stakeholders, and engineering teams.
• Practice and model best practices in technical project and program management such as communications, stakeholder management, planning and scheduling, identifying critical path, managing within budget and resource constraints, managing risk, and escalating appropriately.
• Actively mentors/develops others. Performs Tech promo assessments.

YOU’VE GOT WHAT IT TAKES IF YOU HAVE:

• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related technical or business field
• Experience in a similar role in a SaaS Product organization
• 7+ years of software development or architecture experience
• 7+ years of experience in a software defined infrastructure (SDi, SDDC, SDE) environment, preferably architecting IaaS, SaaS, PaaS offerings
• 5+ years of technical program management experience working directly with software engineering teams
• Systems Thinking: possess a holistic point of view and understand how various components and subsystems within a program or project interact with each other
• Ability to transform product requirements into technology requirements for services
• Strong understanding of system design and service-oriented architecture, ability to design architecture components
• Analytical skills: deal with complex program data, metrics, and performance indicators
• Agile mindset with ability to assess complexity and determine suitable approach to manage an overall program and sub-programs; Waterfall, Scrum, Kanban, etc.
• Project management, leadership, dependency management, and cross-group collaboration experience
• Communication/presentation experience through all levels of the organization, technical and non-technical
• Deep technical expertise of respective service such as cloud, storage, or compute, in design and development
• Experience with modern tools such as Atlassian (Jira, Confluence)

IT WOULD BE NICE IF YOU:

• Broad knowledge of build, integration, deployment, and provisioning of cloud services; primarily MS Azure and Google Cloud
• Advanced understanding of SaaS applications and cloud-native architectures
• Experience with Modern front-end frameworks, responsive web designs, C#, Java, Structured and Unstructured databases, Datawarehouse, and large-scale analytics.
• Expertise in multiple version control systems (Git, GitHub, Bitbucket, etc.) and Cloud Foundry development
• Experience with configuration management systems (Chef, Puppet, BOSH)
• Experience with APIs, Service bus and other integration technologies.
