jobs.title: Senior People Ops Generalist
jobs.description:
540 is looking for a Senior People Ops Generalist to own the operational backbone of our People function. We’re about 100 people across 25+ states, building software for federal missions including the Army, Air Force, and USCIS. Keeping our processes light and our culture strong only works when the machinery underneath is airtight — payroll lands, benefits work, employees get answers, managers get good guidance, and we stay compliant everywhere we operate.

That’s where you come in.

You’ll own the day-to-day operation of People Ops: benefits and 401(k), payroll, culture and employee experience, compliance, leave, employee relations, HR systems. You’ll report directly to our Chief People Officer (CPO), and the two of you will make up the core People Ops team. You’ll also work closely with our Ops Coordinator, Director of Talent, and Senior Talent Acquisition Specialist across the employee lifecycle — from offer and onboarding through promotions, internal talent mobility, and offboarding.

You’re joining at an important moment. 540 is transitioning from a PEO to Rippling ASO, which means we’re taking greater ownership of our benefits, payroll, compliance, and employment risk. Rippling will handle a lot of the mechanics; the judgment calls will belong to us — and many of them will belong to you.

You’ll step into an active migration involving a new benefits stack, state account transitions, and our first in-house payroll runs, with the opportunity and authority to help shape what the People Ops function becomes. Our benefits plan year renews January 1, so you’ll join at a meaningful point in the annual cycle and help own the renewal that shapes our plans for the year ahead.

You won’t inherit a finished function. You’ll inherit a real one, in motion, with the authority to make it better.

Location: Hybrid — Arlington, VA (1-2x per month)
Citizenship & Clearance Requirement: Must be eligible to work in the United States without sponsorship
Education Requirement: Bachelor’s Degree
540 Internal Thrive Level: Senior People Ops Generalist

WHY 540?

540 is a forward-thinking company that the government turns to in order to #getshitdone. We don’t just talk about innovation – we deliver it. We break down barriers, build impactful technology, and solve mission-critical problems.

HOW YOU’LL DRIVE IMPACT

• Own benefits administration across medical, dental, vision, life, disability, FSA/HSA, our Medical Expense Reimbursement Plan (MERP), and voluntary benefits, including enrollments, qualifying life events, and terminations

• Manage carrier invoice reconciliation, along with eligibility and claims escalations

• Own open enrollment - HRIS configuration, employee communications, and post-enrollment audits

• Administer our 401(k) program, including contribution funding, eligibility, and loans, and ACA measurement tracking, 1094-C/1095-C filing, COBRA, and state continuation requirements

• Run end-to-end semi-monthly payroll for approximately 100 employees across 25+ states with support from Rippling ASO, including regular payroll, off-cycles, retroactive pay, bonuses, and final pay

• Direct and verify Rippling’s work on state and local payroll tax registrations, withholding accounts, and unemployment insurance accounts as we hire into new jurisdictions; Rippling handles the filings, and you’ll be the one who confirms they’re right

• Understand and apply state-specific employment and government contracting requirements, including pay frequency, final pay deadlines, expense reimbursement, wage and hour requirements, and pay transparency

• Own onboarding as an employee experience rather than a checklist, with particular attention to the first 90 days, when 540’s culture transfers to new employees

• Partner with the CPO on employee engagement surveys and own their administration, analysis, and translation into visible, meaningful changes

• Own the perks and benefits program as a program: understand what employees actually use, retire what they don’t, and bring the CPO a recommendation at each renewal

• Own day-to-day employee experience programs including Great Place to Work certification, Fortune/Inc submissions

• Support the recognition day to day (Red Hot Awards) program, and make sure it stays fast and real

• Partner with the Ops Coordinator on 540 Week and company culture initiatives

• Administer FMLA, state paid family and medical leave, paid sick leave, parental leave, and other company leave programs across the states where we operate

• Run and document the ADA interactive process and coordinate workers’ compensation claims, injury reporting, and return-to-work processes

• Coach managers through performance concerns, including expectations, documentation, and difficult conversations

• Run the operational side of our employee feedback cycle, including timelines and set-up

• Serve as a trusted first point of contact for employee questions, concerns, and conflicts, handling sensitive information with judgment and discretion

• Maintain our employee handbook and state-specific addenda, and monitor legislative and regulatory changes across every state where we operate, flagging what needs to change before it becomes a problem

• Own compliance requirements including EEO-1, OSHA 300/300A, VETS-4212, state new-hire reporting, pay transparency, pay-data reporting, employment verifications, unemployment claims, and classification reviews

• Serve as an administrator and power user of Rippling, owning data integrity, workflows, permissions, audits, and People reporting

• Use AI and automation to eliminate repetitive People Ops work, improve accuracy, and create more time for work that requires human judgment

REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

• 5+ years of progressive People Operations/HR experience, including at least 2 years of hands-on multi-state payroll experience and a strong understanding of how wage and hour, leave, disability, final pay, reimbursement, and other employment requirements vary by jurisdiction

• A thoughtful, creative approach to People Ops — you design policies, processes, and programs around 540's people and culture rather than copying a template, and you can explain the reasoning behind what you build

• Hands-on benefits administration experience, including open enrollment and experience supporting 401(k), leave, and employee lifecycle programs

• Working knowledge of FLSA, FMLA, ADA, wage and hour requirements, and relevant state-level employment requirements — plus the ability to research and apply requirements when entering a new jurisdiction

• Demonstrated manager coaching and employee relations experience, including guiding managers through performance concerns, documentation, difficult conversations, warnings, and/or performance improvement plans

• Proficiency with a modern HRIS/payroll platform such as Rippling, Paylocity, Gusto

• Strong operational discipline and attention to detail when working with payroll, benefits, employee data, and compliance deadlines

• Sound judgment under ambiguity and the ability to handle highly sensitive employee and company information with complete discretion

• Strong plain-language communication skills — you can explain something like an HDHP or HSA to someone who has never selected a health plan without hiding behind HR jargon

• Comfort operating in a lean People function where you’ll work throughout the full employee lifecycle

• Comfort using AI and automation as part of your day-to-day work

NICE TO HAVE

• PHR/SPHR, SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP, CPP, or FPC certification

• People Operations experience within a mid-sized government contractor, including familiarity with federal contractor reporting requirements such as VETS-4212

• Experience supporting an HRIS implementation, PEO transition, or payroll migration; Rippling experience is a plus

• Experience administering a Medical Expense Reimbursement Plan (MERP)

• Experience supporting a high-growth, geographically distributed organization

• Demonstrated experience delivering successful employee engagement, recognition, and/or employee experience programs, such as earning or maintaining Great Place to Work certification

BENEFITS & PERKS

• Flexible PTO + all Federal holidays off

• Health, dental and vision insurance plans

• Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

• 401k with employer match

• Company-sponsored life insurance, short- and long-term disability

• Professional development (training, certifications, conferences)

• Paid cloud developer accounts

• Referral bonuses

• HQ office perks (parking / metro reimbursement, nitro coffee & lunches)

• Annual social events (540 Week, hackathon, charity golf tournament, etc.)

• Access to 540’s Washington Capitals & Nationals tickets

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY (EEO)

540's policy is to provide equal employment opportunity to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

jobs.title: Operation Program Manager
jobs.description:
Name of Employer: Formlabs, Inc.
Position Title: Operations Program Manager
Position Location: 35 Medford St., Somerville, MA 02143

Duties: Create formal phase-gate product development for manufacturing, enforcing entry/exit criteria for concept,
design, verification, pilot, and ramp stages. Own verification and validation planning across functional,
environmental, and reliability testing. Lead Operations readiness and production ramp planning, integrating
supplier capability, production readiness, and capacity models. Perform engineering trade-off analyses across
mechanical performance, reliability, manufacturability, and cost. - Validate design feasibility through prototyping,
testing, and simulation of structural, thermal, and functional behavior. Apply DFM/DFA principles to ensure
component geometry, interfaces, and tolerances are ready. Perform resource leveling and capacity planning across
engineering, operations, and suppliers. Identify and manage technical and operational risks using structured
mitigation plans. Design the global manufacturing and supplier network across Formlabs factories and external
partners. Perform lead-time and bottleneck analysis to protect launch and ramp schedules. Execute make-vs-buy
and supplier selection frameworks. Lead supplier negotiations and risk mitigation to ensure continuity of supply.
Build end-to-end cost models including BOM, labor, tooling, depreciation, yield, and overhead. Perform design-to-
cost and value-engineering trade studies. Evaluate capital investments using NPV, free cash flow, and ROI analysis.
Model yield, scrap, and rework impact on unit cost. Conduct cost variance and sensitivity analyses. Translate
engineering and manufacturing constraints into business impact assessments. Lead cross-functional Operational
Readiness Meetings for NPI execution. Produce data-driven executive reports integrating cost, yield, capacity, and
schedule. Apply DOE and statistical analysis to optimize yield and reduce variation. Lead root-cause analysis and
CAPA for defects and failures. Provide quality and risk dashboards to leadership. Manage engineering change
control and configuration management. Enforce risk-based quality systems aligned with ISO and industry
standards. Maintain traceability from requirements to validation results. Coordinate compliance across engineering,
operations, and suppliers. Integrate engineering, manufacturing, and supply-chain cost data into financial
governance systems. Perform budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis. Manage inventory valuation and COGS
tracking. Execute process-level cost-reduction initiatives. Define quantitative KPIs for yield, throughput, cycle
time, cost, and readiness. Drive continuous improvement initiatives. Maintain organizational accountability and
reporting structures. 15% of domestic travel required.

Requirements: Bachelor’s degree, or foreign equivalent in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or related
field and two years of experience in mechanical engineering, or hardware product development. Must have two years
of experience in each of the following: managing technically complex product development programs in hardware or
manufacturing; applying technical expertise to program strategy, cost modeling, and decision-making; program
management tools (scheduling, risk management, resource planning, and reporting); understanding of manufacturing and
operations fundamentals, including cost structures, plan vs actual performance management, and demand-supply planning;
and conducting financial/economic analysis and evaluation of long-term investment.

Offered Wage: $150,000 - $200,000/year.

CONTACT: To apply, please send resumes to Kelly Fagan - 35 Medford St. Ste 1, Somerville, MA 02143 or hr-
job@formlabs.com Reference #: 111475.

jobs.title: Developer Advocate
jobs.description:
Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US. 

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.




THE ROLE...

 

Synthesia's API and platform capabilities are quickly becoming the way developers embed AI video into their own products — automated training pipelines, localization workflows, customer-facing apps, and more. We're looking for our first Developer Advocate to make sure the developer world knows it, understands it, and gets building.

 

This is a builder-and-storyteller role. You'll be the face and voice of the Synthesia API to the outside world — writing, coding, speaking, and showing up wherever developers already are — while also being the internal champion who brings their feedback back into the product. You won't just talk about what's possible with Synthesia; you'll build the sample apps, tutorials, and demos that prove it, and you'll do it consistently enough that developers start to recognize your name before they recognize the logo.

 

You'll be part of the Developer Services team and work closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Developer Support to turn technical capability into developer adoption.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Create technical content that developers actually use

 - Write blog posts, tutorials, and how-to guides that show real, working integrations — not just feature announcements

 - Build and maintain sample apps, starter kits, and code snippets across common languages and frameworks

 - Produce video walkthroughs and livestreams using Synthesia's own product wherever it makes sense to "eat our own dog food"

 - Keep a fast, honest cadence — regular, dependable output builds more trust than occasional big launches

Show up where developers are

 - Represent Synthesia at conferences, meetups, hackathons, and webinars — as a speaker, workshop host, and booth presence

 - Run livestreams and community AMAs that go deep on real implementation questions, not marketing talking points

 - Build relationships with individual developers, technical bloggers, and community leaders who influence adoption

 - Travel as needed to be physically present in the communities that matter most to our growth

Be the credible technical voice

 - Get hands-on with the Synthesia API well enough to build things yourself, debug alongside developers, and speak with authority — not from a script

 - Earn trust the way any evangelist does: by being genuinely useful before asking for anything in return

 - Play the long game — plant seeds in developer communities today that turn into adoption months or years down the line

Close the loop with product

 - Channel developer feedback, friction points, and feature requests back to Product and Engineering in a structured way

 - Partner with Developer Support and Documentation to identify where the API's rough edges are creating support burden or lost adoption

 - Help prioritize the developer experience roadmap based on what you're hearing on the ground

Build the flywheel

 - Grow and nurture channels — Discord/Slack community, developer newsletter, social — where developers can find each other and find help

 - Identify and cultivate community advocates and early power users who can become case studies, co-speakers, or contributors

 - Measure what's working (content engagement, API sign-ups, community growth, sentiment) and adjust the playbook accordingly


ABOUT YOU...

 - Experience in developer relations, developer advocacy, technical evangelism, or a similar hybrid technical/communication role — ideally at a platform, API-first, or infrastructure company

 - Genuinely hands-on: comfortable writing code, working with APIs and SDKs, and building demo apps yourself, not just narrating what engineering built

 - A strong, authentic communicator across formats — written, live, and on stage — who can make technical concepts land with a developer audience

 - Comfortable with regular travel and public speaking; energized by meeting developers in person, not just online

 - A track record of sustained output (blog, video, or community content) rather than one-off campaigns — evangelism is a long game, and consistency is what earns trust

 - Skilled at listening as much as broadcasting: you can sit in a developer's frustration and turn it into a clear, actionable signal for the product team

 - Comfortable operating with a lot of autonomy in a fast-moving, still-forming function

 - Bonus: existing following or credibility within a developer community relevant to Synthesia's platform (video, AI/ML, automation, or enterprise software)


THE GOOD STUFF..

In addition to being a part of a great team, working in a fun and innovative environment, we offer:

 - A competitive salary + stock options in our fast-growing Series E startup

 - Hybrid working environment or remote friendly

 - 100% Medical, Dental & Vision

 - 401k Plan

 - Paid parental leave

 - 25 days of annual leave + Public holidays + paid sick leave

 - Fun culture with regular socials

 - A generous referral scheme

 - A brand new computer + monitor

 - Budget and support for conference travel, community events, and content production

Digital Sales Manager – Transform the Future of Surgery Through Digital Innovation

Are you passionate about leading sales teams, driving innovation, and shaping the future of healthcare technology? As a da Vinci Digital Sales Manager (DSM), you will play a pivotal role in accelerating the adoption of Intuitive’s cutting-edge digital ecosystem while building and leading a high-performing sales organization.

In this highly visible leadership role, you will develop and execute strategic growth initiatives, coach and inspire top sales talent, and partner cross-functionally to expand customer engagement with Intuitive’s digital solutions. By helping surgeons and healthcare organizations unlock the power of data, simulation, and connectivity, you will directly contribute to advancing surgical education, performance, and patient outcomes.

Our digital portfolio includes My Intuitive+, which can enhance a robotic-assisted surgery program with AI-powered video analysis, real-time surgical collaboration, and console-integrated simulation—all designed to help surgeons sharpen their skills. The My Intuitive + platform is available exclusively with da Vinci 5.

Key Responsibilities

• Build and Lead a High-Performing Team – Recruit, develop, and coach a world-class Digital Sales team focused on accelerating pipeline growth, customer acquisition, and market expansion.
• Drive Strategic Growth – Design and execute innovative sales strategies that increase adoption, utilization, and long-term customer success across Intuitive's digital portfolio.

This is a unique opportunity to lead at the intersection of healthcare, technology, artificial intelligence, and robotic-assisted surgery. jobs.title: Support Military Partnership
jobs.description:
Spektrum supports apex purchasers (NATO, UN, EU and National Government and Defence) and their Tier 1 supplier ecosystem with a wide range of specialist services. We provide our clients with professional services, specialised aerospace and defence sales, delivery, and operational subject matter expertise. We are looking for personnel to join our team and support key client projects.

Who we are supporting

Allied Command Transformation (ACT) is NATO’s leading agent for change: driving, facilitating, and advocating the continuous improvement of Alliance capabilities to maintain and enhance the military relevance and effectiveness of the Alliance. The main objectives of ACT are: providing appropriate support to NATO missions and operations; leading NATO military transformation; and improving relationships, interaction and practical cooperation with partners, nations and international organisations. ACT therefore leads Alliance concept development, capability development, training and lessons-learned initiatives and provides unfettered military support to policy development within NATO.

The program

Capability Development & Management Support (CDMS)

DCOS Capability Development (CAPDEV) acts as the Supreme Allied Commander Transformation's Director for guidance, direction and coordination of the activities and resources of the Capability Development Directorate.

The Requirements Division will execute all tasks and activities needed to support requirements management for NATO capabilities

The Capability Requirements (CR) Branch will develop the Capability Requirements Brief and recommended courses of action to resolve issues through the life cycle management of requirements using matrixed, cross-functional project-specific Requirements Management teams.

The Requirements Forward Branch (Mons) is responsible for conducting requirements development and management representation and engagement-related functions in Europe.

The Capability Division coordinates the development of capabilities from capability planning through acceptance and then disposal with management entities, NATO Headquarters staff and the NATO Governance Structure

The Capability Forward Branch (Mons) coordinates with ACO, NCIA, NSPA, NATO HQ, territorial Host Nations, and NATO Centres of Excellence (COEs) to support the development of capabilities.

Strategic Plans and Policy (SPP) supports Allied Command Transformation in formalizing military advice to shape future military strategy, political guidance, and other policy documents supporting NATO’s strategic objectives.

Role ID: ACT-CDMS-27-01-A-LC17

Role Duties and Responsibilities

• Contribute to the activities, outputs, coordination requirements, and battle rhythm of the Partnerships Branch in support of NATO’s partnerships objectives.

• Support the Partnerships Branch as the HQ NATO Headquarters Supreme Allied Commander Transformation central point of contact for partnerships-related work strands, including coordination with HQ NATO Headquarters Supreme Allied Commander Transformation Directorates, Branches, NATO HQ, Partner Nations, and relevant International Organizations, as required.

• Contribute to the development and delivery of briefings, point papers, speaking notes, reports, decision-support products, and other staff work for senior officers, decision makers, working groups, and external engagements related to partnerships.

• Contribute to the development, review, refinement, and implementation of policies, directives, concepts, processes, and procedures related to NATO military partnerships, including support to Bi-Strategic Command and Allied Command Transformation - level taskings.

• Support the identification, coordination, and tracking of ACT activities, Programmes of Work, exercises, experiments, training, education, and engagement opportunities open to Partners, ensuring coherence of messaging and alignment with NATO and ACT priorities.

• Support the maintenance of corporate memory, information and knowledge management, lessons identified, document traceability, and quality assurance mechanisms for Partnerships Branch activities.

• Ensure that partnership activities, documentation, and information-sharing considerations are coordinated in accordance with applicable NATO security, releasability, and information-management requirements.

• Support Key Leader Engagement preparation and execution, including background papers, engagement strategies, read-ahead material, talking points, engagement reports, and follow-up actions.

• Be prepared to travel to meetings, conferences, workshops, exercises, and other engagements both within and outside NATO’s boundaries for up to 30 days per year.

• Perform additional tasks as required by the Contracting Officer’s Technical Representative related to the labour category and within the scope of Partnerships Branch responsibilities.

• The role will be divided into three specialized scopes: Partner Capability Development, Innovation and Interoperability Partnerships Strategy, Concept Development, Policy and Analysis Defence Planning Integration and Partnership Framework Implementation

Essential Skills, Experience and Certifications

• University postgraduate degree (master’s or higher) in international relations, international security , international development, military studies (including military technology or operations research), foreign policy, public affairs, political science, or related discipline; or have attended a NATO or national military staff college (OF-3 level or higher).

• Experience working in the field of foreign/international security/international cooperation/defence/military affairs.

• Experience working within NATO Enterprise (preferred); or other International Organisation (in a Defence or Security-related position); or within a national mission, delegation, or embassy to an IO (in a Defence or Security-related position).

• Demonstrate a working knowledge of: NATO Partnerships; or security sector reform / defence and security capacity building; or defence planning; or military capability development / military applications of operations Research.

• Demonstrate experience in drafting for and/or briefing senior leaders/decision makers (Flag Officers and General Officers or civilian equivalent).

Working Location

• Norfolk, VA, United States.

Working Policy

• On-site.

Travel

• Some travel to other NATO sites may be required.

Security Clearance

Valid National or NATO Secret personal security clearance

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
WE’RE HIRING! If you love data and are looking for unlimited growth opportunities, we want to talk with you about joining Further.

Further is a data, cloud, and AI company whose focus is helping companies turn raw data into the right decisions. We have an award winning culture of extraordinary people. Our purpose is to enable people to thrive so that businesses can thrive. We believe that the work you do should matter - it should be meaningful to you professionally and personally, and it should have a positive impact on both you and our clients.  If this sounds exciting to you, let’s chat!

Project Manager

Further is looking for a Project Manager to independently own mid-sized client projects from kickoff through delivery. You'll build the plan, lead the team, manage the budget, and serve as the primary operational point of contact for the client.

This is a hands-on delivery role. You'll be the person who keeps a project clear, predictable, and low-friction — anticipating issues before they become escalations, protecting scope and quality, and giving clients confidence that the work is under control.

What You'll Do

• Plan and execute. Create and manage the detailed project plan — defining scope, building the schedule, securing resources, and managing the budget from kickoff through final delivery.

• Manage the project team. Run the day-to-day: assign tasks, clarify responsibilities, remove roadblocks, and make sure every team member is clear on their role and what's expected of them.

• Own client communication. Serve as the primary operational contact for the client, providing clear and consistent updates on status, tracking progress against milestones, and managing expectations throughout the engagement.

• Manage risk proactively. Identify, document, and mitigate project-level risks and issues. Develop mitigation plans and escalate critical issues to the Program Manager or Practice Lead when needed.

• Own delivery quality. Accountable for delivery process, quality control, and deliverable readiness — ensuring the team's work meets SOW requirements and Further's standards for excellence.

jobs.description:
Technical Leadership (DDR5 / DDR6)

• Own and guide the architecture, design, and implementation of DDR5 PHYs and contribute to DDR6-ready architectures.

• High-speed TX/RX datapaths
• Advanced equalization, termination, and training circuits
• DLL/PLL-based clocking solutions for multi-GHz operation
• Voltage, reference generation, and power-aware IO design
• Drive closure on timing, jitter, noise, SI/PI, and PVT robustness for aggressive DDR5/DDR6 data rates.
• Ensure compliance with JEDEC DDR5 specifications and alignment with evolving DDR6 standards and industry direction.
• Lead post-silicon bring-up, characterization, debug, and yield improvement, including lab and customer-system correlation.

People & Organization Leadership

• Build, lead, and mentor a team of analog and mixed-signal designers focused on high-speed memory interfaces.
• Set technical direction, performance expectations, and development plans for senior and principal engineers.
• Drive hiring, onboarding, and team scaling aligned with DDR5 production and DDR6 development needs.
• Foster a culture of technical rigor, ownership, and execution excellence.

Program & Cross-Functional Execution

• Own DDR5/DDR6 PHY execution balancing schedule, quality, and risk
• Partner closely with: Digital PHY and controller teams SoC integration and system architecture, Package, PCB, SI/PI, and validation teams, Product, program management, and customers
• Interface with foundries, IP vendors, and standards bodies as needed to ensure successful delivery and future readiness.

Methodology, Quality & Roadmap

• Establish robust design and signoff methodologies for next-generation high-speed PHYs.
• Drive continuous improvement in simulation accuracy, mixed-signal verification, and silicon debug efficiency.
• Lead long-term DDR5 sustainment and DDR6 technology roadmap planning, including architectural trade-offs and scaling strategies.
• Anticipate challenges from data-rate scaling, power efficiency, and advanced process technologies

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering (PhD preferred).
• 12+ years of experience in analog/mixed-signal IC design with deep focus on high-speed memory interfaces.
• 5+ years of people-management and technical leadership experience.
• Proven hands-on delivery of DDR5 PHYs or late-stage DDR4 designs transitioning to DDR5
• Strong expertise in: High-speed IO design and signal integrity, PLL/DLL and low-jitter clocking architectures,Mixed-signal verification and silicon validation, Advanced CMOS process considerations for IOs

Preferred Qualifications

• Direct involvement in DDR6 architectural studies or early-stage development.
• Experience at advanced nodes (7nm, 5nm, and below).
• Background in multi-generation memory PHYs or scalable PHY platforms.
• Ability to lead teams delivering multiple concurrent tape-outs.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills across technical and executive audiences.

Leadership Profile

• High technical credibility with the ability to dive deep when needed
• Strong execution mindset with disciplined risk management
• Effective mentor and team builder
• Strategic thinker with a roadmap-driven approach to DDR evolution
• Comfortable balancing hands-on engagement with organizational leadership

jobs.description:
About Cleerly

We’re Cleerly – a healthcare company that’s revolutionizing how heart disease is diagnosed, treated, and tracked. We were founded in 2017 by one of the world’s leading cardiologists and are a growing team of world-class engineering, operations, medical affairs, marketing, and sales leaders. We raised $223M in Series C funding in 2022 which has enabled rapid growth and continued support of our mission. In December 2024 we received an additional $106M in a Series C extension funding. Most of our teams work remotely and have access to our offices in Denver, Colorado, New, York, New York, Dallas, Texas, and Lisbon, Portugal with some roles requiring you to be on-site in a location.

Cleerly has created a new standard of care for heart disease through value-based, AI-driven precision diagnostic solutions with the goal of helping prevent heart attacks. Our technology goes beyond traditional measures of heart disease by enabling comprehensive quantification and characterization of atherosclerosis, or plaque buildup, in each of the heart arteries. Cleerly’s solutions are supported by more than a decade of performing some of the world’s largest clinical trials to identify important findings beyond symptoms that increase a person’s risk of heart attacks.

At Cleerly, we collaborate digitally and use a wide variety of systems. Our people use Google Workspace (GMail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides), Slack, Confluence/Jira, and Zoom Video, prior experience in these areas is a plus. Role or department specific technology needs may vary and will be listed as requirements in the job description.

While we are mostly a remote company, travel is required for some team meetings and cross function projects typically once per month or once per quarter, for some roles like sales or external facing roles travel could be up to 90% of the time.

Cleerly is committed to providing safe and effective medical software that meets customer needs and our intended use. The adherence to all applicable regulatory and statutory requirements establishes a clear framework for setting measurable quality objectives. Our commitment to continually improving our products and processes proactively manages risks, ensuring ongoing compliance throughout the entire software lifecycle.  Understanding this role's relevance and importance is critical to achieving Cleerly's quality objectives.

About the Opportunity

The Cleerly Core Lab is a global team of imaging professionals dedicated to our mission of creating a world without heart attacks. We are seeking self-motivated Core Lab Analysts to join our US Imaging Services team.

In this role, you will review and quality-check Coronary CT exams after they have been processed by our AI algorithms, ensuring comprehensive and accurate analysis for providers, hospitals, and patients. This is an ideal role for a Radiology Technologist with ARRT Certification looking to apply their clinical expertise in a highly operational, tech-forward, remote environment.

Core Responsibilities

• AI Data Verification: Analyze and refine AI-generated outputs from Coronary CTA exams.

• Quality Control: Evaluate Coronary CTA exams for image quality and compliance with clinical standards.

• Team Performance: Meet daily individual KPIs and productivity metrics.

Day-to-Day Execution

• Operational Excellence: Execute daily operational tasks efficiently in accordance with the established work plan.

• Proactive Communication: Maintain open lines of communication across the global team, ensuring strict adherence to training protocols, standardization, and data integrity.

• Continuous Improvement: Actively participate in continuous improvement initiatives by sharing feedback, contributing innovative ideas, and collaborating on team projects.

• Training & Development: Assist with the development and deployment of training materials, and provide constructive performance feedback to team members as needed.

• Team Collaboration: Engage actively in scheduled team communications and meetings, taking on leadership or ownership roles when delegated.

• Performance Metrics: Take accountability for achieving daily metrics, proactively flagging operational issues, and participating in routine problem-solving to resolve workflow deviations.

• Product Insights: Provide valuable operational feedback and clinical insights to support new product development when requested.

Schedule & Remote Work Environment

• Type: Full-time, Remote (Preference for candidates near NYC or Denver).

• Shifts: Must be able to work a continuous 9-hour daily schedule. Current available schedules (ET) include: 1pm–10pm ET

• Operational Coverage & Schedule Stability: Because the Core Lab supports 24/7 patient care, this role requires a continuous daily presence. Candidates must be available to work a set 9-hour daily schedule (which includes a 1-hour break). These schedules may include evenings, weekends, and holidays.

To provide stability for our team, Cleerly establishes the full-year working and holiday calendar every January, allowing team PTO to be scheduled as early as possible for reliable coverage. Standard schedule updates are provided with at least one month’s notice, and any urgent adjustments within that window are subject to mutual agreement.

• Perks: Cleerly provides a computer, monitor, and a work-from-home/internet stipend. You must provide a quiet, distraction-free workspace.

Training & Travel Requirements

• Onboarding: Extensive, mandatory 1-week in-person training in Washington, DC or New York City upon hire, followed by a 1-week session ~2 months later (fully supported with mentorship). Passing the training assessment is required to clear the probationary period.

• Ongoing Travel: Approximately 2-4 weeks per year within the US for training and team development, with potential for occasional international travel.

Qualifications

• Education/Certification: Associate’s Degree in Radiography and active ARRT certification.

• Experience: Experience in CT, Coronary CTA, or 3D post-processing is a strong plus.

• Technical Skills: Strong general computer literacy (Google Workspace/Drive/Sheets).

• Soft Skills: High attention to detail, proactive attitude, strong written communication, and a deep respect for healthcare compliance and patient confidentiality.

• Physical Demands: Ability to sustain prolonged daily screen time requiring excellent visual acuity and color perception.

Compensation

The base salary range for this role varies by location and is aligned to market benchmarks.

• Candidates located in higher-cost labor markets, including California, Washington, New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Massachusetts, and Washington, DC represent the middle to high end of the range, while candidates located in all other U.S. locations represent the low to middle end of the range.

• Final compensation is determined based on location, experience, skills, and internal equity.

This role is eligible for a 10% target annual bonus, resulting in the following base salary and Total Target Compensation (TTC) ranges:

• Base Salary: $80,000 - $85,000

• TTC: $88,000 - $93,500

*Total Target Compensation (TTC): Total Cash Compensation (including base pay, variable pay, commission, bonuses, etc.) Additionally, stock options, paid benefits, and employee perks are part of your total rewards.

Working at Cleerly takes HEART. Discover our Core Values:

• H: Humility- be a servant leader

• E: Excellence- deliver world-changing results

• A: Accountability- do what you say; expect the same from others

• R: Remarkable- inspire & innovate with impact

• T: Teamwork- together we win

Don’t meet 100 percent of the qualifications? Apply anyway and help us diversify our candidate pool and workforce. We value experience, whether gained formally or informally on the job or through other experiences. Job duties, activities and responsibilities are subject to change by our company.

OUR COMPANY IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER.  We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, protected veteran status, religion, physical or mental disability, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, or any other basis protected by law, ordinance, or regulation.

Cranial Technologies also provides treatment with EarWell® to correct infant ear shapes without surgery. With over 600,000+ successful outcomes, EarWell® is a proven, non-invasive treatment option for families.

Pediatricians and parents alike look to our Clinicians as the experts in diagnosing and treating plagiocephaly. Our treating Clinicians develop great relationships with our families at every stage of their treatment process.

We hire from various backgrounds because each background is a great fit in its own way. PTs and OTs are an excellent fit with their background knowledge of symmetry and asymmetry, cervical anatomy, torticollis, and infant/toddler development. Orthotists are also a strong fit because of their hands-on experience with orthotics and direct patient care.

• Direct patient care with minimal paperwork

• No productivity/patient quotas

jobs.title: Workplace Coordinator
jobs.description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The Workplace Coordinator / Workplace Associate owns the day to day front desk experience of our main Austin factory, across the street of our headquarters. This role supports our team, provides a friendly face to guest and team members alike, helps get the vendors coordinated and guided to the correct area or assigned to the correct team member, and keeps the culture strong. With your support, the rest of the team can focus on their work and be more efficient.

This is a high visibility, high trust role. You'll be the first point of contact for guests, onboarding and employees when it comes to the factory environment, and the person other teams count on to keep the space welcoming and organized.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the front desk and serve as the first point of contact for employees, visitors, candidates, vendors and other guests.

 - Coordinate onsite visits, notify interview panels when interviewers arrive, make sure that everyone is welcome and follow the the sign in procedures.

 - Keep the reception area, conference rooms and shared spaces, ensuring they are clean, organized, stocked and ready for employees and visitors.

 - Support employee onboarding sessions., workplace events and other day to day activities.

 - Work closely with the broader Workplace team, IT, Security and HR in order to assist different needs.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 1–3 years of experience in an office or workplace operations or front desk role.

 - Strong organizational skills, attention to detail and an ability to manage multiple priorities.

 - Professional, friendly and approachable communication style with strong customer service focus.

 - Ability to work independently, exercise good judgement and take initiative.

 - Comfortable using Google Workspace, Jira and other workplace tools.

 - Spanish language skills are a plus as the role regularly interacts with delivery drivers, vendors and visitors who might primarily speak Spanish.

 - Flexible and comfortable occasionally adjusting working hours to support business needs, including providing partial coverage during second shift at the factory.

 


ABOUT THE TEAM

Workplace at Base runs on the idea that the best offices are the ones people don't have to think about. Supplies are stocked before anyone notices they're low. Guests are greeted before they have to ask. Problems get fixed before they become complaints. That invisibility is the job and it requires a lot of hard work. We believe a great workplace function is proactive, not reactive, anticipating needs instead of responding to tickets. It's consistent and the experience at one site should feel like the experience at every site, even as we add more of them. We are resourceful, most problems don't need a bigger budget or a bigger team, just better judgment about what's actually worth solving formally versus handling on the fly.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

jobs.title: Founding Product Manager
jobs.description:
Founding Product Manager

Product • New York, New York • Full time • On-site

Base Pay: $200K to $300K | Offers Equity



ABOUT SANDSTONE

Sandstone is on a mission to elevate in-house legal from a support function into a true strategic partner. From day one, we've been clear about what we are—and are not. We are not replacing in-house legal teams. We are building a platform that amplifies them.

Our platform enables modern legal teams to move at the speed of AI, deliver better outcomes, and create measurable business value. We unify legal data, power end-to-end workflows, and organize business context within the tools teams already use. Sandstone is the home for AI-native legal departments.

Today, Sandstone is trusted by Fortune 500 companies and fast-growing innovators alike. We ship quickly, iterate relentlessly, and scale with intention.

When you join Sandstone, you become part of a team that believes deeply in the compounding power of collaboration, rigorous problem-solving, and obsessive attention to detail. Our engineering team is elite, our lawyers ship code every day, and we are dedicated to building the most delightful product an in-house lawyer opens in the morning—and closes at the end of the day.

We work five days a week out of our offices in the Lower East Side. Dogs welcome; shoes optional; chess encouraged.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We need a Founding Product Manager to help us realize our vision: a single pane of glass for in-house legal teams for legal work and institutional knowledge. We already have a team of cracked engineers, preeminent lawyers, and world-class designers; now what we need is a disciplined, rigorous product manager who can help bring the pieces together. We pride ourselves on executing strong ideas faster than any organization in the world - this is a role for folks who roll up their sleeves, get dirty, and get shit done.

As our team matures and grows, we want to build our capacities for user experience research, cross-functional communication, scoping, and risk mitigation - that’s where you’ll come in. We need your help to remain laser-focused on the actual workflow journeys of our end users and find the chokeholds that endanger our continued user growth. As part of this role, you’ll own a product vertical; you’ll also play an integral role on our product leadership team. In addition, you may lead customer enterprise deployments and/or a set of integrations.

To be successful in this role, you will be someone who thrives working in an early-stage, green field environment with a high degree of autonomy. You will collaborate closely with Liam Germain (CTO, Co-founder), Jarryd Strydom (COO, Co-founder), and engineers who care deeply about building a novel user experience. You will also help create and distill Sandstone’s product culture, processes, and systems. “Ship relentlessly” is a core value of our team: we are all builders, and we expect you will be, too.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Own the product roadmap for one of our verticals: decide what to build, prioritize ruthlessly, and ship continuously

 - Set product feature timelines and team goals aggressively but pragmatically: scope feature sets thoughtfully and mitigate risks where practicable

 - As a member of our product leadership team, help decide the future of our product roadmap and how Product works at Sandstone: how we prioritize, how we write things down, how we decide.

 - Move fast on two-way doors and ship to learn. For irreversible decisions, map the scenarios, pressure-test the paths, and make the tradeoffs explicit before we commit. Both modes, deliberately chosen.

 - Partner with our AI & ML engineers to define what "great" looks like for agentic workflows: accuracy, reliability, latency, and the moments where a lawyer needs to stay in the loop. Help decide what we measure and hold the product to it.

 - Spend time with General Counsels, legal ops leaders, and the day-to-day users inside their teams. Sit in on sales and post-sales calls. Study how our end users work in real life, and turn that into the next set of priorities

 - Work closely with Engineering, Design, our Forward-Deployed Engineers, and GTM teams; make sure the right hand knows what the left hand is doing


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 6+ years in product management, ideally including time at an early-stage, high-growth startup—ideally one you helped carry through a step change in size.

 - A track record of shipping 0-to-1 products and then scaling them, with outcomes you can point to.

 - The ability to earn the trust of strong engineers—by being useful, by being right often, and by knowing which projects don't need you.

 - Comfort managing complex systems, mapping genuinely complex workflows and translating them into products that feel simple.

 - You have a demonstrated track record of entrepreneurship or of success in an unstructured environment - you’re hungry, low ego, and generative.

 - You have the empathy to understand what a customer is feeling and the emotional intelligence to know what would feel natural to them.


BONUS

 - Experience in legal tech, legal operations, or building products used by in-house legal teams.

 - Technical enough to prototype, read a PR, or stress-test an approach with engineering before it becomes a spec.


WORKING AT SANDSTONE: BENEFITS & PERKS

 - Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance; HSA available depending on plan selection; 401K

 - 12 weeks paid parental leave

 - Flexible time off (20+ days PTO)

 - Annual learning & development stipend

 - Technology stipend, including unlimited spend on AI tooling

 - Daily lunch for in-office team members

At Sandstone, we value high ownership, flexibility, and curiosity. You'll have an outsized impact, work closely with ambitious colleagues, and help transform how legal teams work for the modern age.

jobs.description:
At Kailera, we are bold, authentic and committed to our mission of developing therapies that give people the power to transform their lives and elevate their overall health. What You’ll Do:

Kailera Therapeutics is seeking an experienced Data Management professional to join as Director, Data Management. This role is accountable for the timely delivery and high-quality execution of Data Management deliverables across early- and late-phase clinical trials. The Director partners closely with key study stakeholders to define and implement a clear, comprehensive data strategy for assigned programs and studies. This position reports directly to the Head of Clinical Data Management.

• Proactively identify risks and develop and implement mitigation or corrective action plans.

• 10+ years of clinical data management experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry (8+ years with an advanced degree).

• Strong command of electronic data capture (EDC) systems and clinical data warehousing technologies, with experience across a range of clinical data management platforms.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience in cardiometabolic disease areas.

jobs.description:
The Global Industry Marketing Director for Oil & Gas owns the marketing strategy and execution for one of IFS's key industry verticals. The role reports into Corporate Marketing but carries full accountability as a member of the Oil & Gas leadership team - bridging central marketing capability with commercial go-to-market execution.

The right candidate has in-depth understanding of the Oil & Gas industry: how operators, EPC contractors, and OFS companies make technology decisions, how buying cycles work, and what a credible IFS value proposition looks like in that context. They are a builder - comfortable setting strategy, developing demand generation programs and getting into the detail of execution - and they know how to align marketing investment directly to pipeline and revenue.

This is a senior role with real commercial ownership. It requires someone who is equally at ease presenting to the leadership team and rolling up their sleeves on a campaign brief. The role spans multiple geographies and time zones, so confidence operating in a global, matrixed environment - aligning regional teams, navigating different market dynamics, and building relationships across cultures - is essential.

The candidate will own the development and execution of Oil & Gas marketing plan globally and work on a variety of programs and actively contribute to the success of the Oil & Gas industry. Typical responsibilities will include:

• Define, own, and execute a global marketing strategy and annual demand generation plan that directly supports the growth in the Oil & Gas industry and go-to-market objectives.
• Build and lead a high-performing global marketing team; own and manage the Oil & Gas marketing budget, allocating investment across programs to maximize pipeline contribution and return.
• Own the content strategy and production of high-impact assets - thought leadership, solution messaging, webinars, event toolkits, and digital content - to support customer acquisition and pipeline goals.
• Define and execute an account-based marketing (ABM) strategy for priority target accounts, in close partnership with the sales and business development teams.
• Enable business development, account management, and regional marketing teams for key demand generation campaigns - providing clear campaign kits covering audience targeting, messaging, channel mix, execution steps, and success metrics.
• Track, analyze, and report on campaign performance - MQLs, SQLs, and pipeline creation - sharing dashboards with stakeholders to drive continuous optimization.
• Partner with Product Marketing to sharpen IFS Cloud's Oil & Gas value proposition; own the Oil & Gas pages on ifs.com, optimizing for SEO, AEO, user journey, and pipeline conversion.
• Apply AI-powered tools across the marketing workflow - content creation, campaign personalization, analytics, and reporting - to improve output quality and team efficiency.
• Lead IFS's presence at priority sector events (ADIPEC, ONS, CERAWeek, OTC, IFS Unleashed, IFS Connect) and manage Oil & Gas analyst relations with Gartner, IDC, and relevant industry bodies.

There is a 10–25% travel requirement as needed.

Required

• 10+ years of progressive marketing experience, with at least 5 years in a senior leadership role.
• Demonstrable experience marketing to, or working within, the Oil & Gas industry

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in English - including the ability to craft compelling executive narratives, present with confidence to senior leadership, and adapt messaging across audiences and formats.
• Experience working in a global, matrixed organization, demonstrating a global mindset-able to navigate diverse cultures, collaborate across regions, and adapt marketing strategies to different international markets.

jobs.description:
Octus

Octus is a leading global provider of credit intelligence, data, and analytics. Since 2013, tens of thousands of professionals across hedge fund, investment banking, management consulting, and law firm verticals have come to rely on Octus to make better, faster, and more confident decisions in pace with the fast-moving credit markets.
For more information, visit: https://octus.com/

Working at Octus

Octus hires growth-minded innovators and trailblazers across the globe to drive our business and culture. Our core values – Action Oriented, Customer First Mindset, Effective Team Players, and Driven to Excel – define an organizational ethos that’s as high-performing as it is human. Among other perks, Octus employees enjoy competitive health benefits, matched 401k and pension plans, PTO, generous parental leave, gym subsidies, educational reimbursements for career development, recognition programs, and much more.

Role

Our Direct Data Services team sits at the hyper-growth intersection of product innovation, domain strategy, and direct client impact. Currently, our Head of Direct Data Services is the primary anchor for credit analyst expertise. We are seeking a Credit Workflow Strategist to partner with him to institutionalize, scale, and expand this deep workflow knowledge across our broader team and our AI product suite.

In this role, you will be deeply embedded in the complex day-to-day workflows of our clients—specifically within the leveraged finance (LevFin) credit markets—and tasked with translating those intricate analytical needs into robust, AI- and data-driven solutions.

Our team is based in our New York City office, and operates on a hybrid, 3 days/week schedule.

Credit Workflow Strategist responsibilities

• Partner with the Head of Direct Data Services to codify LevFin workflow intelligence, scaling and expanding solutions knowledge across the broader internal team and product suite

• Act as a client-facing domain expert and trusted advisor to build relationships and solve complex problems for buyside, sellside, and advisory accounts

• Investigate and map our users' complex financial processes (e.g., credit agreements, debt structures, and covenants) to embed Octus's AI platform seamlessly into their daily workflows

• Apply advanced AI and LLM tools to prototype, test, and design tailored workflows that optimize manual credit analysis and document-heavy research for our clients

• Coordinate with Octus’ product and engineering teams to translate real-world client feedback into platform enhancements and product features

What we look for

• Experience in the leveraged finance credit markets, either on the buyside (credit funds, direct lending, asset management), investment banking, or credit advisory side

• High proficiency and comfort with leading AI tools and LLMs, with a strong interest in prompt optimization and workflow automation

• Strong desire to be client-facing, with a proven ability to build partnerships and solve highly complex operational problems for institutional clients

• Organized, detail-oriented with the ability to prioritize and respond quickly; ability to navigate ambiguity and manage multiple ongoing workstreams

• Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills

• Experience working directly with product, data, or engineering teams is a plus

As a result, compensation may vary within and across similar roles and positions. jobs.title: SDR Enablement Specialist
jobs.description:
ABOUT NOOKS.AI http://Nooks.ai:

Nooks is an applied AI lab building the Agent Workspace for GTM. We design AI agents that operate across the full sales action set, from account strategy to prospect research and outreach. Building 0→1 has never been easier, but selling at the speed of the market remains the last frontier for AI. Our mission is to 10x every seller by automating the busywork so they can focus on what humans do best: closing deals.



Today, over 1,500 customers run on Nooks, including Notion, HubSpot, Cursor, and Rippling. We’ve raised $70M+ from top VCs like Kleiner Perkins, which made its first sales-tech investment in over a decade with us. Since then, we’ve tripled ARR each year for 3 years running and grown a high-caliber team turning the art of sales into a scalable science.




THE ROLE

We’re looking for an SDR Enablement Specialist to help internal GTM teams, product managers, and key customers get more value from established Nooks workflows.

This is a hybrid role combining outbound SDR execution with workflow training and documentation. You’ll lead hands-on enablement sessions, support internal training programs, maintain our Notion and LMS resources, and help turn best practices into clear, repeatable workflows.

To maintain credibility as a Nooks expert (and to stay close to the product and the day-to-day reality of outbound) the role carries an active sales quota:

 - 2 qualified meetings booked per month

 - Minimum weekly outbound activity metrics

You’ll continue to live in Nooks, make calls from the sales floor, and use the product as an active SDR. That firsthand experience will help you document and teach the workflows that make our teams and customers successful.

This role is best suited for someone who wants to build a career in enablement, training, or GTM operations. It is not designed as a path to an AE or CSM promotion.




WHAT YOU’LL DO


LEAD INTERNAL NOOKS WORKFLOW TRAINING

 - Lead setup and Nooks workflow training for new SDRs during onboarding.

 - Teach established workflows across Nooks, HubSpot, and LinkedIn Sales Navigator.

 - Run tactical, hands-on sessions that help teammates confidently execute inside the platform.

jobs.title: Materials Supervisor
jobs.description:
At IEM, we’re not just building innovative electrical distribution systems, we’re shaping the future. IEM is dedicated to delivering world-class solutions for complex power needs. After 75 years, we continue to push the boundaries of what’s possible. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting out, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, grow, and make a lasting impact on industries that power the world’s most dynamic markets.

Position Summary:

IEM is currently seeking a Materials Supervisor for our San Antonio, Texas location and will report into the VP of Supply Chain.

This position will be based temporarily in NE San Antonio while our new manufacturing plant is coming online. Our permanent location is approximately 25 minutes away at Brooks, 7515 Inner Circle Dr., San Antonio, 78235. The position is also 100% in-office and does not offer remote work.

The Materials Supervisor is responsible for supervising the day-to-day materials operations, ensuring the safe, accurate, and uninterrupted flow of materials from receipt through supermarket inventory, point-of-use replenishment, production support, WIP, and final product shipment. This role oversees the team members and daily execution needed to maintain material availability, inventory accuracy, and production support.

The Materials Supervisor is expected to be a hands-on leader who supervises daily materials activities and supports continuous improvement efforts. The role partners closely with Supply Chain, Planning, Purchasing, Production, Engineering, and Quality to resolve material constraints, support material flow, participate in Kaizen initiatives, and help maintain standardized processes that support operational excellence.

Key Responsibilities:

• Supervise daily materials management activities, including supermarket operations, receiving, inventory control, material handling, replenishment, point-of-use delivery, WIP, and finished-goods material flow.

• Support the accuracy, availability, and flow of raw material, WIP, and finished-goods inventories by reinforcing transactional discipline, location control, cycle counting, and corrective action.

• Support the implementation of standardized materials management processes aligned with production requirements.

• Maintain and update the Plan for Every Part (PFEP) system, including part characteristics, demand and usage, container quantities, replenishment methods, storage locations, and point-of-use requirements.

• Support the design and day-to-day execution of lean material replenishment systems, including Kanban, supermarkets, point-of-use inventory, pull systems, and milk runs.

• Partner with Purchasing/Supply Chain and Planning to ensure materials are on track to support production schedules, and escalate shortages, constraints, or risks to customer commitments.

• Coordinate supermarket and point-of-use material flow, supporting continuous improvement of warehouse layout, slotting, material presentation, and replenishment efficiency.

• Support inventory optimization efforts that balance material availability, service levels, working capital, inventory turns, and production continuity.

• Participate in and help lead cross-functional Kaizen events and structured problem-solving activities focused on material flow, inventory accuracy, warehouse productivity, and production support.

• Use data and operational metrics to identify root causes and support improvement opportunities, applying tools such as A3, PDCA, 5 Why, Pareto analysis, Value Stream Mapping, and standard work as appropriate.

• Partner with Production Planning and Operations to monitor material availability and production progress, escalating material issues that threaten schedule attainment.

• Partner with the MRB, Purchasing, and Quality teams to support resolution of supplier issues, vendor return material authorizations, and material discrepancies.

• Support inventory control governance, in partnership with Finance, to help identify discrepancies, determine root causes, and implement corrective actions.

• Track and report materials KPIs, including inventory accuracy, shortages, replenishment performance, inventory turns, warehouse productivity, dock-to-stock performance, and material delivery to point of use.

• Supervise, coach, and develop materials and warehouse team members by establishing clear expectations and building accountability.

• Maintain a safe and healthy work environment by enforcing company policies and applicable local, state, and federal environmental, health, and safety requirements.

• Perform additional duties as assigned to support the team and organization.

Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in supply chain management, logistics, business, industrial engineering, or a related discipline; equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.

• 4+ years of experience in materials management, inventory control, warehouse operations, logistics, or supply chain within a manufacturing environment.

• 2+ years of experience supervising or leading a team in a warehouse, materials, inventory, or manufacturing environment.

• Experience supporting or participating in lean warehouse and material replenishment systems, including PFEP, Kanban, supermarket, pull, and point-of-use concepts.

• Experience participating in Kaizen events and structured problem-solving efforts.

• Experience working with ERP/MRP systems for inventory and materials planning; SAP, Oracle, or Infor Syteline experience is a plus.

• APICS CPIM/CSCP, Six Sigma, or Lean Manufacturing certification is preferred.

• Demonstrated career ambition with a track record of growth and increasing responsibility; highly promotable with the potential to take on broader leadership roles within a fast-paced, high-growth organization.

The future is bright at IEM. As IEM accelerates into its next phase of growth in San Antonio, we expect to create new opportunities across manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, logistics, and corporate functions. Keep an eye on our careers page to stay connected and explore the roles that will help power what’s next.

Compensation actually offered for this role will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate's geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors. A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to the full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the level and position offered.

Why Join IEM

At IEM, you’ll join a team that powers some of the world’s most ambitious projects. We’re engineers, makers, and problem-solvers who thrive on tackling complex challenges and delivering solutions that keep industries moving forward. If you’re driven, collaborative, and ready to make an impact, we’d love to hear from you. Your creativity and passion can help us achieve great things—come be part of the journey.

Learn more about IEM at https://www.iemfg.com

We offer comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support our employees' well-being, growth, and long-term success. View a snapshot of our benefits at https://www.iemfg.com/careers

Recruiting Scams

Beware of recruiting scams. IEM never charges candidates fees, and all recruiter emails come from an @iemfg.com address. If you suspect fraudulent activity, do not share personal information and report it to us at iemfg.com/contact

jobs.title: Lead Nuclear Digital Instrumentation & Controls (I&C)
jobs.description:
We don’t just build technology—we engineer the future. From next-gen aerospace to cutting-edge defense systems, we tackle the toughest, mission-critical challenges that keep people safe and push the limits of innovation. This is where problem-solvers, innovators, and big thinkers thrive.

Quest Defense Systems and Solutions is looking for a Lead Nuclear Digital Instrumentation & Controls (I&C) IV&V Engineer to provide technical leadership in the verification and validation of complex digital control systems used in the nuclear industry.

This is an engineering role—not simply a test execution position. You will determine what needs to be verified, how it should be tested, and what evidence is needed to demonstrate compliance. You'll work across software, hardware, firmware, FPGA, systems engineering, quality, and project teams to evaluate system performance, identify technical risks, and ensure requirements are fully verified.

Location: role is remote with significant travel to customer and project locations.

Travel: The initial training period requires approximately 6 months in Wilmington, NC, followed by project work in Nampa, ID. Candidates should be comfortable with extended travel and onsite customer support.

• Adheres to ethical standards of practice.
• Calls for an ethics consult when appropriate.

EBP and Research

• Implements nursing interventions consistent with the established plan of care based on evidenced based care.
• Maintains and advances the professional image and science of nursing and the practice of professional nursing through use of best available evidence utilizing resources such as Ovid/Joanna Briggs, Up to Date, Culture Vision, and other reliable sources of evidence.

Healing Safe Environment

• Promotes and strives to protect the health, safety and rights of the patient

• Rounds hourly in collaboration with patient care technician

• Participates as a unit safety facilitator or as identified resource for quality initiatives as requested
• Participates in unit huddles

Relationship to Colleagues

Shared Leadership

• Demonstrates effective interpersonal skills in leading and directing others; deals with conflict directly and appropriately.
• Demonstrates proficiency in the charge nurse/preceptor role when assigned; assumes responsibility for coordinating patient care for the entire unit.

• Assists with precepting, unit orientation, and mentoring as requested.
• Participates in the peer evaluation process by providing feedback to colleagues on a regular basis, and through participation in clinical case peer review.
• Works collaboratively with all hospital services to responsibly accomplish daily work and maintain an environment of excellence.
• Identifies barriers to effective clinical practice and communicates to nursing leadership and practice operations council.

Resource Utilization

• Ensures an appropriate level of care order is documented in the EMR for all admissions.
• Understands and adheres to the charging of supplies.
• Participates in any value based unit/organizational initiative.
• Demonstrates a personal commitment to decreasing utilization overtime hours.

Use of Technology

• Assures all electronic and paper documentation is complete.
• Utilizes the guardrails for the Alaris pump.
• Understands physiologic monitoring and the implications to drive changes to clinical management of the patient.
• Utilizes the bed management system
• Identifies new technologies for unit, hospital or system use.
• Participates in CEOC activities for the advancement and optimization of the medical record as requested.

Relationship to Self

Professional Practice

• Attends internal professional development offerings i.e. Schwartz Rounds, Nursing Grand Rounds.
• Obtains certification in the nursing specialty of practice.
• Demonstrates accountability for his/her professional practice-competencies, ELM learning, dress code adherence
• Participates in professional organization through membership, leadership, or committee work

Required:

• Basic Life Support
• Strong interpersonal skills
• Ability to collaborate with others
• Strong analytic abilities
• Associate Degree Nursing (ADN) acceptable with commitment to obtain a BSN from an accredited program within three years of first day of employment in clinical nurse role.

Preferred:

Additional Information

Northwestern Medicine is an equal opportunity employer (disability, VETS) and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, gender identity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or any other protected status.
