jobs.title: Applied AI Scientist, Autonomous Defense
jobs.description:
Get to Know Us

Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs. 

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

 

What You'll Do

We're looking for an AI Researcher to build the agents that turn our offensive knowledge into defensive action.



You'll build agents that reason from a proven attack path to the specific control changes that break it - EDR policy, firewall and segmentation rules, conditional access, detection content, cloud IAM, GPO - apply or stage those changes in the customer's environment, and then prove the fix by re-running the attack.



That last part is why this is tractable. Most defensive AI has no ground truth and gets graded on whether its advice sounds reasonable. Ours gets graded on whether the attack still works. You will have a real outcome signal on a short loop, and hundreds of thousands of prior tests to learn from. It is also why this is hard. These agents run inside customer tenants and modify  production security controls. A bad change is an outage or a new hole in someone's defense. The reasoning problem and the safety problem are the same problem here, and you will own both.



The goal is closed-loop defense: find, fix, verify, running autonomously at enterprise scale. If you want to work on agents where the feedback is real and the stakes are real, this is the job for you.



Responsibilities

 - Build the reasoning systems that map proven attack paths and exploitation telemetry to specific, applicable control changes, ranked by effectiveness against operational blast radius.

 - Turn our pentest data into training and evaluation data. Extract the signal of why an attack succeeded in one environment and failed in another.

 - Design and run counterfactual experiments in representative test environments: would this change have broken this attack chain, what does it cost operationally, and does it generalize beyond the tenant it was learned in.

 - Design the reasoning layer over heterogeneous control planes so an agent can work across vendor APIs with different policy models without a hardcoded playbook per product.

 - Design the safety architecture for autonomous change — dry-run and simulation, blast-radius classification, approval gates for high-impact actions, staged rollout, rollback, and an audit trail a customer's change board will accept.

 - Work with our attack engineers and detection engineers to define target agent behavior and diagnose failure modes: ineffective remediations, over-broad changes, business-breaking policy edits, and recommendations that look right and don't hold on re-test.

 - Own problems end to end in a 0→1 environment where requirements are ambiguous, systems move fast, and reliability matters, because the output lands in someone's production security posture.



What You'll Bring

Required

 - Strong ML engineering experience building, evaluating, and deploying production AI systems, with hands-on work in deep learning, transformer models, and PyTorch.

 - Hands-on experience with at least one of: post-training large language models (supervised fine-tuning, distillation, preference optimization, RL), or designing agentic systems with tool use, planning, and long-horizon execution that hold up outside a demo.

 - A track record of building evaluation systems for open-ended tasks where there is no clean label and success is judged by outcome.

 - Experience reasoning over structured, heterogeneous, messy real-world data — configurations, graphs, logs, policy documents — rather than clean benchmark datasets.

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals and a track record of shipping and maintaining production-quality code in Python, not just scripts and proofs of concept.

 - Experience with data pipelines, distributed systems, and cloud infrastructure, preferably AWS.

 - Ability to work across model behavior, APIs, and infrastructure, and to collaborate closely with attack engineers, detection engineers, product, and infrastructure.

 - Ability to independently research unfamiliar systems and rapidly become the team's expert.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, including clear technical documentation.

 - Master's in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, plus 4+ years of professional engineering experience.
   
   

You do not need to have been a pentester or a SOC analyst. You do need to be seriously interested in how attackers and defenders actually operate, and willing to learn it in depth. The reasoning we are building cannot be designed by someone who does not understand the domain.



Preferred

 - Background in detection engineering, purple teaming, security engineering, offensive security, or incident response.

 - Hands-on familiarity with security control planes and their APIs and policy models: EDR (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Defender), firewalls and segmentation (Palo Alto, Fortinet), identity and conditional access (Entra ID, Okta), SIEM and detection content (Splunk, Sentinel), cloud IAM, WAF, MDM, and GPO.

 - Experience with causal or counterfactual inference, or with graph reasoning, planning, and search over large state spaces. Familiarity with Neo4j and attack-path analysis.

 - Experience building automation that takes write actions in production systems, along with the safety and change-management machinery around it.

 - Experience with adversarial robustness or prompt injection, particularly where an agent consumes untrusted input from the environment it operates in.

 - Experience integrating ML into production, multi-tenant SaaS, or running ML systems in customer-controlled or air-gapped environments.

 

Perks of Horizon3

 - Inclusive Team: We value diversity and promote an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.

 - Growth Opportunities: Be part of a dynamic and growing team with numerous career development opportunities.

 - Innovative Culture: Work in a collaborative environment that encourages creativity and out-of-the-box thinking.

 - Hybrid & Remote Work: We embrace a mix of remote and hybrid work models depending on role and location, including our Chicago office, where some roles require regular in-office presence.

 - Competitive Compensation: We offer competitive salary, equity and benefits. Our benefits include health, vision & dental insurance for you and your family, a flexible vacation policy, and generous parental leave.



Compensation and Values

At Horizon3, we believe that our people are our greatest asset, and our compensation philosophy reflects this core value. We are committed to fostering an environment where all employees feel valued, respected, and rewarded for their contributions. Our compensation structure is designed to be fair, competitive, and transparent, ensuring that every team member is recognized and compensated equitably across roles, levels, and locations.

In accordance with various State’s transparency regulations, we provide the following salary range information for this position:

 - Base salary range: $313,000 - $369,000 annually. The exact salary will be determined based on the selected candidate’s location, qualifications, experience, and relevant skills.

 - Additional compensation: All full-time roles are eligible for an equity package in the form of stock options.



You Belong Here

Horizon3 is not just an equal opportunity employer - we are a community that values diversity, equity, and inclusion as fundamental principles of our culture and success. We are dedicated to fostering a workplace where everyone feels welcome and respected, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, or any other legally protected status by law.

Our commitment to diversity and inclusion means we strive to attract, develop, and retain a workforce that reflects the varied communities we serve. We believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation and strengthen our ability to create cutting-edge cybersecurity solutions. At Horizon3, every team member is valued and supported in an environment that encourages personal and professional growth.

We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experiences, and we encourage all qualified individuals to apply. Come be a part of Horizon3, where your unique contributions are recognized, and your potential is limitless.



Other Duties

jobs.title: FP&A Manager
jobs.description:
The Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet (Global Energy Alliance) The Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet (Global Energy Alliance) works for a world where everyone has access to affordable, reliable, clean electricity and the means to use it to improve their lives. Our Alliance builds transformative public, private, philanthropic partnerships to end energy poverty and accelerate green economic opportunity. Founded in 2021 by The Rockefeller Foundation, IKEA Foundation, and Bezos Earth Fund, we design innovative projects/programs, unlock finance, strengthen institutions and transform markets, delivering progress anchored in deep community engagement. By uniting actors across the value chain, from households to heads of state, we go beyond individual projects to drive lasting systems change. With work in more than 30 countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, our Alliance aims to reach 1 billion people with clean electricity, prevent 4 billion tons of carbon emissions and create or improve 150 million jobs.

The FP&A Manager will report to Managing Director Global Finance with a dotted line to Controller and work closely with the US finance team to ensure the efficient and accurate financial operation of the US entity. The FP&A Manager is a key member of the Finance team, responsible for strengthening the organization's financial planning, forecasting, reporting and analysis capabilities while supporting the day-to-day financial operations of the U.S. organization.

This is a hands-on role that combines financial planning and analysis, management reporting, budgeting and forecasting, and U.S. financial operations. The FP&A Manager will work closely with the CFO, finance leadership, program and operational leaders, fundraising, and global colleagues to ensure that financial information is accurate, timely and useful for decision-making. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable building a financial model, explaining a budget variance to a program leader, preparing a month-end journal entry, reconciling a bank account, and presenting financial insights to senior leadership.

As a global nonprofit, the Global Energy Alliance operates across multiple countries and programs. The FP&A Manager will therefore help connect U.S. financial reporting and operations with global planning, forecasting and resource allocation, and will collaborate effectively with colleagues across multiple time zones and cultural environments.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting

• Work closely with MD Global Finance to lead the organization’s annual budgeting process in partnership with development, program, and operational leaders.

• Build and maintain financial models covering revenue, personnel, operating expenses, programs, strategic initiatives, and portfolio deployment.

• Partner with budget owners to develop realistic financial assumptions and monitor performance against approved budgets.

• Prepare scenario analyses to support strategic decisions, including changes in funding, staffing, program activity and organizational priorities.

• Analyze financial performance by country, region, program and/or funding source, and support consolidation of global financial information.

Financial Analysis & Management Reporting

• Perform budget-to-actual and forecast-to-actual variance analysis and prepare financial reporting packages for all budget holders.

• Identify key financial trends, risks, opportunities and drivers and translate them into actionable recommendations.

• Work closely with MD Global Finance to develop dashboards and management reports that provide clear visibility into organizational financial performance.

• Prepare financial presentations and analysis for the CFO, MD Global Finance, Leadership Team, and the Finance & Investment and Audit & Risk Committees of the Board as appropriate.

• Provide ad hoc financial analysis to support strategic and operational decision-making.

Financial close, reconciliations and reporting

• Support the timely completion of the month-end, close in line with department and CFO deadlines.

• Prepare monthly balance-sheet reconciliations for assigned accounts — including grant payables (grants schedule-- payables and lapses), payroll control accounts and benefits-related entries.

• Complete monthly reconciliations for bank accounts, ensuring reconciling items are documented and resolved on a timely basis.

• Reconcile grants expense and grants payable between NetSuite and Salesforce and maintain grant roll forward schedules.

• Prepare monthly payroll-related schedules, including health-insurance allocations, reclassify monthly bills by department in NetSuite, and reconcile Activpayroll withdrawals and BRI FSA prepaid-plan accounts to bank statements and funding reports.

• Prepare, review and/or coordinate recurring and non-recurring month-end journal entries, including accruals, prepaids, allocations and other adjustments.

• Support the AP process when AP Manager is out of the office

Grants, funding and compliance support

• Proactively support the Gants Management team including expense allocations and financial / compliance KPIs (burn rate, unspent balance, and similar).

• Lead in calculating GEA's direct and indirect rates based on audited financial statements.

• Assist MD Global Finance in preparing funding applications for prospective funders.

• Support implementation of financial controls to safeguard organizational assets and data integrity.

• Support other administrative and compliance efforts, including regulatory filings.

• Track grant budgets, expenditures and funding utilization, and analyze the financial implications of grant-funded programs, PIC and PRIs.

Revenue & Funding Forecasting

• Partner with Fundraising leadership to forecast contributed revenue, grants and other funding sources.

• Monitor actual revenue against forecast and identify changes in timing, probability or funding levels.

• Develop revenue scenarios based on donor commitments, grant pipelines and historical trends, and assess the impact of changes in funding on organizational liquidity and program plans.

• Provide leadership with early visibility into potential funding risks and opportunities.

State registrations and external compliance (Grant Thornton)

• Maintain a GEA Inc registration tracker (building on Grant Thornton's tracker) to hold key compliance data in one place, updated quarterly.

• Work with Grant Thornton to manage state registrations and annual renewals, ensuring annual reports and renewals are filed on time and coordinating internally so GT receives what it needs.

Audit readiness

• Support the work with auditors, external advisers, the US-based Director / Controller and MD Global Finance to prepare the annual and year-end audit process.

• Own the completeness and accuracy of assigned reconciliations.

• Maintain audit-ready records for 100% of assigned accounts, ensuring reconciliations and supporting files are complete, organized and saved in designated folders each month — including manual checks and accounts receivable for contributions, lapse, refunds and employee reimbursements.

• Submit all assigned annual audit requests, samples and supporting documents by the requested deadlines.

Systems, Reporting & Data

• Maintain and enhance financial models, reporting tools and planning templates, and develop standardized reporting and analytical tools for budget owners.

• Work with NetSuite, Salesforce and future budgeting systems to improve financial reporting and planning, ensuring consistency between accounting data, planning models and management reporting.

• Explore automation and business intelligence solutions to reduce manual processes and improve financial visibility.

• Assist with the preparation and review of financial policies and procedures.

Core responsibilities are outlined above; however, our team operates dynamically. You will have the opportunity to take on additional projects/tasks and adapt your duties to support overall company growth and priorities.

Qualifications & Experience

• CPA, CMA, MBA, CFA, or equivalent preferred.

• A bachelor's degree in accounting or a related field is required.

• At least 5 years of relevant work experience in FP&A related roles; 501(c)(3) / non-profit experience is required, specifically with fund accounting and contracts management.

• Demonstrated knowledge and deep understanding of US GAAP.

• Expert knowledge of Excel and MS Office, Salesforce, and NetSuite.

• Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Experience working within multi-functional, matrixed, multi-country teams.

• Experience operating with budgets across matrixed organizations and in a multi-stakeholder environment.

• Proven experience working effectively and autonomously as part of a team.

• Strong experience with budgeting, forecasting, financial modeling and variance analysis.

• Ability to explain financial information to non-financial colleagues, and to manage competing priorities and meet recurring monthly deadlines.

• Experience with multi-currency financial reporting or forecasting.

• Experience with systems such as Adaptive Planning, Planful, Anaplan or similar, and with Power BI, Power Query M codes, Power Pivot, DAX Measures and formulas, SOL, Tableau or other financial visualization tools.

Behavioral Competencies

• Financial Acumen: strong accounting and FP&A fundamentals, including financial modeling, forecasting, variance analysis, cash-flow analysis and reconciliation.

• Business Partnership: a consultative approach with strong stakeholder management and the ability to influence without authority, working comfortably with senior leaders and non-financial managers.

• Communication: Excellent interpersonal abilities, including strong listening, writing and verbal skills; demonstrates assertiveness and effective engagement with stakeholders.

• Startup Mindset and Agility: The ability and interest to pivot priorities as needed by the organization and finance team.

• Embrace New Challenges: A curious, perpetual learner who stays abreast of developments in the field.

• Relationship Building and Influence: Strong professional presence and experience working in an organization with multiple stakeholders.

• Decision-making: Ability to evaluate risks and opportunities, apply analytical and problem-solving skills, and take initiative to drive for results.

• Execution and Attention to Detail: Strong project-management skills and effective personal time management. Impeccable attention to detail

• Strategic Ability: Able to evaluate risks and opportunities using analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion: Committed to the mission of the Alliance and to inclusion, equity and diversity in every aspect of the work.

Compensation & Location
This is a full-time, exempt position with an annualized starting salary of $115,000–$130,000, commensurate with experience. GEAPP provides a comprehensive benefits package including a robust paid time off plan of 28 days of annual leave in addition to a company-wide end-of-year closure, a 401(k) retirement plan with a 10% employer contribution, $1,000 annually for work-from-home expenses, and $100 monthly for transit.

This position can be based wither in our DC or NYC office, however please note there is only one role available. GEAPP prides itself on being a flexible employer, and employees typically operate on a hybrid schedule that includes two days in the office per week.

The application deadline for this role is Friday, September 25th, applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

We operate from a strong commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion in everything we do. It is not only the right thing to do – we could not make an impact without our team members' diverse perspectives and experiences. We expect all Global Energy Alliance employees to contribute by developing their unique perspectives and talent, challenging conventional wisdom through evidence and reason, and amplifying marginalized voices.

Global Energy Alliance is committed to the principles of equal employment opportunity and compliance with all federal, state, and local laws concerning employment discrimination, including the Americans with Disabilities Act. To this end, the organization ensures equal opportunity to all employees and applicants regardless of race, color, age, gender, sexual orientation, religion, marital status, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, lawful alien status, physical, mental, and medical disability, veteran status, or liability for service in the United States Armed Forces.

Global Energy Alliance is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Part Time Floor Leader - The Streets at Southpoint
jobs.description:
Position: Part Time Floor Leader

Weekly: 20-29 hours

Interview Plan

Floor Leader

As a Floor Leader, you'll play a vital role in supporting the Store Management Team across all areas of the business. This includes everything from driving sales and opening/closing the store to analyzing sales results and leading training sessions. Together with your fellow leaders, you'll work to ensure that every aspect of the store is firing on all cylinders, creating an exceptional customer experience, a happy and motivated staff, and operational excellence that would make even the most detail-oriented among us proud.

Your day-to-day will be spent on the shop floor, where you'll lead and inspire a team of sales associates to achieve and surpass their goals. By fostering a culture of passion and positivity, you'll help create a work environment that's both productive and fun, resulting in happy customers and happy employees. The Floor Leader role is all about making the world a better place one soap at a time!

Responsibilities:

Sales & Customer Experience:

• Driving Sales: Utilize the StoreForce dashboard results to provide effective coaching and feedback to the sales team, and make necessary adjustments to the shop floor structure to meet and exceed sales goals. Take ownership for your results and actively work to grow the contribution of your segments to the store’s overall sales. Celebrate sales achievements with your team!

• Customer Experience: Lead by example in delivering a world-class customer experience on the shop floor, including product demonstrations. Observe and listen to consultations, collaborate with your team, and strive to exceed daily sales goals. By fostering a culture of excellence in customer service, you'll drive sales, create a loyal customer base, and build a positive reputation for your store.

• Building the Brand: Educate customers on Lush brand values, and articulate our position on Fighting Animal Testing, Freshest Cosmetics, Ethical Buying, 100% Vegetarian, Handmade, and Naked Packaging in the shop and through community engagement, hosting store parties, and other traffic-driving initiatives.

• Product Passion: increase the depth of your product knowledge through constant learning and consistently make informed product recommendations for every need.

Team Involvement:

• Development: Train and coach Sales Ambassadors and peers on effective sales techniques and product knowledge to improve their performance, support the growth of your team, and to increase sales. Lead by example, take ownership of your development, assess your performance, and actively seek feedback, resources, and opportunities to improve and elevate your skills, knowledge and abilities.

• Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging: Encourage open communication and actively listen to team members perspectives related to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging (DEIB). Foster a sense of belonging by promoting teamwork, encouraging collaboration, and recognizing and valuing each employee's unique contributions.

Operational Excellence:

• Cash Handling and Store Opening/Closing: Manage cash handling, including customer transactions, opening/closing the register, reconciling cash drawers, preparing nightly deposits, and securing the store at the end of each day. As required at your store location, take deposits to the bank.

• Time and Attendance: Lead by example in terms of attendance and punctuality, and encourage the same from all employees. Monitor employee breaks to ensure they are taking their scheduled breaks, promoting a healthy work environment and improving employee wellbeing. Review daily communications, including store updates and task lists, to ensure that team members are informed and prepared for their shifts, promoting a culture of preparedness and organization.

• Visuals and Merchandising: Maintain a clean, organized, and visually appealing store to enhance the customer's shopping experience and drive sales.

• Stock and Inventory: Train your team on inventory best practices and fresh standards, and support management with inventory tasks. Utilize Visual Merchandising guidelines to make real-time adjustments to product displays based on sales and improve the customer experience.

• Policies and Procedures: Support your management team to keep your store compliant and ensure your staff are practicing company standards for opening and closing, product integrity, respectful workplace, and health and safety.

Qualifications:

Required:

• Minimum 1 year of experience in:

• customer service and sales

• cash handling and opening/closing procedures

• supervisory experience involving coaching, feedback, and training

• problem-solving issues related to customer service in day-to-day operations

• a fast-paced team environment

• Knowledge and passion for skincare, natural beauty, and ethical business

• Flexible schedule to accommodate store needs, including evenings, weekends, and holidays

Preferred:

• Experience with consultation-based customer service models

• Experience analyzing sales metrics

• Experience working in skincare or cosmetics

• Experience in cross cultural collaboration and DEIB or social justice training

• Fluency in Spanish, French or other languages

Streets at Southpoint Pay

$16.50—$16.50 USD

Best of luck on your job search, and don't forget to follow us to learn more!

We Are Lush

YouTube
LinkedIn

Find our Personal Privacy Policy details here.

Lush Handmade Cosmetics participates in E-Verify in certain US states including AL, GA, NC, SC, FL, AZ, UT, TN and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the United States.

Lush Cosmetics North America respectfully recognizes that our business operates on Indigenous territory across Turtle Island. As a business headquartered in Canada, our largest facilities are located on the unceded territories of the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh, as well as here on the lands of the Mississaugas of the Credit, Anishnabeg, Chippewa, Haudenosaunee and Wendat, and now home to many diverse First Nations, Inuit and Métis peoples.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant
jobs.description:
Mission Lane is combining the power of data, technology, and exceptional service to pave a clear way forward for millions of people on the path to financial success. By attracting top talent and leveraging cutting-edge technology, we’re enabling people to unlock real financial progress. Sound like a mission you can get behind?

We're looking for an experienced Executive Assistant to support Mission Lane's executive team, reporting to the Chief Operating Officer with matrixed support to other senior executives.

The impact you'll make:

A Mission Lane cardholder is working toward something specific: paying down a balance, building a credit history strong enough to qualify for their first apartment, saving toward a goal they've been chasing for months. Their progress depends on Mission Lane's leadership making sound decisions, quarter after quarter, that take time and focus to get right. The Executive Assistant is vital to our customers’ progress by protecting, prioritizing, and organizing our leadership’s time.

Day-to-day as Executive Assistant, you will:

• Manage complex, frequently shifting calendars for multiple executives, resolving conflicts and anticipating scheduling needs before they surface.

• Coordinate logistics, agendas, and materials for Executive Committee meetings, Board meetings, leadership offsites, and town halls.

• Arrange detailed travel itineraries, including flights, lodging, and ground transportation, for executive trips.

• Draft, proofread, and format correspondence, presentations, and reports on behalf of the executives you support, exercising sound judgment with confidential information.

• Process and reconcile expense reports, invoices, and purchase requests in line with company policy.

• Serve as a primary point of contact between the executives you support and their leadership teams, other Executive Committee members, Board members, regulators, and external partners.

• Attend select leadership meetings, taking notes and tracking action items through to completion, and follow up with stakeholders to keep them on schedule.

• Partner with the Facilities & Events Manager to execute team offsites and department events, including budget and vendor coordination.

• Partner with the Executive Assistant supporting the CEO to align scheduling practices and provide backup coverage across the executive suite.

• Maintain a high level of confidentiality with sensitive information.

You'll thrive in this role if:

• You can look at a leader's day and know what needs their attention and what can wait, based on your understanding of the business.

• You've already built your own systems and approach for managing someone's calendar, inbox, and priorities, and you're ready to apply them here while being open to adjusting them as you learn how we work.

• You've worked inside a bank or another regulated environment, so confidentiality and process are already second nature.

Minimum qualifications:

• 5+ years of experience as an Executive Assistant supporting C-suite or senior executives, ideally within financial services or fintech.

• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex, competing calendars and to handle confidential and sensitive information with sound judgment and discretion.

• Advanced proficiency with Google Workspace and Mac, along with expense and travel management platforms.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to represent executives professionally with the Board, regulators, and external partners.

• Proven ability to build trusted working relationships with senior executives, Board members, and cross-functional stakeholders at all levels.

• High degree of professionalism, initiative, and adaptability in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

• Ability to travel 6+ times per year for high quality in person collaboration.

Preferred qualifications:

• Experience supporting executives within a regulated bank, credit union, or other depository institution.

• Familiarity with Board and Board Committee meeting logistics, materials preparation, and governance practices.

• Bachelor's degree.

Compensation:

Annual full-time starting base salary range: $87,000–$122,000.

This role is eligible for additional compensation in the forms of participation in our annual incentive and equity programs.

Pay is based on factors such as work experience, education, certification(s), training, skills, and competencies related to the role. Mission Lane also offers a comprehensive benefits plan, which includes paid time off, 401(k) match, a monthly wellness stipend, health/dental/vision insurance options, disability coverage, paid parental leave, flexible spending account (for childcare and healthcare), life insurance, and a remote-first work environment.

About Mission Lane:

Founded in December 2018, Mission Lane is a purpose-driven fintech company based in the U.S., with headquarters in Richmond, Virginia.

It all started with a realization:  nearly fifty percent of the adult population in the U.S. doesn’t have access to a clear line of credit. Most traditional credit card companies either overlook or overcharge this group because they have less-than-perfect credit scores or no scores at all. We decided this just wouldn’t do.

In partnership with our sponsor banks, we offer credit cards under the Mission Lane brand name, with better, clearer terms, and a more refined customer experience than the alternatives available to people working hard to improve their credit. To date, over four million consumers have chosen Mission Lane, earning high customer ratings on Credit Karma for its market segment and industry leading Net Promoter scores.

Mission Lane has cumulatively raised over $600 million of equity from leading investors, including Invus Opportunities, QED Investors, LL Funds, funds affiliated with Oaktree Capital Management, and other leading investors.

Our commitment to a workplace built on respect and dignity is guided by our core value of Unity. We believe that everyone plays a vital role in our shared purpose, and we actively cultivate an environment where all individuals have the opportunity to do their best work. By fostering a culture of empathy and collaboration, we create a strong sense of belonging and support for every team member.

Mission Lane is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or any other protected status.

Mission Lane provides reasonable accommodations to applicants who need them for medical or religious reasons, as required by law.  Applicants can initiate an accommodation request by contacting peopleexperience@missionlane.com.

Mission Lane is not sponsoring new applicant employment authorization and please, no third-party recruiters.

Application Integrity:

Our cardholders trust us with their financial well-being, and this trust starts with the integrity of the people on our team. We're looking for team members who share our dedication to transparency and truth. Please verify that the information in your application is accurate and complete.

Providing any information to Mission Lane that is not completely truthful at any point during the application or hiring process may result in removal from the hiring process, disqualification from future opportunities, withdrawal of an offer or other sanctions for candidates and, in addition for employees, disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Defensive Agent
jobs.description:
Get to Know Us

Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs. 

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

 

What You'll Do

We are hiring a Staff Software Engineer to lead the technical work for NodeZero's defensive agents: the systems that translate proven attack paths into continuous actionable remediation.



You'll set direction alongside our AI researchers, who define what the agents should reason about, and lead the engineers who build the platform underneath them. Over time this role owns the technical strategy for how autonomous remediation becomes a core NodeZero product capability rather than a set of recommendations in a report.



This is a technical leadership role without direct people management. You lead through architecture, code, design review, and mentorship, not through performance reviews and headcount. It is also not a pure architect role. You will write production code every week, review PRs from the engineers you lead, and partner closely with Product to sequence the right problems in the right order. You will be the person who both draws the system diagram on the whiteboard and commits the first slice of it to main.




RESPONSIBILITIES


LEADERSHIP & TEAM DEVELOPMENT

jobs.title: Assistant General Counsel, Employment (Senior Director)
jobs.description:
Reports to Equinox’s VP Legal Operations & Compliance  |  Hudson Yards, Manhattan, NY  |  Hybrid — 4 days/week in office; 1 day remote

Equinox isn't just a fitness company — it's shaping the future of wellness, longevity, hospitality, and media.  As Assistant General Counsel, Employment, you'll be the legal backbone protecting and empowering the people who make that happen — a workforce as varied as our brands spanning health club personnel, corporate teams, and media talent across the country, and in the UK and Canada.

We are seeking a business-minded, experienced, employment attorney to serve as a primary legal advisor on all workforce matters across a global portfolio that includes  Equinox Health Clubs, SoulCycle, Equinox Hotels, and Equinox Media. You’ll help build and modernize how Equinox manages employment risk across a fast-growing, multi-brand portfolio. No two days look the same.

Reporting to the VP Legal Operations & Compliance, you will primarily focus on ensuring that the company stays compliant with current and emerging state and federal employment laws.  You will also be a trusted and strategic partner to the Chief Legal Officer on high-stakes mediation, arbitration, and litigation, and to People & Culture, Risk Management, Asset Protection and senior leadership on various employment-related matters. This is a high-visibility, high-impact leadership role for someone who thrives in a fast-moving, people-first environment.

Who You'll Work With

You'll join a team of 16 people supporting the CLO's office, and will work closely with People & Culture, Risk Management and Asset Protection.

What You’ll Do

• Track and ensure compliance with evolving federal, state, and local employment law; translate developments into compliant policies, manuals, agreements, and SOPs.
• Identify and advise on legal risk across the employee lifecycle — hiring, performance, discipline, and terminations, and produce and report on employment risk metrics.
• Spot systemic risk trends and recommend proactive legal or policy changes on wage & hour, benefits, and leave-of-absence issues; partner with People & Culture to implement them.
• Partner with Employee Relations on allegations of harassment, hostile work environment, discrimination, and retaliation, as well as disability accommodations and leaves of absence.
• Draft agency (e.g., EEOC) position statements and respond to pre-mediation, pre-arbitration, and pre-litigation demand letters.
• Manage employment-related claims asserted under the company's ADR Program — and help shape how that program evolves.
• Lead an annual audit to ensure job descriptions, offer letters, employment agreements, restrictive covenant agreements, executive arrangements, and separation agreements stay legally current across all brands.
• Partner with People & Culture on building and delivering training for people managers (terminations, performance management, harassment prevention).
• Help leverage AI-assisted analysis, legal research, and drafting tools as part of a broader push toward more efficient legal operations.

• JD from an accredited law school; admitted to New York or at least one U.S. state bar.
• 10+ years of employment law experience, ideally including 3–5 years at an employment law firm and 2–3 years in-house at a large, multi-state employer.
• Deep knowledge of federal, state, and local employment law: wage & hour, discrimination, leave, accommodations, and workforce restructuring.
• Proven track record managing employment claims and EEOC/agency matters.
• Strong business instincts — you balance legal risk with operational reality and give actionable answers, not just issue-spotting.
• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; you make complex legal concepts accessible to non-lawyers and can influence at every level.
• Strong interpersonal skills, with experience advising senior executives and P&C leadership.
• Highly organized and detail-oriented, comfortable managing a busy, varied docket with competing priorities.
• Comfort using AI-assisted legal research and drafting tools (e.g., Claude or similar) as part of a modern legal practice.

Pay Transparency:  $245K – $260K + bonus

AS A MEMBER OF THE EQUINOX TEAM YOU WILL RECEIVE:

• We offer competitive salary, benefits, and industry leading commission opportunities for club employees
• Complimentary Club membership
• Perks and incentives with our products and services including Personal Training, Pilates, Spa and Shop

jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

1,000+ customers across 50+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $100M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI and Graceview.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

 - We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

 - We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

 - We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.




THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Marketing Manager or Senior Marketing Manager to join our NYC team and lead the execution of high-impact marketing programs across the US. This role will play a key part in driving brand awareness, pipeline growth, and customer loyalty through campaigns that leverage account-based marketing strategies, creative brand marketing, integrated cross-channel approaches, and content marketing.

You’ll report to the Marketing Director, US and collaborate closely with the global marketing team, including demand generation, product marketing, and brand. You’ll be embedded in the regional go-to-market and engagement teams to plan and execute programs that drive customer acquisition, engage target accounts, and nurture customer relationships. You will play a key role towards achieving new business pipeline, upsell pipeline and renewals targets across the US.

What You’ll Do

 - Build, manage and execute a pipeline of customer stories which translate Legora’s impact into compelling proof points, driving advocacy and loyalty.

 - Lead the conception and execution of integrated marketing campaigns, coordinating across an array of digital, social, content, and in-person channels to deliver cohesive go-to-market initiatives.

 - Partner with the US Growth team to align marketing initiatives with pipeline goals, account strategies, and customer acquisition priorities.

 - Develop content amplification strategies that extend the reach of Legora’s thought leadership, product stories, and customer narratives across relevant US channels.

 - Source and activate customer advocates, identifying US customers for case studies, co-marketing opportunities, testimonials, and speaking engagements.

 - Track performance of all regional marketing activities, analyzing results, reporting ROI, and using insights to refine and optimize future programs.

 - Generate creative concepts that elevate brand experience, enhancing engagement, differentiation, and the overall impact of Legora’s presence at every touchpoint.

What You Bring

What’s In It For You

 - Competitive package: Comprehensive salary, benefits, and tools for success.

jobs.title: Global Head of Legal
jobs.description:
About Blank Street

At Blank Street, we're on a mission to become the defining food and beverage brand of our generation. From the very beginning, we've set out to add a spark to ordinary experiences through elevated products, attention to detail, and a commitment to making every moment memorable. We're motivated by the millions of customers we serve across cities, and know that our potential is unlimited. It all starts with our people and their commitment to make magic happen each and every day. Like the sound of this? Keep reading

Add a Spark to the Ordinary…

Blank Street is seeking a smart, business-minded and technically excellent Global Head of Legal to join as our first legal hire and help build our legal function from the ground up. This role owns all legal matters, coordinating our network of external counsel, across our growing footprint — corporate governance, cap table management, fundraising workstreams, commercial contracts, employment law, real estate and store leases, litigation and disputes, intellectual property, and regulatory compliance — across the US and UK, and as we continue to expand into new states, and geographies.

As Blank Street scales, you'll be the primary legal partner to our executive team and every function across the business — Finance, People, Real Estate, Supply Chain, Digital and Operations — providing pragmatic, risk-aware counsel that moves fast without slowing the business down. You'll manage and help negotiate a high volume of commercial agreements (vendors, landlords, technology partners, marketing), manage our cap table, guide our investment processes, own our corporate governance and entity structure across jurisdictions, and be the first point of contact for employment matters, disputes, and regulatory inquiries.

Beyond day-to-day legal support, you'll help build the legal infrastructure Blank Street needs to scale responsibly: templated contracts and playbooks, a scalable approach to store lease review and new-market entry, and the judgment to know when to handle something in-house versus bring in outside counsel. This is a high-impact, high-ownership role for someone who takes pride in being both a trusted advisor and a hands-on operator — equal parts strategist and executor — and who wants to build a best-in-class legal function as we grow globally.

This is an in-person role based in our New York office, reporting to the Sr. Director of Global Finance, partnering closely with all department heads as well as outside counsel .

Who We’re Looking For

• JD from an accredited law school and active bar admission (US required)

• 5+ years of legal experience, ideally combining law firm training with public or in-house experience in a high-growth, high-paced, commercial environments.

• Broad generalist legal expertise across commercial contracts, corporate governance, employment law, and real estate, with the judgment to know when to escalate to specialized outside counsel.

• Experience supporting multi-jurisdiction operations (US multi-state, and/or UK or the EU) and new market entry.

• A builder's mindset — comfortable being the first legal hire, creating processes, templates, and playbooks from scratch, and flexing between high-level strategy and hands-on execution.

• Strong commercial instincts — able to balance legal risk with the speed and pragmatism a fast-growing business needs.

• Excellent communication skills, able to translate complex legal matters clearly for non-legal stakeholders, from store operators to executives.

• Ability to work independently, manage a high volume of competing priorities, and own outcomes end-to-end with minimal oversight.

• A team-first, discreet, and trustworthy approach to handling sensitive company, employee, and legal matters.

What You'll Own:

• Serve as Blank Street's in-house legal counsel, owning all legal matters across our US and UK footprint (and future international expansion), advising the executive team on legal risk and strategy.

• Draft, review, and negotiate a high volume of commercial agreements, including vendor, supplier, technology, marketing, and partnership contracts, balancing legal protection with commercial speed.

• Support real estate legal matters, alongside external counsel, including store lease review, negotiation, and renewals, partnering closely with the Real Estate and New Store & Facilities teams on new market and location openings.

• Lead employment law matters across jurisdictions, alongside external counsel, partnering with the People team on policies, disputes, terminations, and compliance with local labor and employment regulations.

• Own corporate governance and entity management across all Blank Street entities and jurisdictions, including resolutions, and equity/cap table matters in partnership with Finance.

• Manage litigation, disputes, and regulatory inquiries end-to-end, engaging and directing outside counsel where needed while retaining ownership of strategy and outcomes.

• Advise on intellectual property matters, including trademarks, brand protection, and licensing across markets.

• Partner with Product and Digital teams on legal considerations for the app, subscriptions, and e-commerce, including terms of service, privacy, and data protection compliance.

• Support new market entry and expansion, researching jurisdiction-specific legal and regulatory requirements alongside Finance and Tax.

• Develop and maintain a library of contract templates, playbooks, and legal policies to scale legal support efficiently as the company grows.

• Build and manage relationships with outside counsel across jurisdictions, owning budget, scope, and quality of external legal spend.

• Proactively identify legal and regulatory risk as Blank Street scales, and design practical mitigation strategies before issues arise.

• Take a major role in Blank Street’s financing processes, alongside external counsel, advising the execute team.

Benefits & Perks:

• $200,000-250,000 annual salary Blank Street, in good faith, believes that the posted salary range is accurate for this role in New York City at the time of posting. Our salary ranges are rooted in the desire to pay competitively relative to our organization size and industry, reflecting just one part of the total compensation package. Blank Street may pay more or less than the posted range based on factors such as relevant experience and skills, qualifications and location, among others. This range may be modified in the future.

• Equity package

• 15 days of paid annual leave (on top of company-observed holidays and sick time)

• Three health plan options, with full coverage available for two employee-only tiers

• Commuter benefits

• Parental leave

• Bereavement leave

• Exclusive access to our coveted Regulars program – yes, that means free coffee, matcha and more! ☕️

• Regular social outings with the team

• Free Blank Street swag

jobs.title: Trader Trainee (September 2027)
jobs.description:
At Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC), we're seeking ambitious, analytical, and curious graduates to join our Trader Trainee Program, a structured two-year development journey designed to prepare the next generation of commodity traders and commercial leaders. Program Start Date: September 1, 2027

This is more than an entry-level role. It's an opportunity to learn how global agricultural commodities move from farm to customer, gain hands-on exposure to international markets, and develop the commercial skills needed to succeed in a fast-paced trading environment.

What Makes Commodity Trading Different?

When people hear the word "trader," they often think of hedge funds, investment banks, or trading financial instruments from behind a screen.

That's not what this role is.

We are looking for individuals who are passionate about the business of moving and merchandising physical commodities. Success in this program comes from curiosity about supply chains, market fundamentals, customer relationships, and global trade. While futures and risk management are important components of the role, this is first and foremost a career path in physical commodity trading and merchandising, not a traditional financial markets trading role.

At LDC, you'll learn how commodities are sourced, transported, stored, marketed, and sold around the world. You'll gain exposure to supply and demand dynamics, logistics, risk management, customer relationships, and commercial strategy while helping move essential products through the global food and agriculture supply chain.

Whether it's understanding crop conditions, analyzing market trends, evaluating trade flows, or supporting commercial decisions, you'll develop the skills and business acumen needed to build a long-term career in commodity trading.

What You'll Experience

As a Trader Trainee, you'll participate in LDC's Global Commercial Graduate Program and gain exposure to multiple areas of the business through structured rotations, formal training, mentorship, and real-world commercial experience. The program is designed to develop market awareness, analytical rigor, commercial acumen, adaptability, and relationship-building skills required for success in commodity trading.

Throughout the program, you'll:

• Learn how physical agricultural commodities are traded in domestic and international markets.
• Develop an understanding of market fundamentals, pricing, risk management, and trade execution.
• Analyze supply and demand trends, market research, and commercial opportunities.
• Gain exposure to logistics, execution, research, operations, and commercial teams.
• Participate in formal development courses covering trading fundamentals, market analysis, risk management, execution, and business communications.
• Receive mentorship and coaching from experienced traders and commercial leaders.
• Build a global network through LDC's international commercial organization.
• Work on meaningful projects that contribute directly to commercial decision-making.

What You'll Learn

By the end of the program, you'll develop experience in:

• Understanding the physical flow of commodities through domestic and export markets.
• Identifying market trends and commercial opportunities.
• Negotiating and managing risk.
• Using market intelligence to support trading and merchandising decisions.
• Leveraging data and analytics to drive commercial insights.
• Understanding logistics, quality, customer needs, and supply chain economics.
• Building strong relationships across customers, suppliers, and internal stakeholders.

Why Join LDC?

For more than 170 years, LDC has connected farmers, markets, and consumers around the world. As part of our Trader Trainee Program, you'll gain exposure to global commodity markets, work alongside experienced commercial professionals, and participate in a structured development journey designed to accelerate your growth.

Through rotations, formal learning, mentorship, and hands-on commercial experience, you'll build the foundation for a successful career in commodity trading, merchandising, marketing, research, or other commercial leadership roles. Graduates who successfully complete the program may have the opportunity to transition into permanent commercial positions within the organization.

If you're ready to launch a career at the intersection of global markets, agriculture, analytics, and commercial strategy, we encourage you to apply and join the next generation of trading talent at LDC.

Who We're Looking For

We're hiring for potential, not prior trading experience.

You may be a great fit if you are:

• Graduating with a Bachelor's or Master's degree by Summer 2027, preferably in economics, finance or mathematics.
• Passionate about global trade, agriculture, economics, supply chains, or commodity markets.
• Excited by the idea of building a career in physical commodity trading and merchandising.
• Analytical and comfortable working with large amounts of data and information.
• A strong communicator who enjoys collaborating and building relationships.
• Curious, resilient, and motivated to continuously learn.
• Able to think critically, solve problems, and make informed decisions in dynamic environments.
• Must be open to relocate to either Memphis, TN or Wilton, CT.

Preferred Areas of Study

• Agricultural Economics
• Economics
• Finance
• Mathematics
• Business
• Supply Chain Management
• Data Analytics

Equivalent degrees and experiences will also be considered.

What We Offer

We provide a dynamic and stimulating international environment, which will stretch and develop your abilities and channel your skills and expertise with outstanding career development opportunities in one of the largest and most solid private companies in the world.

- Comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental and vision care coverage, flexible spending account plans, employee assistance program, life insurance and disability coverage

- 401k with Company Match

- Family Friendly Benefits including childbirth and parental leave, fertility and family building benefits

- Paid Time Off (PTO) and Paid Holidays

- Flexible work available (not applicable to all roles)

Diversity & Inclusion

LDC is driven by a set of shared values and high ethical standards, with diversity and inclusion being part of our DNA. LDC is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing a working environment that embraces and values diversity, equity and inclusion.

LDC encourages diversity, supports local communities and environmental initiatives. We encourage people of all backgrounds to apply.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

Sustainability

Sustainable value is at the heart of our purpose as a company.

We are passionate about creating fair and sustainable value, both for our business and for other value chain stakeholders: our people, our business partners, the communities we touch and the environment around us

jobs.title: Flagship Pioneering: AI Automation Engineering Co-Op
jobs.description:
This position is open exclusively to current Northeastern University Co-Op students.

Work Period: January 2027 to June 2027. This is a full - time, 40 hours per week position with 5 days in office.

About Flagship Pioneering

Flagship Pioneering is a biotechnology company that invents and builds platform companies that change the world. We bring together the greatest scientific minds with entrepreneurial company builders and assemble the capital to allow them to take courageous leaps. Those big leaps in human health and sustainability exponentially accelerate scientific progress in areas ranging from cancer detection and treatment to nature-positive agriculture.

What sets Flagship apart is our ability to advance biotechnology by uniting life science innovation, company creation, and capital investment under one roof in a way that is largely without precedent. Our scientific founders, entrepreneurial leaders, and professional capital managers are each aligned around an institutionalized process that enables us to innovate and transform for the benefit of people and planet.

Many of the companies Flagship has founded have addressed humanity’s most urgent challenges: vaccinating billions of people against COVID-19, curing intractable diseases, improving human health, preempting illness, and feeding the world by improving the resiliency and sustainability of agriculture.

Flagship has been recognized twice on FORTUNE’s “Change the World” list, an annual ranking of companies that have made a positive social and environmental impact through activities that are part of their core business strategies, and has been twice named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies.

Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program

Welcome to Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program for the cohort dreaming big and taking courageous leaps.You'll join fellow peers across our ecosystem of companies and learning firsthand how we build first-in-category companies. You’ll have access to enrichment sessions, a dedicated professional development track, and a mentor that help guide you toward your next step. By the end, you will carry on a meaningful project outcome, a genuine network, and a front-row view of how Flagship pioneer new ventures that change the world.

About the Team / Role

This is a hands-on building role. You will work closely with cross-functional stakeholders to design, prototype, and deploy AI-powered solutions that improve how teams work. Projects range from low-code automations using platforms like Zapier, Vercel, and Workato to full-stack applications built with tools like Claude Code and VS Code, written in Python or JavaScript, and deployed on cloud infrastructure like AWS.

You will take ownership of projects from start to finish: understanding a business process, exploring how to redesign it with AI, building a working solution, and iterating until it holds up in practice.

We’re looking for someone who is curious about not just how to build, but how to build well. That means learning to evaluate which tools and approaches fit a given problem, thinking through a design before jumping into code, and being open to feedback on your approach along the way.

Who This Is For

This role is for builders who are curious, resourceful, and eager to learn. You don’t need to know everything, but you should be excited to figure things out. You’re a strong fit if you:

• Have looked at a manual process and thought, “This wouldn’t exist like this if it were built today”

• Like to prototype quickly and learn by building

• Have hands-on experience building with AI tools, models, or APIs, even in personal or school projects

• Are starting to develop instincts for choosing the right tool for the job, not just using the one you know best

• Ask questions about why something is designed a certain way, not just how to make it work

• Care about whether something actually works reliably, not just in a demo

• Are energized by new technology and lean into learning it

• Can explain what you built and why to someone non-technical

Key Responsibilities

• Build and deploy automations using low-code platforms (e.g., Zapier, Workato) and, where needed, custom code (e.g., Python, JavaScript) to automate business workflows

• Integrate AI models via APIs into automation pipelines

• Help deploy and maintain applications on cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS)

• Learn to evaluate different tools and approaches for new projects, considering tradeoffs like speed, complexity, and long-term maintainability

• Test your own work thoroughly, with a focus on accuracy and edge cases, especially for data-sensitive workflows

• Iterate on proof-of-concept solutions based on real-world performance and feedback from business stakeholders

• Keep clear notes on how your solutions are built so others can understand, maintain, and extend them

• Support AI tool pilots and help create training materials that make it easier for non-technical users to adopt AI-enabled workflows

Basic Requirements

• Current graduate student in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field

• Proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, JavaScript)

• Basic understanding of APIs, webhooks, and how web services communicate

• Comfort working with AI tools in a development or productivity context

• Strong problem-solving skills and a willingness to learn new tools quickly

Preferred Requirements

• Experience with low-code or no-code automation platforms (e.g., Zapier, Make, Power Automate, Workato)

• Experience building and deploying applications on cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP)

• Familiarity with version control (Git) and development environments like VS Code

What We Offer

• Build alongside founders. You’ll work inside the same hypothesis-driven process Flagship uses to conceive and launch first-in-category companies.

• This can be the start of a longer story. Strong co-ops are considered for future opportunities across Flagship and its portfolio companies, not just for this one role.

• Work alongside people who left the safe path. Your colleagues are scientists, engineers, and operators who chose to build something new rather than join something already established.

• Take on real ownership. You're contributing to ventures that are still being defined. Your work can shape real decisions, not just support them.

• Be paid like the contributor you are. Compensation reflects the real work you take on.

Flagship Pioneering is committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status.

jobs.title: Studio Manager, Chestnut Hill
jobs.description:
SoulCycle is seeking a Studio Manager who will contribute to the company growth by expertly and efficiently managing their studio and leading their studio team. The ideal candidate will have a passion for the SoulCycle culture and brand. This person will be interpersonally savvy with a strong business acumen and have the ability to creatively problem solve and learn on the fly. This person embodies integrity, confidence, is a role model, is bold, is strategic, and is responsible for and the ultimate owner of the success and health of your business.

The responsibilities and duties of this position described here are representative of those an employee must perform. This is not a comprehensive list and other duties may be assigned.

INTERPERSONAL SAVVY

• Foster the SoulCycle Community and Culture in your studio
• Set the weather in your studio so your team loves to come to work
• Be a hospitality champion that provides exceptional hospitality to riders and staff, and inspires their team to uphold high hospitality standards and our core values
• Build and foster relationships in your studio, with your instructors and local community
• Acknowledge your teams wins and show gratitude

BUSINESS ACUMEN

• Develop holistic business plans that encompass ridership and retail goals
• Analyze and manage studio profit and loss statements
• Identify and execute opportunities with corporate partnerships and community impact

BUILDING EFFECTIVE TEAMS

• Coach your team on time management and prioritization of tasks/initiatives to ensure all deadlines are met

LEARNING ON THE FLY

• Be an expert on studio specific and company-wide operational procedures and policies
• Seamlessly transition yourself, team, and studio to new ways of working and processes
• Be open to, embrace and manage change within your studio and your team

CREATIVE PROBLEM SOLVING

• Confidently manage conflict in high pressure situations
• Demonstrate a solution oriented mindset and ability to execute within company standards in any situation

jobs.title: HRIS Analyst II - Workday
jobs.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The HRIS Analyst II reports directly to the HRIS Senior Manager and is important for optimizing and supporting Workday Benefits, Core HCM, HR reporting, and related areas. Primary responsibilities include system configuration, issue troubleshooting, data analysis, testing, production support, and creating mid-level reports. Working with senior HRIS analysts, the HR operations team, and partners, you will guide enhancements to provide HR technology solutions.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 2+ days/week.

Responsibilities:

• Be subject matter expert for the Workday Benefits module, with expertise extending to core HCM, Payroll, and/or Absence and Time Tracking.

• Lead the system configuration for Benefits Annual Enrollment.

• Be the primary contact for benefits-related vendor integrations and resolution of technical issues.

• Deliver technical and user support for Workday, handling questions, troubleshooting, and resolving issues across supported modules.

• Execute assigned production support tickets and project tasks with high accuracy and within target deadlines.

• Maintain HCM production support processes, encompassing monitoring, detailed analysis, and issue resolution.

• Define, refine, and maintain business process configurations.

• Configure, schedule, and oversee automated mass actions and system alert notifications.

• Participate in Workday's biannual feature update cycles.

• Collaborate with the Workday Security team to configure and maintain domain and business process security policies.

• Design and deploy Workday solutions tailored to meet functional requirements and improve operational efficiency.

• Test, and implement new feature enhancements, analyzing impacts across HCM, Benefits, Payroll, reporting, and integrations.

• Audit and validate system data and reports to preserve data integrity and maintain internal control standards.

• Review end-user data entry practices to identify process gaps and strengthen data governance controls.

• Provide HRIS system maintenance, solution implementations, and module troubleshooting.

• Partner with senior HRIS analysts to achieve shared goals, exchange technical knowledge, and foster skill growth.

• Engage with HR partners to lead new module functionality, enhancements, and broader HCM programs.

• Communicate technical insights, analytical findings to non-technical partners.

• Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

• You will report to the HRIS Senior Manager.

Basic Qualifications:

• Minimum 2 years of experience in an HRIS Analyst role or comparable HR systems position.

• Minimum 2 years of hands-on experience using Workday.

• Professional experience in HR, Payroll, and Benefits operations.

• Experience with Workday report writing and generation.

• Background in maintaining Workday business processes, security protocols, system releases, notifications, and automated mass operations.

• Advanced proficiency in Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel, including complex formulas, pivot tables, macros, modeling.

• Exceptional problem-solving, analytical, collaboration.

• Experience conveying complex technical concepts and data findings into clear, accessible recommendations for non-technical partners.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Hands-on experience managing Workday benefits, Workday Time Tracking and Absence modules.
