jobs.title: Staff Electrical Operator
jobs.description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE DATA CENTER OPERATIONS TEAM

The Data Center Operations team keeps live, mission-critical facilities running while the buildings around them are still being built.

Examples of key problems the team is working on:

 - Operate 480V to 15kV+ electrical distribution, generators, switchgear, and UPS systems in facilities running live AI training workloads where downtime is not an option.

 - Run safe switching, lockout/tagout, and energization procedures in buildings where construction, commissioning, and production operations overlap on the same electrical systems.

 - Build the operating procedures, emergency response playbooks, and operator training programs for facilities that are scaling faster than any standard runbook covers.

 - Drive incident response and root-cause analysis on electrical events so the same failure never takes capacity offline twice.


ROLE SCOPE

 - Own day-to-day operation and troubleshooting of medium and high-voltage electrical distribution, including switchgear, generators, UPS systems, and associated protection and controls, in live data center environments.

 - Run switching operations, lockout/tagout, and energization work to NFPA 70E and arc flash standards, with documentation rigorous enough to stand up to a safety audit.

 - Lead electrical incident response on shift and on call, isolating faults, restoring power, and producing root-cause reports that change how the facility is operated.

 - Build and maintain SOPs, MOPs, and EOPs for electrical systems, and keep them accurate as new capacity comes online.

 - Drive alarm monitoring and response through BMS and EPMS platforms, tuning thresholds and escalation paths so real problems surface before they become outages.

 - Train and mentor junior operators to the point where they can run switching and response procedures without you in the room.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would. https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c

 - You've spent years operating and troubleshooting 480V to 15kV+ electrical distribution equipment hands-on in live hyperscale or large colocation data centers.

 - You have deep working experience with generators, medium-voltage switchgear, UPS systems, and the BMS/EPMS platforms that monitor them.

 - You know NFPA 70E, arc flash boundaries, and lockout/tagout procedures well enough to write them, enforce them, and catch a shortcut before it becomes an incident.

 - You have a track record of shift-based or on-call critical facility operations, and you've been the person who restores power at 3am.

 - You operate independently. Given a new facility with incomplete documentation, you build the procedures rather than wait for them.

 - You've trained junior operators and can raise a team's standard, not just your own output.

 - You're comfortable running live operations inside an active build environment where construction and commissioning share the floor with production load.

 - Bonus: NETA certification, journeyman or master electrician license, or commissioning experience on greenfield data center electrical systems.



We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.



You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application--  someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

jobs.title: Senior Talent Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are

We are creators who live to be original.

For the past two decades, we’ve been building a playground for creating original work. A place where a diverse collective of artists, thinkers and makers can express themselves, be bold, and experiment freely. A place where brands come to be authentic, challenge conformity and stand out from the crowd.

What We're Looking for

Brand New School is seeking a Senior Talent Manager to lead our talent department across our LA and NY studios.

This is a senior-level role for an experienced talent professional with 5+ years of experience in creative talent management and staffing. The ideal candidate has a strong network of freelance artists and a deep understanding of the creative industry, from design and animation to VFX, CG, illustration, and emerging creative disciplines.

The Senior Talent Manager will be responsible for ensuring BNS has the right talent, in the right place, at the right time. This includes managing our internal artist roster, sourcing and booking freelance talent, building and maintaining relationships with artists and representatives, negotiating rates and availability, and partnering closely with Producers, Executive Producers, and Heads of Production to staff projects effectively.

Responsibilities

Talent Strategy & Department Leadership

• Manage, mentor, and develop internal Talent team members, providing direction, feedback, and support.

• Establish and maintain efficient talent management processes, systems, and best practices.

• Proactively anticipate staffing needs based on upcoming projects, studio bandwidth, and evolving creative capabilities.

• Partner with leadership to identify gaps in our internal roster and develop strategies to address them.

Freelance Talent Management

• Maintain and actively grow a strong network of freelance artists, including designers, art directors, animators, CG artists, VFX artists, illustrators, editors, and other creative specialists.

• Source, vet, and recommend freelance talent based on project needs, creative fit, availability, budget, and experience level.

• Negotiate rates, schedules, terms, and availability with freelance artists and representatives. As well as maintain an organized and up-to-date talent database and roster.

• Stay current on emerging talent, new creative disciplines, and industry trends.

Staffing & Resource Management

• Oversee scheduling and allocation of internal staff and freelance talent across projects in LA, UK, and NY.

• Partner closely with Producers, Executive Producers, Heads of Production, Creative Directors, and Directors to determine staffing needs.

• Make thoughtful staffing recommendations that maximize creative quality, efficiency, and artist fit while minimizing burnout.

Qualifications

• 5+ years of experience in talent management, creative staffing, or a related role within the creative industry.

• Proven experience leading a talent, staffing, or recruiting function or team.

• Extensive network of freelance creative talent with established relationships across multiple disciplines.

• Strong understanding of the design, animation, VFX, CG, and broader creative production landscape.

• Demonstrated experience booking freelance talent and negotiating rates, availability, and terms.

• Excellent interpersonal and relationship-building skills with the ability to work effectively with artists, producers, directors, representatives, and leadership.

• Highly organized with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

• Proactive, resourceful, and comfortable operating independently in a fast-paced creative environment.

• Comfortable working across our LA and NY studios and within a hybrid work environment.

• Bachelor's degree preferred, but not required.

Benefits

• Competitive salary

• Health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance

• One Medical account

• Company sponsored continued education

• Peer bonus system

• Generous PTO / sick leave

• Company administered 401(k) plan with matching

• Dog friendly work environment 🐶

jobs.title: Principal Water Resources Engineer
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a Principal Water Resources Engineer located in Portland or Seattle to lead high-quality project delivery and support the continued growth of our Pacific Northwest water resources

practice. This Principal will work closely with the existing management team and technical staff in

Portland, Seattle and Northern California to enhance ongoing project and client management, as well as develop a regional strategic growth plan. This role focuses on stream and river restoration, fish passage design, floodplain management, coastal resiliency and stormwater management, while combining technical leadership, project management, and practice growth responsibilities. The successful candidate

will bring deep water resources expertise, strong client relationships, and a proven ability to develop

opportunities, lead pursuits, and grow a project portfolio across Oregon, Washington, and the broader Pacific Northwest.

As a senior member of the team, they will provide technical leadership and mentorship,

help solve complex business and engineering challenges, and play a key role in expanding AECOM's regional presence while leveraging the resources, technical depth, and global reach of one of the world's leading infrastructure consulting firms. This opportunity is ideally suited for a seller-doer who wants to help build a leading Pacific Northwest water resources practice while leveraging the technical depth, brand recognition, and resources of AECOM's global water business.

Responsibilities may include:

• Proven experience in water resources engineering (e,g, restoration, hydrology/hydraulics, dams, levees, stormwater, flood control, drainage, culverts, bridges, bank stabilization) from planning to modeling to detailed design and construction supervision. The ideal candidate will have the technical credibility to lead complex water resources projects and the market presence to help win similar work.
• Identifies new business opportunities for AECOM, coordinates and participates in project presentations to clients and other external groups, and promotes AECOM’s capabilities, marketing its services among existing and prospective clients. A key expectation of this role is active business development, including maintaining and expanding relationships with public- sector, transportation, municipal, environmental, and infrastructure clients in the Pacific Northwest.
• Participates in project opportunity evaluation, consultant selection, and the preparation of AECOM's qualification/experience statements. This includes helping identify the right opportunities for AECOM, shaping capture strategies, contributing to go/no-go decisions, and developing winning proposal approaches.
• Coordinates and participates in contract negotiations with clients and subcontractors and drafts complex professional service agreements and addenda for review by senior management. The candidate should be comfortable moving projects from early client conversations through scope development, contracting, delivery, and follow-on work.
• Directs project team and client compliance with contract terms and monitors subcontractors' compliance with contractual commitments.
• Prepares project work plan, scope, schedule, and budget, and communicates these to project team members; monitors/manages project production for compliance with schedule, budget, and quality objectives. The role requires strong project management discipline, including proactive communication with clients, technical staff, teaming partners, and AECOM leadership.
• May supervise technical professionals, associate project managers, and design staff including workload and staffing management. The candidate will also help mentor and grow staff in the Pacific Northwest, with support from AECOM’s broader regional and national water resources teams.
• Monitors and reports financial status of projects to technical managers.
• Performs such other duties as the supervisor may from time to time deem necessary.

Minimum Requirements

• Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering and 10+ years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
• Professional Engineer in Oregon and/or Washington (or ability to obtain PE license within 6 months of hire)

Preferred Qualifications

• 20+ years of relevant Water Resources experience and 10+ years of Project Management experience
• Strong relations and work history with clients in the Pacific Northwest and ability to leverage existing relationships to grow the business.
• Demonstrated “seller-doer” experience, including both successful project delivery and measurable contributions to client development, proposal wins, revenue growth, or strategic market positioning.
• Experience building or strengthening a regional practice, service line, client account, or technical team.
• Ability to work collaboratively with AECOM’s national and global technical experts while developing a stronger local water resources presence in the Pacific Northwest.
• Experience in preparing site civil design plans and grading. Experience in construction management or engineering support during construction.
• Demonstrated proficiency in AutoCAD/Civil 3D, Microstation, ArcGIS.
• Experience with hydrologic, hydraulic, and geomorphic concepts, principles, and models (e.g., SRH-2D/SMS, HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, HydroCAD, SWMM).
• Experience and familiarity with geomorphic field data collection techniques including pebble counts, channel and floodplain morphology measurements, and stream stability assessment.
• Understanding of federal, state and local regulatory and permitting processes for water resources engineering projects.
• Demonstrated experience in floodplain modeling/mapping and knowledge of FEMA requirements.
• Experience with hydrology and hydraulics associated with dams, reservoirs, levees (e.g., precipitation frequency analysis, dam breach inundation analysis, spillway capacity analysis/design).
• An MS or PhD in a relevant subject.
• Membership in an appropriate professional organization (River Restoration Northwest, Northwest Regional Floodplain Management Association (NORFMA), etc).
• Certified in WSDOT Fish Passage and Stream Restoration Training.
• Certified Floodplain Manager (CFM)
• Coding experience (e.g. Python) and experience in using/developing digital tools for hydrology and hydraulics.

• Sponsorship is not available for this position
• Relocation is not available for this position

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

En Soho House, un cocinero de línea III  es responsable de contribuir al servicio y apoyar a una sección específica, preparar alimentos y salsas a la perfección y ayudar a los chefs sénior cuando sea necesario. Un cocinero de línea III exitoso es un socio fundamental del equipo debido a sus habilidades culinarias específicas y apreciadas en una o más estaciones. Aunque no es experto en todas las estaciones, un cocinero de línea III está hiperespecializado y tiene una capacidad demostrada para ejecutar correctamente todos los platos del menú, desde la preparación hasta el emplatado, y ofrecer platos de la máxima calidad desde dos o más estaciones.

• Responsable de aprender todos los platos del menú y de ser capaz de producir platos consistentes y de calidad en entornos dinámicos y exigentes en una o más estaciones.

The CNC Machinist is responsible for producing machined parts by programming, setting up, and operating a computer numerical control (CNC) machine, maintaining quality and safety standards, keeping records, and maintaining equipment and supplies.

Shift: Monday - Thursday 3pm - 1am

$$ This position is eligible for a $1,500 sign on bonus.  $750 at 90 days and remainder paid out at completion of 180 days.  $$

Essential Functions/Responsibilities

• Adhere to production schedules by studying work orders, blueprints, engineering plans, material specifications, and machining parameters, and interpret complex geometric dimensions and tolerances (GD&T).
• Program, set up, and operate CNC machines by entering instructions, setting tool registers, offsets, compensation, and conditional switches using G-code and/or conversational programming, with minimal assistance.
• Load raw material safely and verify setup by measuring positions and first-run parts to ensure compliance with international standards.
• Monitor part specifications during drilling, grooving, cutting, turning, and facing operations. Identify malfunctions, apply troubleshooting techniques, and make corrective adjustments to programs or replace worn tools as needed.

Education/Experience

• Associate degree in Machining Technology or related field plus three (3) years of CNC machining experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
• Experience with FANUC controls, Haas mill/lathe machining, and CMM (coordinate-measuring machine) preferred.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

• Technical Skills. Proficiency in CNC programming (G-code and conversational), blueprint interpretation, and GD&T. Strong mechanical aptitude with ability to use dimensional measuring tools, perform geometric calculations, and troubleshoot machine malfunctions.
• Computer Skills. Proficient with CNC machining software, arc/radius programming, and tool compensation techniques.
• Communication. Ability to communicate effectively in English verbally and in writing.

Physical/Sensory Requirements

Ability to stand for extended periods, lift up to 75 pounds occasionally and 25 pounds frequently, and perform fine motor tasks. Must have close vision, color vision, and depth perception. PPE required.

Working Environment

Manufacturing environment with exposure to ambient and controlled temperatures, light to moderate airborne graphite dust, and moderate background noise.

jobs.title: Demand Generation & Field Marketing Specialist
jobs.description:
About StackOne

StackOne is the integration infrastructure for AI agents. Backed by GV and Workday Ventures ($24M raised), we make it possible for any AI agent — whether our customers build it into their product or buy it off the shelf — to take real action across the enterprise stack. Our platform gives agents 430+ connectors and 26,000+ pre-built actions, an AI connector builder for everything not covered yet, and the production layer agents actually need: semantic tool discovery that cuts token use by up to 80%, managed authentication and per-action permissions, the most accurate prompt injection defense on the market, and end-to-end observability.

Join us on our fast trajectory to build the future of agentic integrations.

Role 

Own demand generation at StackOne — the marketing function that sits closest to the actual sales motion. Your job is to turn our growing top-of-funnel signal — event engagement, LinkedIn activity, outbound outreach — into a qualified pipeline within the accounts and segments that matter most. You'll work directly alongside our Founding Growth (Marketing) and partner closely with sales, scaling channels that are already producing results. 

Full ownership of demand generation across outbound and events, working hand-in-hand with marketing and sales on target-account strategy. We want someone who thinks critically about the audience in the room and turns passive attention into real conversations. Early motion, real traction, plenty of room to shape how this function grows.



What You’ll Be Doing  

 - Own our outbound demand gen channel end-to-end (targeting, sequencing, experimentation) and scale it past its early wins.

 - Own demand generation around events end-to-end. That includes booth messaging, on-site content, side events, and the follow-up that turns attendee engagement into a qualified pipeline. 

*Vendor logistics, booth build, and on-site setup sit with a dedicated events manager, so you can focus on the audience and the narrative, not the delivery.

 - Partner with the Founding Growth (Marketing) to shape event and channel strategy, then run with it independently once it's agreed.

 - Build lightweight ABM-style campaigns for key accounts and segments, and adapt broader company campaigns to fit a specific account or customer segment.

 - Run experiments across channels to find what actually converts, and double down on what works.

 - Turn early signal, like event attendees, LinkedIn engagement, outbound replies into marketing-qualified leads and pipeline.

 - Track and report on sourced/influenced pipeline, event ROI, and channel performance — the metrics that matter here are pipeline and revenue impact.

 - Work closely with sales on how qualified leads hand off into the pipeline.

Qualifications

 - 3+ years of demand generation experience with a track record of driving measurable results at a previous company.

 - Experience turning early-stage signals (events, social engagement, outbound) into qualified pipeline.

 - Comfortable owning outbound campaigns and event-driven demand gen end-to-end, from strategy input to execution.

 - Startup experience, or genuine comfort with startup pace — later-stage startup or more structured B2B/enterprise backgrounds are also a strong fit.

 - High ownership mindset, bias for action, and comfort operating in ambiguity.

Nice to have: field marketing or ABM experience (running events/campaigns tied to specific accounts or territories), early SDR/sales-development experience that transitioned into marketing, community or partnerships experience, an existing personal network or presence on LinkedIn, B2B/enterprise exposure.

Dealbreaker: no demand-generation experience, or a background only in large-company marketing.



Benefits

 - Join one of the best-funded, fastest-growing startups in the AI infrastructure ecosystem.

 - Work alongside an experienced team, with backgrounds from Google, Microsoft, Oracle, Coinbase, JP Morgan, and more.

 - Meaningful share options — share in the company's success as we grow.

 - 25 days PTO + 1 additional day per year of tenure.

 - Health insurance.

 - 401(k).

 - Remote-first, with regular in-person time in the Bay Area.

 - $1,000 for your home office setup + $500/year top-up.

 - Annual team offsites to sunny spots (last ones were in Croatia and Portugal ☀️)

We deliver scientific breakthroughs by identifying critical gaps in care and develop differentiated products with a focus on novel mechanisms of action that enable meaningful advancements in patient outcomes. Our industry-leading neuroscience portfolio includes FDA-approved treatments for major depressive disorder, agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease, excessive daytime sleepiness associated with narcolepsy and obstructive sleep apnea, and migraine, as well as multiple novel product candidates addressing a broad range of serious neurological and psychiatric conditions that impact over 150 million people in the United States. Together, we are on a mission to solve some of the brain’s biggest problems so patients and their loved ones can flourish. For more information, please visit us at www.axsome.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Axsome Therapeutics is seeking a Specialty Account Manager (SAM) to execute commercial activities for assigned geographies, establish relationships with customers, and ensure successful promotion of AUVELITY for major depressive disorder in adults and potential future indications. This role is field-based and will require gaining access to customers in a clinic or hospital setting while also maximizing the ability to engage through digital channels.

Qualifications / Requirements

• Minimum of 5 years of field customer experience and/or account management. Minimum of 3 years Healthcare Professional experience with relevant CNS experience will also meet the qualifications for this role

• 5 years of consistent top performance in the pharmaceutical, biotech or medical sales space

• Psychiatry/CNS experience strongly preferred

• Launch experience strongly preferred

Ámbito del puesto

En Soho House, un cocinero de línea II  es responsable de mantener una o dos estaciones, preparar alimentos y salsas a la perfección y ayudar a los chefs senior con el servicio. Como cocinero de línea II, te desenvuelves bien en entornos dinámicos e influyes positivamente en el equipo al demostrar habilidades altamente especializadas en dos estaciones y mantener la calma durante un servicio ajetreado.

Un cocinero de línea II exitoso es un socio fundamental del equipo debido a sus habilidades culinarias específicas y apreciadas en dos o más estaciones. Aunque no es experto en todas las estaciones, un cocinero de línea II está altamente especializado y tiene una capacidad demostrada para ejecutar correctamente todos los platos del menú, desde la preparación hasta el emplatado, y ofrecer platos de la máxima calidad desde dos o más estaciones.

Responsabilidades clave

• Responsable de aprender los ingredientes de todos los platos del menú y capaz de producir platos consistentes y de calidad en entornos dinámicos y exigentes y en dos puestos.

• Apoyo diario en la preparación, así como en el mantenimiento de la cocina, el equipo y el inventario cuando sea necesario.

• Las responsabilidades diarias también incluyen la preparación de alimentos en la despensa, la estación de frituras y otras áreas de la cocina, respetando las solicitudes de alergias y las modificaciones específicas de los platos.

• Prepara todos los alimentos según las instrucciones, de forma higiénica y puntual. Además, es capaz de cumplir con los procedimientos de seguridad, higiene y manipulación de alimentos.

• Sigue las recetas, los controles de porciones y las especificaciones de presentación establecidas por la cocina, prestando atención a las temperaturas de cocción y la calidad para reducir los costes adicionales.

• Ayudar con el inventario para que la cocina funcione con un coste sostenible de los alimentos.

• Prepara las estaciones de acuerdo con las directrices de la cocina y mantiene un área de trabajo segura, limpia, organizada y bien abastecida.

• Producción y ejecución de platos a la carta. Incluidas ideas para banquetes de fin de semana y comidas de equipo.

• Trabajar para alcanzar objetivos específicos y los estándares de Soho House en cuanto a la rapidez del servicio y la coherencia de la experiencia para los estándares de servicio de Soho House.

• Asegurarse de que se sigue el procedimiento adecuado de control de horarios y asistencia al fichar la entrada y la salida de los turnos y los descansos.

• Apoyar al segundo chef ejecutivo y al segundo chef junior en las reuniones previas y posteriores al servicio cuando se solicite.

• Influir positivamente en los equipos bajo presión y proporcionar un ambiente de trabajo acogedor que aumente la moral del personal.

• Asistir a las formaciones de «Cook House» y apoyar la tutoría y la formación de los integrantes nuevos y existentes del equipo en las áreas que desean desarrollar.

• Ayudar con la limpieza, el saneamiento y la organización de la cocina, las cámaras frigoríficas y todas las áreas de almacenamiento.

• Comprometerse a proporcionar un servicio de calidad y conocimientos sobre alimentos.

• Realizar todas las demás tareas que le asigne el supervisor o el Gerente.

Experiencia requerida

• Mínimo de 2 años de experiencia en un entorno profesional dinámico, sofisticado y accesible.

• Sólidos conocimientos de cocina profesional, incluyendo habilidades en el manejo de cuchillos.

• Certificado de manipulador de alimentos.

• Gran capacidad de comunicación, capacidad para seguir instrucciones y mentalidad de trabajo en equipo.

• Capacidad proactiva para establecer relaciones profesionales con todos los líderes y el equipo de cocina.

• Horario flexible y capacidad para trabajar por la mañana, por la noche, los fines de semana y los días festivos (según sea necesario).

• Capacidad demostrada para ejecutar todos los platos del menú y preparar y servir adecuadamente platos de la máxima calidad en todas las estaciones.

Requisitos físicos

• Debe ser capaz de agarrar, sujetar, girar y sostener objetos con las manos.

• Debe ser capaz de trabajar de pie durante al menos 8-10 horas.

• Se requieren movimientos rápidos para desplazarse de una parte a otra de la cocina y las zonas de almacenamiento.

• Debe ser capaz de mover, tirar, transportar o levantar hasta 50 libras ocasionalmente y 35 libras regularmente.

• Exposición ocasional al frío, al calor y al agua.

• Ocasionalmente, arrodillarse, agacharse, ponerse en cuclillas y trepar según sea necesario.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Bioanalytical
jobs.description:
Join our team in a dynamic hybrid role, offering flexibility to work remotely or from our headquarters in Watertown, MA.

COMPANY OVERVIEW:

Disc Medicine is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company committed to discovering, developing, and commercializing novel treatments for patients who suffer from serious hematologic diseases. We are building a portfolio of innovative, first-in-class therapeutic candidates that aim to address a wide spectrum of hematologic diseases by targeting fundamental biological pathways of red blood cell biology, specifically heme biosynthesis and iron homeostasis. Disc Medicine values collaboration, professional development, and scientific integrity and promotes an inclusive company culture that empowers and inspires.

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Associate Director/Director, Bioanalytical will provide technical and operational support for bioanalytical activities supporting DISC Medicine’s drug development programs. This role will independently oversee outsourced bioanalytical studies conducted in GLP/GCP and non-GLP environments and support a broad range of drug modalities.

The successful candidate should have extensive expertise in regulated bioanalysis, demonstrated industry experience supporting both pre-clinical and clinical development, and a strong understanding of regulatory expectations for bioanalytical sciences. This individual will work cross-functionally with discovery, nonclinical, clinical, DMPK, and external CRO partners to ensure high-quality bioanalytical support, including PK, anti-drug antibody (ADA), and biomarker analyses, across different programs.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Lead technical and operational bioanalytical activities, including assay development, validation, sample analysis, data review and reporting, regulatory document authoring, and regulatory interactions, supporting drug candidates ranging from small molecules to biologics. This includes bioanalytical assays for PK, biomarkers, and ADA across preclinical and clinical programs.

• Serve as the bioanalytical project lead and strategic partner to internal cross-functional teams to identify and address bioanalytical needs for assigned development programs.

• Collaborate closely with CROs and external laboratories to develop and execute bioanalytical strategies, including method development, validation, sample analysis, troubleshooting, and issue resolution.

• Oversee bioanalytical timelines, data quality, resource planning, and vendor deliverables to ensure alignment with program objectives and regulatory requirements.

• Serve as the Subject Matter Expert (SME) for bioanalytical sciences within DISC Medicine.

• Contribute to regulatory submissions and interactions, including preparation and review of bioanalytical sections of regulatory documents and responses to regulatory inquiries.

REQUIREMENTS:

• Ph.D. in a relevant scientific discipline with 8+ years of industry experience in bioanalysis. Level will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.

• Hands-on experience supporting GLP toxicology and clinical studies, with strong familiarity with applicable bioanalytical regulatory guidance and industry best practices.

• Demonstrated expertise in bioanalytical assay development and validation, including LC-MS/MS, ligand-binding assays, and cell-based assays, supporting both small molecules and biologics.

• Practical, hands-on experience with cell-based assays, including flow cytometry and cell-based neutralizing antibody (NAb) assays, is preferred.

• Experience with biomarker and/or pharmacodynamic (PD) marker bioanalysis is highly desirable.

• Broad understanding of drug discovery and development, including DMPK/ADME principles and the role of bioanalysis in supporting preclinical and clinical development.

• Proven experience managing CROs and external vendors, including oversight of timelines, quality, budgets, and deliverables, with a willingness to remain hands-on in technical execution and problem solving.

• Excellent interpersonal, communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate complex scientific concepts to both technical and cross-functional audiences.

The annual base salary range for this position is listed below. Actual pay rates are determined by considering multiple factors including qualifications, relevance of experience, education & credentials, subject matter expertise, and internal parity.

$187,000—$228,000 USD

jobs.description:
About AlphaSense:

The world’s most sophisticated companies rely on AlphaSense to remove uncertainty from decision-making. With market intelligence and search built on proven AI, AlphaSense delivers insights that matter from content you can trust. Our universe of public and private content includes equity research, company filings, event transcripts, expert calls, news, trade journals, and clients’ own research content.

Founded in 2011, AlphaSense is headquartered in New York City with more than 2,000 employees across the globe and offices in the U.S., U.K., Finland, India, Singapore, Canada, and Ireland. Come join us!

About the Role:

We're seeking a Customer Success Platform Content Implementation Manager to own the build, quality, and ongoing maintenance of our Gainsight content— including playbooks, health rules, and human handoff alerting logic. This role sits at the intersection of customer marketing and RevOps, translating lifecycle strategy into scalable, reliably-functioning CSP content. You'll be the Customer Marketing content builder in Gainsight, ensuring every playbook is built to specification, monitoring and reporting on their success to lifecycle managers and CS counterparts.

Who You Are:

• 5+ years of hands-on experience building and maintaining playbooks, rules, and workflows in Gainsight CSP (required)

• Demonstrated experience designing alerting or handoff logic between marketing/lifecycle systems and human teams (CS, Sales, RevOps)

• Strong systems-thinking mindset with a track record of building for scale — able to anticipate where logic will break as volume, segments, or use cases multiply

• Experience partnering closely with RevOps or CS Ops on shared data models, CRM integrations, and cross-system dependencies

• Rigorous approach to QA and documentation; comfortable establishing process and standards where none exist

• Familiarity with customer health scoring, lifecycle segmentation, or adoption frameworks strongly preferred

• Analytical mindset with the ability to troubleshoot logic issues independently and communicate root cause clearly to non-technical stakeholders

• Excellent cross-functional communication and project management skills; able to manage multiple concurrent build requests and competing priorities

• B2B SaaS experience preferred; customer marketing, customer success, or RevOps background all relevant

What You’ll Do:

• Own end-to-end build of Gainsight CSP playbooks — from requirements gathering with lifecycle marketing, CS, and RevOps stakeholders through configuration, testing, and launch

• Design and maintain human handoff alerting logic in partnership with RevOps, ensuring the right signals route to the right owners at the right time with minimal false positives or missed triggers

• Establish and enforce build quality standards (naming conventions, documentation, QA/testing protocols, version control) so playbooks scale cleanly as new use cases and teams are added

• Monitor and report on live playbooks and alerts on an ongoing basis, proactively identifying and resolving breakage, logic drift, or data issues before they impact customers

• Partner with Lifecycle lead and RevOps on data architecture and system dependencies (CRM, health score inputs, product usage data) that feed CSP logic, flagging upstream issues that affect playbook accuracy

• Build and maintain internal documentation of playbook logic, ownership, and change history to support auditability and smooth handoffs as the team scales

• Continuously evaluate the playbook portfolio for redundancy, performance, and opportunities for consolidation or optimization as lifecycle and adoption strategy evolves

• Serve as Customer Marketing Gainsight subject matter expert, advising lifecycle marketing and CS stakeholders on capabilities and constraints when building new initiatives

jobs.title: Tax Strategy & Incentives Manager
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

Vultr is on a mission to make high-performance cloud infrastructure easy to use, affordable, and locally accessible for enterprises and AI innovators around the world. With 33 global cloud data center locations, Vultr is trusted by hundreds of thousands of active customers across 185 countries for its flexible, scalable, global Cloud Compute, Cloud GPU, Bare Metal, and Cloud Storage solutions. In December 2024 Vultr announced an equity financing at a $3.5 billion valuation. Founded by David Aninowsky and self-funded for over a decade, Vultr has grown to become the world’s largest privately-held cloud infrastructure company.

Vultr Cares

 - 100% company-paid insurance premiums for employee medical, dental and vision plans.

 - 401(k) plan that matches 100% up to 4%, with immediate vesting

 - Professional Development Reimbursement of $2,500 each year

 - 11 Holidays + Paid Time Off Accrual + Rollover Plan

 - Commitment matters to Vultr! Increased PTO at 3 year and 10 year anniversary + 1 month paid sabbatical every 5 years + Anniversary Bonus each year

 - $500 stipend for remote office setup in first year + $400 each following year

 - Internet reimbursement up to $75 per month

 - Gym membership reimbursement up to $50 per month

 - Company paid Wellable subscription
   
   

Join Vultr

Vultr is seeking a proactive and strategic Tax Strategy & Incentives Manager to own and manage our multi-state data center tax credit and incentive strategy across our expanding infrastructure footprint. Reporting directly to the Global Tax Director this role will act as our subject matter expert on state and local data center tax incentives—securing programs directly in-house when appropriate and orchestrating specialized external tax, legal, and economic development advisors for complex multi-jurisdictional negotiations.

This is a high-impact, cross-functional role where your ability to balance internal execution with external advisor management will directly influence Vultr’s expansion velocity, capital efficiency, and tax strategy as we build the next generation of cloud and AI infrastructure.



Key Responsibilities

 - Strategic Cross-Functional Communication: Act as the primary tax liaison for business initiatives, proactively surfacing tax implications early in contract negotiations, site selection, and operational changes. Translate complex tax regulations into clear, actionable guidance for non-tax stakeholders.

 - Evaluate state and local data center tax incentive opportunities, exemption programs, and statutory tax credits across current and target deployment locations.

 - Execute end-to-end incentive applications, tax filings, and sales/use tax exemption registrations directly in-house for standard statutory jurisdictions.

 - Manage & Orchestrate external tax advisors, legal counsel, and economic development consultants on complex, high-stakes, or specialized discretionary incentive negotiations and site selection engagements.

 - Model tax savings, capital expenditure thresholds, and return-on-investment (ROI) to evaluate site selection trade-offs in direct partnership with Real Estate, Infrastructure, and Legal teams.

 - Maintain ongoing compliance lifecycle management for all secured incentives, ensuring data center CapEx, power utilization, and job creation commitments are tracked to prevent clawbacks.

 - Compliance Control Management: Maintain strong internal controls, including reconciliations, to ensure data integrity across tax-related processes and support recurring audits.

 - Administer sales and use tax exemption certificates and direct-pay permits for qualifying server, storage, GPU, cooling, and power equipment purchases.

 - Monitor legislative developments, state statutory data center incentive changes, and green energy tax trends to keep the Global Tax Director informed of emerging risks and opportunities.



Qualifications

 - 5+ years of progressive experience in US State & Local Tax (SALT), specializing in location incentives, indirect tax exemptions, or corporate state tax planning.

 - CPA or JD preferred

 - Direct Experience with state data center incentive frameworks, sales/use tax equipment exemptions, and property tax abatement.

 - State or Local Government Experience Preferred: Prior experience working within a State Department of Revenue, State Economic Development Agency, or local taxing authority is a strong plus.

 - Proven experience managing external service providers, law firms, or accounting consultancy teams to drive clear project milestones and budget efficiency.

 - Advanced financial modeling skills with the ability to turn complex state tax regulations into clear financial projections for non-tax stakeholders.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, or related field.



Compensation

$120,000 – $140,000

Final compensation will vary depending on years of experience, background/skill set, location, and applicable laws.




INCLUSION & PRIVACY

We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds and experiences, and we prohibit discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status under applicable laws. Vultr will consider qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records in accordance with applicable laws and will not conduct a background check until after an offer of employment has been extended and accepted.

We also take your privacy seriously. We handle personal information responsibly and follow applicable laws, including U.S. privacy rules and India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Your data is used only for legitimate business purposes and is protected with proper security measures.

Where allowed by law, applicants may request details about the data we collect, access or delete their information, withdraw consent for its use, and opt out of nonessential communications. For more details, please see our Privacy Policy https://www.vultr.com/legal/privacy/.

• You bring integrity, adaptability, and a commitment to Edmentum’s mission and inclusive culture.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Data Scientist
jobs.description:
Fin, now part of Salesforce, is on a mission to help businesses provide perfect customer experiences.

Our AI Agent Fin is the highest-performing AI Customer Agent on the market today, enabling businesses to deliver impeccable, always-on customer support across the customer journey, from service, to sales, to ecommerce. Powered by our own AI models, Fin resolves complex customer issues end-to-end across every channel, with minimal set-up and integration. Fin can also be combined with our natively integrated Intercom help desk, giving modern support teams one single system.

Together with Salesforce, the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success, we're building the future of customer experience. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn't a buzzword, it's a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing, and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI.

Ready to level up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You're in the right place. Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

What’s the opportunity?

The Research, Analytics & Data Science (RAD) team at Intercom uses data and insights to drive evidence-based decision-making. We're a team of data scientists and product researchers who use data - both big and small - to unlock actionable insights about our customers, our products and our business. We generate insights that build customer empathy, drive product strategy and shape products that deliver real value to our customers.

We’re now seeing strong demand for data scientists who can apply their expertise directly with our most strategic customers. As a Forward Deployed Data Scientist, you’ll embed with customers to build Enterprise-grade Fin deployments. You’ll play a pivotal role in transforming how our most strategic customers scale customer support — working closely with them and our go-to-market teams to design, build, and implement data-driven solutions that unlock measurable impact. You’ll also feed insights from these frontline deployments back into Intercom’s product and strategy — helping shape the future of AI customer service.

This is a high-ownership role for someone who thrives in ambiguous environments, is energized by solving complex, real-world problems with data, and is motivated by seeing their work translate into both customer impact and product evolution.

What will I be doing?

• Drive the adoption of Fin by helping customers automate and scale their support operations.

• Embed with strategic customers to understand their support workflows, data, and business challenges — to identify and implement opportunities where AI can deliver measurable impact.

• Steer customers toward best practices in measurement and AI adoption to realize the full value of Fin.

• Partner closely with Sales, Success, and Product to deliver seamless customer experiences and successful deployments, and to create feedback loops that shape product development.

• Use AI to prototype, test, and scale data-driven solutions, building tools that make us faster and more effective in driving Fin adoption and customer impact.

What skills do I need?

• Proven ability to apply data science in real-world business contexts to drive measurable outcomes.

• Strong collaboration mindset; skilled at working across Sales, Success, Product, and Engineering.

• High adaptability and ownership: able to shift between deep technical analysis and high-level strategic framing.

• Excellent communication skills, both technical and non-technical.

• Rapid prototyping with systems thinking: you know when a customer needs a fast, bespoke answer, and when to build something others will keep using.

• Excellent SQL and production-aware Python, you write code other people can run, not just code that runs once and are experienced applying analytical and statistical methods to real business problems.

• Experience with AI/ML evaluation, LLM-driven applications, or conversational AI.

• Willing to travel and work on-site with customers to build deep relationships and uncover insights firsthand.

Bonus skills and attributes

• Experience in technical consulting, customer-facing analytics, or SaaS product data science.

• Experience reframing the problem, not just solving it, you've spotted when the question you were handed wasn't the right one, and changed what got worked on.

• Experience applying AI to scale the data science workflow.

*Proof of eligibility to work in the United States is required.

The base salary range for candidates within the San Francisco Bay Area is $206,600- $229,000. Actual base pay will depend on a variety of factors such as education, skills, experience, location, etc. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. All regular employees may also be eligible for the corporate bonus program or a sales incentive (target included in OTE) as well as stock in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs).

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

In the United States, compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, job level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, and benefits. At Fin, we want to give people what they need to do the best work of their careers. Our benefits and programs are designed to support your health and wellbeing, your family, your time away from work, and your financial future. Policies

Fin has a hybrid working policy. We believe that working in person helps us stay connected, collaborate easier and create a great culture while still providing flexibility to work from home. We expect employees to be in the office at least three days per week.

We have a radically open and accepting culture at Fin. We avoid spending time on divisive subjects to foster a safe and cohesive work environment for everyone. We respect personal opinion and expression on these topics on personal social platforms on personal time, and do not challenge or confront anyone for their views on non-work related topics. Our goal is to focus on doing incredible work to achieve our goals and unite the company through our core values.

It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. jobs.title: Principal FPGA Emulation Engineer
jobs.description:
About the Role

Renesas is seeking a Principal FPGA Emulation & Prototyping Engineer to build and own the FPGA-based platforms that emulate our mixed-signal power ASICs before silicon. Working shoulder to shoulder with our silicon RTL and DSP architects, you will bring their designs up on FPGA to validate real-time digital, mixed-signal, and power-control architectures pre-silicon — proving out control loops, catching RTL issues early, and de-risking tape-out.

These FPGA platforms are emulation vehicles, not production hardware. Success is measured by how faithfully and how fast they reproduce the target silicon: functional equivalence to the golden ASIC RTL, real-time (or near-real-time) performance for closed-loop power and DSP validation, and deep visibility for pre-silicon debug.

What You'll Do

• Partner closely with silicon RTL and DSP architects to bring ASIC designs up on FPGA — advising on FPGA-ability and turning architectural intent into a working, real-time emulation platform.
• Adapt ASIC RTL for FPGA emulation while preserving functional equivalence to the golden design — handling clock-gating conversion, memory/SRAM macro mapping, reset and initialization schemes, tri-state/bus conversion, and stubbing or modeling of analog/mixed-signal blocks.
• Map designs onto the FPGA fabric to fit and to hit emulation speed — steering resource inference (DSP/multiplier slices, block vs. distributed memory), clocking, and pipelining so the design achieves the real-time performance the validation requires.
• Build the real-time environment around the digital core: model or interface to the analog and power stages (ADC/DAC/PWM, gate drivers, plant/converter models), including hardware-in-the-loop with real or emulated power hardware where needed.
• Develop deep pre-silicon debug and visibility — logic analysis, long-run waveform capture, triggering, and assertions — and enable firmware/software co-development ahead of silicon.
• Define and continuously improve the emulation methodology, RTL/FPGA-ability guidelines, flows, and automation (TCL/Python).
• Provide technical leadership: mentor engineers, lead reviews, and drive emulation and tooling decisions across the silicon and systems teams.

Required Qualifications

• Extensive FPGA design and implementation experience (typically 10+ years), including a track record of FPGA prototyping or emulation of ASIC/SoC designs.
• Expert-level RTL design in SystemVerilog and/or VHDL, with deep familiarity working from ASIC-style RTL.
• Deep understanding of FPGA internal architecture and primitives — DSP/multiplier slices, block and distributed RAM, carry chains, and clocking — and a proven ability to map designs onto these resources to fit large ASIC RTL and reach real-time emulation performance (memory/SRAM macro mapping, DSP inference, clock-enable conversion, control-set and fanout management).
• Hands-on experience adapting ASIC RTL for FPGA: clock-gating conversion, memory macro replacement, reset schemes, tri-state conversion, and multi-clock/CDC handling.
• Strong command of the full FPGA implementation flow — synthesis, place-and-route, timing analysis, and constraint development (XDC/SDC) — on large Xilinx and/or Intel (Altera) devices, using Vivado and/or Quartus.
• Hardware bring-up and debug experience: in-system logic analysis (ILA/SignalTap), lab instrumentation, and long-run pre-silicon debug.
• Proficiency scripting for automation (TCL, Python).
• Demonstrated technical leadership — mentoring, reviews, and driving cross-team technical decisions.
• BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).

Preferred Qualifications

• Real-time, hardware-in-the-loop emulation and modeling of analog/mixed-signal and power stages (ADC/DAC/PWM interfaces, plant/converter models).
• Understanding of digital power-conversion control and mixed-signal systems — converter topologies, control loops, PWM/PFM, and magnetics — to build faithful models and validate power-control architectures.
• FPGA DSP implementation and real-time emulation of DSP datapaths: FIR/IIR/CIC filters, interpolation/decimation, FFT, FEC, including high-throughput techniques such as folding/unfolding.
• Experience with commercial FPGA prototyping platforms such as Synopsys HAPS, Cadence Protium, or Siemens Veloce.
• Model-based design with Simulink and/or Xilinx System Generator.
• High-speed interface experience: JESD204B, PCIe, 1G/10G Ethernet, Aurora.
• ASIC design or tape-out exposure, including DFT/scan considerations in emulation.
• Ability to architect and build a custom in-house FPGA prototyping platform — board architecture, high-speed PCB design, signal integrity, and bring-up — a plus as we may develop our own hardware in the future.
• Embedded/microcontroller and firmware co-development experience (C/assembly); MATLAB, C/C++.

Renesas is an embedded semiconductor solution provider driven by its Purpose, To Make Our Lives Easier. With a global team of over 21,000 engineers and problem solvers in more than 30 countries, we offer the opportunity to work on world‑leading technology for Automotive, Industrial, Infrastructure, and IoT, shaping a safer, healthier, greener, and smarter future.

At Renesas, TAGIE is our culture, grounded in being Transparent, Agile, Global, Innovative, and Entrepreneurial. It shapes how we work, grow and deliver on our purpose together. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Co-Op
jobs.description:
As a Mechanical Engineering Co-Op at Lexington Medical, you will design, test, and document parts for the AEON surgical stapler. This is a six-month, full-time co-op on our engineering team in Bedford, Massachusetts, and the projects are real ones: components going into a product used in operating rooms, and processes running on our own production floor. The work moves from CAD and drawings through fixture builds, testing, and the documentation that has to stand up to regulatory scrutiny, so you finish the term with a clear picture of how a medical device actually gets made.

About Lexington Medical

Lexington Medical is a medical device company designing and manufacturing surgical stapling technology at our headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, just outside Boston. Our AEON™ Endostapler is an FDA-cleared, minimally invasive surgical stapler used in operating rooms around the world. With engineering, manufacturing, and quality working closely together, engineers stay close to the product and see their work move from an idea through prototyping, testing, manufacturing, and ultimately into the operating room.

About the Role

As a Mechanical Engineering Co-Op, you will sit with our R&D engineering team and take on new product development work to the next generation of surgical staplers. Expect to spend your time across CAD and drawings, the lab, and the machine shop as you help develop new products. Because our teams are small, co-ops are given real scope.

Responsibilities

• Design and revise components and component drawings in accordance with industry and Lexington Medical drawing standards.

• Design test fixtures to characterize the performance of new components. Fabricate them using a combination of outsourcing and in-house rapid prototyping.

• Plan and run engineering tests on new products, then write the test protocols and engineering reports that document what you found.

• Operate lab equipment with minimal supervision, including mills, lathes, test stands, and 3D printers.

• Perform dimensional and functional quality checks using calipers, micrometers, optical comparators, and other inspection instruments.

• Complete the documentation required by our quality system so that your work holds up under FDA and internal audit requirements.

Qualifications

• Currently enrolled at an accredited university as an undergraduate or graduate student in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related technical discipline.

• Prior internship, co-op, or substantial hands-on project experience in engineering or manufacturing.

• Working knowledge of 3D CAD, and the ability to read and create engineering drawings, including the basics of GD&T.

• Comfortable working with machines such as mills, lathes, band saws, and belt sanders.

• Ability to operate FDM and SLA 3D printers is a plus.

• Experience with machining, injection molding, or metal stamping is a plus.

• Coursework or project experience in design of experiments, statistics, or test method development is a plus.

What Success Looks Like

• In your first month, you are designing fixtures and running tests with light oversight, and you are asking the questions that catch problems early rather than waiting to be told.

• By the midpoint of the co-op, you own a defined project end to end, including the designs, test data and documentation behind it.

• By June, you leave behind constructed fixtures, protocols, and data reports the team keeps using after you go back to school, and you can explain how a design decision traces through testing and documentation to the finished design.

Location & Work Arrangement

This position is based at our headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, in the Greater Boston area, and is an on-site role. The co-op runs full-time, five days per week, from January 2027 through June 2027.

$28.00 to $34.00 USD per hour

Job Summary:

SmithRx is looking for a dynamic and experienced leader to serve as the Manager, Clinical Review Operations and Quality Assurance. This pivotal role is responsible for the integrity, efficiency, and clinical strategy of our prior authorization (PA) ecosystem. You will lead a multidisciplinary function, integrating Quality Assurance (QA) oversight, technical system management, and medication policy execution. The Account Manager maintains and expands relationships with assigned account base customers, with intentions to maximize sales/profit for every account and most importantly to expand CR market penetration within the assigned area.

jobs.description:
Role

We are creating a new Head of Invoicing role to lead our Invoicing function across the Europe, Middle East and Africa ("EMEA") region, bringing together teams that currently operate separately across the region into a single, unified function. This role brings senior leadership, structure and consistency to how we manage invoicing end to end, and will standardise practice in an ERP-agnostic way — building the foundation for a future move to a single group ERP.

What you'll do

• You'll take end-to-end ownership of the EMEA invoicing function, defining strategy, governance, policies, procedures, and a standardized control framework that supports regional consistency and future ERP integration.
• You'll build, lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team across multiple locations, providing clear direction, performance management, and fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
• You'll serve as the senior invoicing lead across EMEA, partnering with Finance leadership, the Regional CFO, operational, sales, client services teams, and clients to resolve escalations, improve processes, and strengthen billing discipline.
• You'll drive invoicing excellence by improving billing accuracy, timeliness, completeness, and dispute resolution, maximizing revenue protection while delivering insight-led reporting on performance, cycle times, backlog, accuracy, and revenue impact.
• You'll lead invoicing-related transformation initiatives, including ERP standardization and broader systems and process change, ensuring invoicing requirements are effectively represented as the business evolves and supporting other priorities as required.

What we offer

• Comprehensive remuneration: Motivating financial packages based upon market rates for your role and is proportionate to your qualifications, level of experiences and skills profile
• Pension Scheme: Generous employer contribution with the ability to allow and increase employee contributions
• Annual leave: All our employees are entitled to 22 days paid leave. Enhanced maternity and paternity, including shared parental leave and adoption leave
• Flexible working: We recognise the value of working flexibly and is keen to ensure all employees enjoy an excellent work-life blend. As such, we are open to conversations with employees related to setting up flexible working arrangements
• Support and development: We will ensure you have the right training, tools and development plan to grow and improve your skills every day

About You

• You have significant experience in invoicing, billing, order-to-cash, or revenue operations, with a proven track record of leading, developing, and managing teams across multiple countries, shared service environments, or onshore/offshore delivery models.
• You have successfully led process, policy, systems, or ERP transformation initiatives, including standardizing practices across multiple ERP or billing platforms and supporting ERP migration, consolidation, or system-agnostic process design.
• You are a confident and credible communicator with the ability to influence senior stakeholders, represent the business externally with clients, and balance hands-on operational delivery with strategic leadership.
• You have strong expertise in improving billing accuracy, timeliness, and revenue realization, supported by excellent analytical, organizational, attention-to-detail, and problem-solving skills, along with advanced MS Office and Excel capabilities.
• You bring a strong results-driven mindset, an understanding of multi-currency and multi-jurisdiction operations in a global environment, fluency in English, and ideally French language skills and a professional accountancy or finance qualification.

 - Read about us in the NYT https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/05/business/dealbook/clay-ai-marketing-fundraise.html, Forbes http://google.com/search?q=forbes+clay&rlz=1C5OZZY_enUS1155US1155&oq=forbes+clay&gs_lcrp=EgZjaHJvbWUyBggAEEUYOTIHCAEQABiABDIHCAIQABiABDIHCAMQABiABDIHCAQQABiABDIHCAUQABiABDIHCAYQABiABDIHCAcQABiABDIHCAgQABiABDIHCAkQABiABNIBBzkzM2owajSoAgOwAgHxBVAe8UAxJx_p&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8, First Round Review https://review.firstround.com/podcast/inside-clays-unconventional-path-to-1-25b/, and more https://www.clay.com/press.
   
   

Hear from our employees directly on our Glassdoor https://www.glassdoor.com/Overview/Working-at-Clay-EI_IE9850794.11,15.htm page!


GTM ENGINEER @ CLAY

Clay is the GTM platform of choice for the best revenue teams in the world. From Anthropic to Notion to Stripe, growth teams use Clay to find their GTM Alpha. Our journey to $100M ARR was powered by creativity, and a belief that the best GTM teams treat their go-to-market like a product: constantly shipping new plays, experimenting, and never assuming that what worked last quarter will work next quarter. We sell that way too.

We describe ourselves as go-to-market consultants: account executives with a product mindset. We don't just sell Clay. We learn how a prospect's GTM motion actually works and show them what's possible with Clay. Every deal is a net-new customer discovering Clay for the first time. Our motion is high-velocity but consultative; we move fast, but we also go deep. This role won't look the same in six months as it does today, and that's the point. We're looking for people who want to grow alongside us and help redefine what great selling looks like. 



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own and close net-new business end-to-end

 - Prospect into target accounts and build pipeline alongside managing inbound leads

 - Run tailored product evaluations and demos that connect Clay's capabilities to a prospect's specific workflows and pain points

 - Lead consultative discovery that helps prospects see the possibilities of Clay

 - Build business cases that win budget and internal champions

 - Work cross-functionally with product, engineering, services, and customer teams to shape solutions and stay sharp on what Clay can do

 - Help build our sales playbook, processes, and culture as we scale

 - Use AI creatively, whether to improve your workflows or that of your customers




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 4+ years in a closing role (AE, senior AE, or sales leader) with a track record of carrying and exceeding quota

 - Proven ability to build pipeline, not just manage it

 - Experience closing new-logo deals in the $50K-$100K range with multiple stakeholders in a consultative, solutions-oriented selling motion

 - High business IQ: you can walk into a conversation with a company you've never sold to, quickly understand their GTM motion, and identify where Clay creates value. This is the single most important skill in the role

 - Creative and resourceful, whether that's finding clever ways to use AI tools in your own work or learning and pitching all of Clay’s exciting use cases

 - Experience with a formal sales methodology (we don't care which one, but you have a structured approach to running deals)

 - You're a strong communicator who can hold a room without dominating it

 - You're excited about contributing to a growing team, not just hitting your own number




WHY THIS ROLE

The best GTM teams we work with don't run the same playbook forever. They ship new plays constantly, automate what's manual, and treat every part of their go-to-market as something that can be improved. We do the same internally, and as a GTME, you'll be immersed in that culture and bring those ideas directly into how you sell.

We believe we're building the future of what great salespeople look like in a post-AI world. You'll get a front-row seat to how the best GTM teams in tech actually operate, across every motion, segment, and vertical. You'll build relationships with revenue leaders at companies you admire and develop the pattern recognition that makes great GTM leaders.

If you don't fit the mold of a traditional account executive, you're welcome here. People from non-traditional backgrounds (founders, software engineers, former educators, product managers, and more!) have shaped our sales organization in meaningful ways.


Meet our amazing GTME crew!

jobs.title: Medical Director, Miami & DC
jobs.description:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.



Role Purpose

You own the clinical bar across the Neko clinics in the Miami + DC region.



That means every consultation in your area meets the same threshold of safety, quality, and member experience across your region. It means the clinical teams working with you are developing, not just performing. It means clinical issues are being seen and addressed before they show up in audits or member complaints. And it means clinical judgment shows up at the table when operational decisions are being made.



You'll partner closely with the U.S. Head of Clinical Enablement, who holds final clinical authority for the US market, and operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Manager for your region who owns the operational side. The clinical health of the region is yours.



What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

 - Hold the clinical standard across every site in your area

 - Manage and develop the clinicians in your region: performance conversations, development plans, coaching, and the honest feedback that turns good clinicians into great ones.

 - Ensure lead clinicians in your market(s) are performing excellently and that the clinical teams have the appropriate clinical escalation pathways in place.

 - Lead clinical hiring for your area against defined criteria, and partner with the Training and Education team to close training gaps as they emerge.

 - Own the review and closure of clinical incidents and near-misses in your area, making sure learnings are actually applied, not just documented.

 - Operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Manager: co-owning quality, member experience, and business goals, attending and contributing to Weekly and Monthly Business Reviews, and bringing clinical input into operational decisions before they're made.

 - Round your sites regularly to observe, support, and listen, surfacing what's working so it can spread, and what isn't so it can be addressed.

 - Build and maintain trusted relationships with the specialist clinicians who receive Neko referrals monitoring referral quality and addressing breakdowns quickly.

 - Know the local regulatory landscape: licensing requirements, referral obligations, market-specific clinical rules etc and flag emerging risks before they become problems.

 - Lead or participate in clinical pilots as required - defining success, capturing learnings, and documenting outcomes so the rest of the company can learn from your region.



What We're Hiring For

 - Holds the Bar at Scale. You're the kind of clinical leader who can make sure every consultation feels the same regardless of site or clinician, not by micromanaging, but by setting a clear standard, coaching to it, and noticing when it drifts. You're rigorous without being rigid.

 - Develops the Clinicians You Lead. You take clinician development seriously. You give honest feedback even when it's uncomfortable. You spot what someone needs before they ask. You know the difference between a clinician who needs coaching and one who needs to leave, and you don't avoid either conversation.

 - The Dyad That Actually Works. You bring clinical judgment into operational decisions before they're made and you stay constructive when clinical standards and operational targets pull in different directions. When you escalate, it's because something genuinely needs leadership attention, not because you've stopped trying to resolve it locally.

 - Reads the Pattern, Not Just the Report. You don't just review the data. You see what it's telling you. You round your sites and notice things that don't show up in dashboards. When you spot a pattern you trace it to the root cause and you make sure the right people hear about it.

 - Trusted Outside the Walls. The referral network, the regulators, the specialist clinicians who receive Neko members: these relationships sit with you. You represent Neko credibly because you're a credible clinician yourself. People in the local medical community know your name, and when you flag something, they take it seriously.

Minimum Requirements

 - MD, DO, NP or PA with active Florida and DC license in good standing.

 - Board certification in a relevant specialty (Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, or equivalent).

 - 4+ years of medical leadership experience, including direct management of clinicians.

 - Demonstrated experience holding clinical standards across multiple sites or a large clinical team.



Preferred

 - Experience in preventive care, tech enabled healthcare or longitudinal care models.

 - Experience operating in a clinical-operational dyad structure.

 - Experience leading clinical pilots or scaling new clinical workflows across multiple sites.



Compensation & Benefits

 - Paid Time Off & Holidays

 - Equity Eligible role

 - Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance

 - 401(k) Retirement Plan

 - Commuter Benefits

 - Wellness Rewards Program

 - Complimentary full Neko scan for you and eligible family members
